- **Claim:** "the likeness of His light" in Qur'an 24:35 is a scribe's error for "the light of the believer"

> [!note]- Ibn Abbas, Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim, vol.8, pp.154-155, no.14560
> [14560] حدثنا علي بن الحسين ، ثنا نصر بن علي ، أخبرني أبي عن شبل بن عباد عن قيس بن سعد ، عن عطاء عن ابن عباس : * (اللَّه نُورُ السَّماواتِ والأَرْضِ مَثَلُ
> * ( نُورِه ) * قال : هي خطأ من الكاتب هو أعظم من أن يكون نوره مثل نور المشكاة قال : مثل نور المؤمن كمشكاة .
>
> [14560] Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us. Nasr ibn Ali narrated to us. My father informed me, from Shibl ibn Abbad, from Qays ibn Sad, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas,
>
> > “God is the Light of the heavens and the earth; the likeness of His light.” He said, “It is a mistake by the scribe. He is too great for His light to be like the light of a niche.” He said, “The likeness of the believer’s light is like a niche.”

Abu Shahba quotes the exegete Abu Hayyan, who calls whoever reports the 24:27 statement from Ibn Abbas a heretic. Ibn Ashtah, quoted by al-Suyuti, explains the error as a poor choice among the seven ahruf. Ma'rifat, an Imami scholar, reviews ten such reports of early scribal error. He says they must be interpreted or rejected.

> [!tip]- Abu Shahba, al-Madkhal, p.365, quoting Abu Hayyan
> 1 - أن هذا القول غير صحيح في نسبته إلى ابن عباس وهو مدسوس عليه ، دسه الملاحدة والزنادقة ، قال أبو حيان ما نصه : إن من روى عن ابن عباس أنه قال ذلك فهو طاعن في الإسلام ملحد في الدين ، وابن عباس بريء من ذلك القول .
>
> 1. This statement is not correctly attributed to Ibn Abbas. It was falsely inserted into his words, and the heretics and the zindiqs inserted it. Abu Hayyan said, in these exact words, "Whoever reports from Ibn Abbas that he said this is attacking Islam and is a heretic in religion, and Ibn Abbas is innocent of that statement."

> [!tip]- Ibn Ashtah, in al-Suyuti, al-Itqan, vol.1, p.557
> وقد أجاب ابن أشتة عن هذه الآثار كلّها بأنّ المراد أخطئوا في الاختيار ، وما هو الأولى لجمع الناس عليه من الأحرف السبعة ، لا أنّ الذي كتب خطأ خارج عن القرآن .
>
> Ibn Ashtah answered all of these reports by saying that what is meant is that they made a mistake in choosing, from among the seven ahruf, the one that was best for bringing people together. He did not mean that what was written was an error lying outside the Quran.

> [!tip]- Ma'rifat, al-Tamhid fi Ulum al-Qur'an, vol.1, p.370
> أمّا نفس المحتوى وصحّة ما تضمّنته من تبديل نصّ المصحف الشريف ، فهذا شيء لا نكاد نصدّقه البتة . لأنّه هوالتحريف الذي أجمعت الأُمّة الإسلاميّة على عدم تسرّبه إلى كتاب اللّه العزيز الحميد : «إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحافِظُونَ» . (5) فلابدّ من الأخذ في تأويلها إلى وجه معقول أو رفضها رأسا . (6)
>
> As for the content itself, and the soundness of what it contains about altering the text of the noble Mushaf, this is something we can hardly ever believe. It is the very distortion that the Muslim community agreed has never seeped into the Book of God, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, "Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its guardians." (Quran 15:9) So one must either interpret these reports in some reasonable way or reject them outright.

Al-Hakim graded the 24:27 report sahih by the standard of al-Bukhari and Muslim.

## The Mushaf of Fatimah

- **Source:** Abu Mansur al-Azhari, Tahdhib al-Lugha, vol.4, p.149; Murtada al-Askari, al-Mushaf fi al-Riwayat wa al-Athar, p.10
- **Speaker:** al-Layth, quoted by al-Azhari; al-Askari
- **Claim:** a mushaf is any bound collection of written pages

The Kafi reports speak of a Mushaf of Fatimah ﵍. The word mushaf means any bound collection of pages, as the two sources below define it.

> [!tip]- al-Layth, in al-Azhari, Tahdhib al-Lugha, vol.4, p.149
> قال : وإنما سُمِّي المُصْحَفُ مُصْحَفاً لأنه أُصْحِفَ أي جعل جامعاً للصُّحُف المكتوبة بين الدَّفَّتَيْن .
>
> He said that the mushaf is called a mushaf because it was "ushifa", meaning that it was made a collection of the written sheets between the two covers.

> [!tip]- al-Askari, al-Mushaf fi al-Riwayat wa al-Athar, p.10
> إنّ المصحف اسم لكلّ كتاب مجلد قرآناً كان أم غير قرآن .
>
> The mushaf is a name for every bound book, whether it is a Quran or not a Quran.

Al-Layth defines the mushaf as written sheets gathered between two covers. Al-Askari concludes that the word names any bound book, Qur'an or not.

- **Source:** al-Kafi, vol.1, pp.238-240, chapter on al-Sahifa, al-Jafr, al-Jami'a and the Mushaf of Fatimah, nos.1-3
- **Speaker:** Imam al-Sadiq ﵇, through Abu Basir, Hammad ibn Uthman and al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Ala'
- **Claim:** the Mushaf of Fatimah ﵍ holds no letter of the Qur'an

> [!info]- Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.239, no.1
> ثم سكت ساعة ثم قال : وإن عندنا لمصحف فاطمة ﵍ وما يدريهم ما مصحف فاطمة ﵍ ؟ قال : قلت : وما مصحف فاطمة ﵍ ؟ قال : مصحف فيه مثل قرآنكم هذا ثلاث مرات ، والله ما فيه من قرآنكم حرف واحد ، قال : قلت : هذا والله العلم قال : إنه لعلم وما هو بذاك .
>
> > Then he was silent for a while, and then he said, "We also have the Mushaf of Fatima. And what do they know of the Mushaf of Fatima?"
>
> > He said, "I said, 'And what is the Mushaf of Fatima?'"
>
> > He said, "It is a mushaf containing three times the like of this Quran of yours. By God, there is not a single letter of your Quran in it."
>
> > He said, "I said, 'This, by God, is knowledge.'"
>
> > He said, "It is knowledge, but it is not that."

> [!info]- Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.240, no.2
> 2 - عدة من أصحابنا ، عن أحمد بن محمد ، عن عمر بن عبد العزيز ، عن حماد بن عثمان قال : سمعت أبا عبد الله ﵇ يقول : تظهر الزنادقة في سنة ثمان وعشرين ومائة وذلك أني نظرت في مصحف فاطمة ﵍ ، قال : قلت : وما مصحف فاطمة ؟ قال : إن الله تعالى لما قبض نبيه ﵌ دخل على فاطمة ﵍ من وفاته من الحزن ما لا يعلمه إلا الله ﷿ فأرسل الله إليها ملكا يسلي غمها ويحدثها ، فشكت ذلك (1) إلى أمير المؤمنين ﵇ فقال : إذا أحسست بذلك وسمعت الصوت قولي لي فأعلمته بذلك فجعل أمير المؤمنين ﵇ يكتب كلما سمع حتى أثبت من ذلك مصحفا قال : ثم قال : أما إنه ليس فيه شئ من الحلال والحرام ولكن فيه علم ما يكون .
>
> 2. A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said that he heard Abu Abd Allah say,
>
> > "The heretics will appear in the year one hundred and twenty-eight, and that is because I looked in the Mushaf of Fatima."
>
> > He said, "I said, 'And what is the Mushaf of Fatima?'"
>
> > He said, "When God the Exalted took back His Prophet, there came upon Fatima, because of his death, a grief that only God the Mighty and Majestic knows. So God sent her an angel to console her in her sorrow and to speak with her. She complained of this to the Commander of the Believers, and he said, 'When you sense that and hear the voice, tell me.' She told him about it, and the Commander of the Believers began to write down everything he heard, until he had put together a mushaf from it."
>
> > He said, "Then he said, 'It contains nothing of the lawful and the unlawful, but it contains knowledge of what will happen.'"

> [!info]- Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.240, no.3
> 3 - عدة من أصحابنا ، عن أحمد بن محمد ، عن علي بن الحكم ، عن الحسين ابن أبي العلاء قال : سمعت أبا عبد الله ﵇ يقول : إن عندي الجفر الأبيض ، قال : قلت : فأي شئ فيه ؟ قال : زبور داود ، وتوراة موسى ، وإنجيل عيسى ، وصحف إبراهيم ﵈ والحلال والحرام ، ومصحف فاطمة ، ما أزعم أن فيه قرآنا ، وفيه ما يحتاج الناس إلينا ولا نحتاج إلى أحد حتى فيه الجلدة ، ونصف الجلدة ، وربع الجلدة وأرش الخدش .
>
> 3. A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Ala, who said that he heard Abu Abd Allah say,
>
> > "I have the White Jafr."
>
> > He said, "I said, 'And what is in it?'"
>
> > He said, "The Psalms of David, the Torah of Moses, the Gospel of Jesus, the scrolls of Abraham, the lawful and the unlawful, and the Mushaf of Fatima. I do not claim that it contains a Quran. It contains what people need from us, while we need nothing from anyone. It even contains the lash, the half lash, the quarter lash, and the compensation for a scratch."

In the first report Imam al-Sadiq ﵇ says the book is three times the size of the Qur'an. He swears it holds no letter of the Qur'an. In the second, an angel consoles Fatimah ﵍ after the Prophet's ﷺ death, and Ali ﵇ writes down what she hears. The Imam ﵇ says the book holds no law and holds knowledge of what will happen. In the third, he lists the Mushaf of Fatimah ﵍ among the contents of the White Jafr. He adds, "I do not claim that it contains a Qur'an."

## Ali's Codex and His Teaching

- **Source:** al-Kafi, vol.1, p.64, no.1, in the chapter on the difference of hadith, vol.1, pp.62-64
- **Speaker:** Imam Ali ﵇, through Sulaym ibn Qays
- **Claim:** Ali ﵇ wrote every verse in his own hand, and the Prophet ﷺ taught him its interpretation, abrogation and scope

> [!info]- Imam Ali, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.64, no.1
> فما نزلت على رسول الله ﵌ آية من القرآن إلا أقرأنيها وأملاها علي فكتبتها بخطي وعلمني تأويلها وتفسيرها وناسخها ومنسوخها ، ومحكمها ومتشابهها ، وخاصها وعامها ، ودعا الله أن يعطيني فهمها ، وحفظها ، فما نسيت آية من كتاب الله ولا علما أملاه علي وكتبته ، منذ دعا الله لي بما دعا ، وما ترك شيئا علمه الله من حلال ولا حرام ، ولا أمر ولا نهي كان أو يكون ولا كتاب منزل على أحد قبله من طاعة أو معصية إلا علمنيه وحفظته ، فلم أنس حرفا واحدا
>
> > No verse of the Quran was sent down to the Messenger of God except that he had me recite it and dictated it to me, and I wrote it in my own hand. He taught me its interpretation (ta'wil) and its explanation (tafsir), its abrogating and abrogated verses, its decisive and ambiguous verses, and its particular and general verses.
>
> > He prayed to God to give me understanding of it and memory of it. So I have not forgotten a verse of the Book of God, nor any knowledge that he dictated to me and I wrote down, since he prayed to God for me as he prayed.
>
> > He left nothing that God had taught him, whether permitted or forbidden, command or prohibition, what has been or what will be, or any book sent down to anyone before him, whether of obedience or of disobedience, except that he taught it to me and I memorized it. I did not forget a single letter.

Imam Ali ﵇ says the Prophet ﷺ dictated every revealed verse to him and he wrote it in his own hand. He says the Prophet ﷺ also taught him each verse's interpretation, its abrogating and abrogated verses, and its decisive and ambiguous verses. He adds that the Prophet ﷺ prayed for his memory and that he forgot nothing.

- **Source:** al-Tabrisi, al-Ihtijaj, vol.1, p.281
- **Speaker:** Imam Ali ﵇, in the report of Ishaq ibn Musa from Imam al-Kazim ﵇
- **Claim:** Ali ﵇ gathered the Qur'an after the Prophet's ﷺ burial and the people refused it

> [!info]- Imam Ali, al-Ihtijaj, vol.1, p.281
> فلما توفي رسول الله ﵌ اشتغلت بدفنه والفراغ من شأنه ثم آليت يمينا (1) أني لا أرتدي إلا للصلاة حتى أجمع القرآن ففعلت ، ثم أخذته وجئت به فأعرضته عليهم قالوا : لا حاجة لنا به
>
> > When the Messenger of God died, I was occupied with burying him and finishing his affairs. Then I swore an oath that I would not put on my cloak except for prayer until I had collected the Quran, and I did so. Then I took it, brought it, and presented it to them.
>
> > They said, "We have no need of it."

Imam Ali ﵇ says he gathered the Qur'an after burying the Prophet ﷺ and the people refused it. The report of Salim ibn Salama gives the same refusal. Neither report says how Ali's ﵇ copy differed. Al-Mufid inclines to the view that the removed material was Ali's ﵇ interpretation. Al-Tabataba'i places any difference in the order of suras or of some verses.

- **Source:** Nahj al-Balagha, sermon 176, p.252, and sermon 156, p.219, Subhi Salih numbering
- **Speaker:** Imam Ali ﵇, without an isnad
- **Claim:** this Qur'an guides without misleading, and the Book of God is the firm rope

> [!info]- Imam Ali, Nahj al-Balagha, sermon 176, p.252
> واعْلَمُوا أَنَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ هُوَ النَّاصِحُ الَّذِي لَا يَغُشُّ - والْهَادِي الَّذِي لَا يُضِلُّ والْمُحَدِّثُ الَّذِي لَا يَكْذِبُ
>
> > Know that this Quran is the adviser who does not deceive, the guide who does not lead astray, and the speaker who does not lie.

> [!info]- Imam Ali, Nahj al-Balagha, sermon 156, p.219
> وعَلَيْكُمْ بِكِتَابِ اللَّه - فَإِنَّه الْحَبْلُ الْمَتِينُ والنُّورُ الْمُبِينُ - والشِّفَاءُ النَّافِعُ والرِّيُّ النَّاقِعُ - والْعِصْمَةُ لِلْمُتَمَسِّكِ والنَّجَاةُ لِلْمُتَعَلِّقِ - لَا يَعْوَجُّ فَيُقَامَ ولَا يَزِيغُ فَيُسْتَعْتَبَ - ولَا تُخْلِقُه كَثْرَةُ الرَّدِّ ووُلُوجُ السَّمْعِ - مَنْ قَالَ بِه صَدَقَ ومَنْ عَمِلَ بِه سَبَقَ
>
> > Hold fast to the Book of God, for it is the firm rope and the clear light, the beneficial cure and the quenching drink, a protection for whoever holds to it and a rescue for whoever clings to it. It does not bend, so that it would need straightening, and it does not swerve, so that it would need to be turned back. Repeated recitation and constant hearing do not wear it out. Whoever speaks by it speaks truly, and whoever acts by it takes the lead.

Sermon 176 calls "this Qur'an" an adviser who does not deceive and a guide who does not lead astray. Sermon 156 tells its hearers to hold fast to the Book of God as the firm rope. Nahj al-Balagha gives both sermons without a chain of transmission.

## Ali's Reading in the Printed Mushaf

- **Source:** al-Dhahabi, Ma'rifat al-Qurra' al-Kibar, vol.1, p.208
- **Speaker:** Asim and Hafs ibn Sulayman, as reported by al-Dhahabi (d.748 AH)
- **Claim:** Hafs read through Asim and Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami to Ali ﵇

> [!note]- al-Dhahabi, Ma'rifat al-Qurra' al-Kibar, vol.1, p.208
> وروى جماعة ، عن عمرو بن الصباح ، عن حفص الغاضري ، عن عاصم ، عن أبي عبد الرحمن ، عن علي بالقراءة . وذكر عاصم أنه لم يخالف أبا عبد الرحمن في شيء من قراءته ، وأن أبا عبد الرحمن لم يخالف عليا في شيء من قراءته .
>
> A group transmitted from Amr ibn al-Sabbah, from Hafs al-Ghadiri, from Asim, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from Ali, concerning the recitation.
>
> > Asim mentioned that he never differed from Abu Abd al-Rahman in any part of his recitation, and that Abu Abd al-Rahman never differed from Ali in any part of his recitation.

> [!note]- Hafs, in al-Dhahabi, Ma'rifat al-Qurra' al-Kibar, vol.1, p.208
> ويروى عن حفص بن سليمان ، قال : قال لي عاصم : ما كان من القراءة التي قرأت بها على أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي ، فهي التي أقرأتك بها ، وما كان من القراءة التي أقرأت بها أبا بكر بن عياش ، فهي القراءة التي عرضتها على زرّ بن حبيش ، عن ابن مسعود .
>
> It is reported from Hafs ibn Sulayman, who said.
>
> > Asim said to me, “Whatever recitation I recited to Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, that is the one I taught you. And whatever recitation I taught Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, that is the recitation I presented to Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ibn Masud.”

Asim says he never departed from al-Sulami's reading, and al-Sulami never departed from Ali's ﵇. Asim taught Hafs the reading he had recited to al-Sulami. He taught Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, known as Shu'ba, the reading he had presented to Zirr ibn Hubaysh from Ibn Mas'ud. By these reports, the Hafs reading descends through al-Sulami from Ali ﵇.

> [!tip]- the introduction to the Cairo printing, in al-Tabrizi, Tanzih al-Shi'a al-Ithnay Ashariyya, vol.1, p.41
> تعريف بهذا المصحف الشريف كتب هذا المصحف وضبط على ما يوافق رواية حفص بن سليمان بن المغيرة الأسدي الكوفي بقراءة عاصم بن أبي النجود الكوفي التابعي ، عن أبي عبد الرحمن عبد الله بن حبيب السلمي ، عن عثمان بن عفان ، وعلي بن أبي طالب ﵇ ، وزيد بن ثابت ، وأبي بن كعب ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه (وآله) وسلم .
>
> Introduction to this noble Quran codex. This codex was written and vocalized in agreement with the transmission of Hafs ibn Sulayman ibn al-Mughira al-Asadi al-Kufi, from the recitation of Asim ibn Abi al-Najud al-Kufi, a Follower, from Abu Abd al-Rahman Abd Allah ibn Habib al-Sulami, from Uthman ibn Affan, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Zayd ibn Thabit and Ubayy ibn Kab, from the Prophet.

The introduction to the Cairo printing of the Qur'an, quoted by al-Tabrizi, says the printing follows Hafs from Asim. It traces Asim's reading through al-Sulami to four Companions, Ali ﵇ among them.

- **Source:** Ibn Mihran, al-Mabsut fi al-Qira'at al-Ashr, p.440; al-Shawkani, Fath al-Qadir, vol.2, p.183
- **Speaker:** Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash; al-Shawkani
- **Claim:** readings from Ali ﵇ survive inside the canonical readings

> [!note]- Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, in Ibn Mihran, al-Mabsut, p.440
> واختار أبو بكر بن عياش {عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ} خفيفة الراء أيضا . وهو من الحروف العشرة التي ذكرت أنه قال : " أنا أدخلتها من قراءة علي - ﵁ - في قراءة عاصم حتى استخلصت قراءته " . يعني قراءة علي بن أبي طالب ﵇ .
>
> Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash also chose the reading "he acknowledged part of it" with a light ra. It is one of the ten readings concerning which I mentioned that he said, "I introduced them from the reading of Ali into the reading of Asim, until I had distilled his reading." He means the reading of Ali ibn Abi Talib.

> [!tip]- al-Shawkani, Fath al-Qadir, vol.2, p.183
> قرأ حمزة والكسائي " فارقوا دينهم " وهي قراءة علي بن أبي طالب : أي تركوا دينهم وخرجوا عنه . وقرأ الباقون فرقوا بالتشديد إلا النخعي فإنه قرأ بالتخفيف .
>
> Hamza and al-Kisai read “they parted from their religion,” which is also the reading of Ali ibn Abi Talib, meaning that they left their religion and went out from it. The other reciters read “they divided their religion,” with the doubled letter, except al-Nakhai, who read it with the light form.

Shu'ba says he brought ten readings from Ali's ﵇ reading into his reading of Asim. One of them is 'arafa with a light ra in Qur'an 66:3. The printed text of al-Mabsut gives both readings the same vocalization, including the doubling mark, so only Ibn Mihran's words "light" and "doubled" tell them apart. Al-Shawkani reports that Hamza and al-Kisa'i read faraqu in Qur'an 6:159, and he names it Ali's ﵇ reading. These reports place readings attributed to Ali ﵇ inside the canonical readings of Asim, Hamza and al-Kisa'i.

## Collection in the Imami Sources

- **Source:** al-Majlisi, Bihar al-Anwar, vol.89, pp.77-78, quoting al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi through Jami' al-Usul
- **Speaker:** Zayd ibn Thabit
- **Claim:** Zayd gathered the Qur'an for Abu Bakr from scraps of parchment, palm stalks, thin stones and the memories of men

Al-Majlisi's Bihar al-Anwar carries the Sunni account of how the Qur'an was collected. He copied Zayd ibn Thabit's report and labels it as al-Bukhari's and al-Tirmidhi's.

> [!note]- Zayd ibn Thabit, in al-Majlisi, Bihar al-Anwar, vol.89, pp.77-78
> أقول : روى البخاري والترمذي في صحيحيهما وذكره في جامع الأصول في حرف التاء في باب ترتيب القرآن وتأليفه وجمعه ، عن زيد بن ثابت قال : أرسل إلى أبو بكر بعد مقتل أهل اليمامة فإذا عمر جالس عنده ، فقال أبو بكر : إن عمر جاءني فقال : إن القتل قد استحر يوم اليمامة بقراء القرآن ، وإني أخشى أن يستحر القتل بالقراء في كل المواطن ، فيذهب من القرآن كثير وإني أرى أن
> تذهب بجمع القرآن ، قال : قلت لعمر : وكيف أفعل شيئا لم يفعله رسول الله ﵌ فقال عمر : هو والله خير ، فلم يزل يراجعني في ذلك حتى شرح الله صدري للذي شرح له صدر عمر ، ورأيت في ذلك الذي رأي عمر ، قال زيد : فقال لي أبو بكر : إنك رجل شاب عاقل ، لا نتهمك ، قد كنت تكتب الوحي لرسول الله ﵌ فتتبع القرآن فأجمعه ، قال زيد : فوالله لو كلفني نقل جبل من الجبال ، ما كان أثقل على مما أمرني به من جمع القرآن . قال : قلت : كيف تفعلان شيئا لم يفعله رسول الله ؟ فقال أبو بكر : هو والله خير ، قال : فلم يزل أبو بكر يراجعني - وفي رواية أخرى فلم يزل عمر يراجعني - حتى شرح الله صدري للذي شرح له صدر أبي بكر قال : فتتبعت القرآن : أجمعه من الرقاع والعسب واللخاف وصدور الرجال حتى وجدت آخر سورة التوبة مع خزيمة أو أبي خزيمة الأنصاري لم أجدها مع أحد غيره " لقد جائكم رسول من أنفسكم عزيز عليه " خاتمة براءة . قال : فكانت الصحف عند أبي بكر حتى توفاه الله ثم عند عمر حتى توفاه الله ، ثم حفصة بنت عمر ، قال بعض الرواة : فيه اللخاف يعني الخزف ، قال في جامع الأصول : أخرجه البخاري والترمذي .
>
> I say that al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi reported in their two Sahih collections, and it is also mentioned in Jami al-Usul under the letter ta, in the chapter on the arrangement, composition and collection of the Quran, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said
>
> > Abu Bakr sent for me after the killing of the people of Yamama, and Umar was sitting with him. Abu Bakr said, "Umar came to me and said, 'Killing has become fierce on the day of Yamama among the reciters of the Quran, and I fear that killing will become fierce among the reciters in every place, so that much of the Quran goes. I think you should go about the collection of the Quran.' I said to Umar, 'How can I do something the Messenger of God did not do?' Umar said, 'By God, it is good.' He kept going back to me about it until God opened my chest to what he had opened Umar's chest to, and I came to hold on that matter the view that Umar held."
>
> > Zayd said, "Abu Bakr then said to me, 'You are a young and intelligent man, and we do not suspect you. You used to write down the revelation for the Messenger of God, so seek out the Quran and collect it.'" Zayd said, "By God, if he had charged me with moving one of the mountains, it would not have been heavier on me than what he commanded me to do in collecting the Quran."
>
> > He said, "I said, 'How can you two do something the Messenger of God did not do?' Abu Bakr said, 'By God, it is good.'" He said, "Abu Bakr kept going back to me about it (in another narration, Umar kept going back to me) until God opened my chest to what he had opened Abu Bakr's chest to."
>
> > He said, "So I sought out the Quran, collecting it from scraps of parchment, palm stalks, thin stones (lakhaf) and the chests of men, until I found the end of Surat al-Tawba with Khuzayma, or Abu Khuzayma, the Ansari. I did not find it with anyone else, 'A messenger has come to you from among yourselves, it is grievous to him...', the closing verses of Bara'a." He said, "The sheets then remained with Abu Bakr until God took him, then with Umar until God took him, then with Hafsa, the daughter of Umar."
>
> > Some of the transmitters said that in this report lakhaf means pottery.
>
> He said in Jami al-Usul that al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi transmitted it.

In Zayd's account, the killing on the day of Yamama has been heavy among the Qur'an reciters. Umar fears that much of the Qur'an will be lost and urges Abu Bakr to collect it. Abu Bakr then asks Zayd to gather the Qur'an. He gathers it from scraps of parchment, palm stalks, thin stones and men's memories. A narrator glosses the word for thin stones, lakhaf, as pottery.

> [!note]- Uthman, in al-Askari, al-Qur'an al-Karim wa Riwayat al-Madrasatayn, vol.1, p.211
> في مسند أحمد بسنده عن ابن عباس أنه قال في حديثه عن الخليفة عثمان أنّه قال : إن رسول اللّه ( ص ) كان مما يأتي عليه الزمان ينزل عليه من السور ذوات العدد ، وكان إذا أنزل عليه الشيء يدعو بعض من يكتب عنده ، يقول : ضعوا هذا في السورة التي يذكر فيها كذا وكذا ، وينزل عليه الآيات فيقول : ضعوا هذه الآيات في السورة التي يذكر فيها كذا وكذا ، وينزل عليه الآية فيقول : ضعوا هذه الآية في السورة التي يذكر فيها كذا وكذا (9) .
>
> In the Musnad of Ahmad, with its chain of transmission, from Ibn Abbas, who said in his report about the caliph Uthman that he said.
>
> > “Time would often pass for the Messenger of God while a number of surahs were being revealed to him. Whenever something was revealed to him, he would call one of those who wrote for him and say, ‘Put this in the surah in which such and such is mentioned.’ Verses would be revealed to him and he would say, ‘Put these verses in the surah in which such and such is mentioned.’ A verse would be revealed to him and he would say, ‘Put this verse in the surah in which such and such is mentioned.’”

Al-Askari cites Musnad Ahmad, where Ibn Abbas reports Uthman's account. The Prophet ﷺ told his scribes to place each revealed verse in a named sura. By this report, the Prophet ﷺ assigned verses to their suras.

- **Source:** Ibn Abi Dawud, Kitab al-Masahif, p.67, no.39
- **Speaker:** Imam Ali ﵇, through Suwayd ibn Ghafala
- **Claim:** had Uthman not done it with the codices, Ali ﵇ would have

> [!note]- Imam Ali, Ibn Abi Dawud, Kitab al-Masahif, p.67, no.39
> [ 39 ] حدثنا (39) عبد اللّه قال حدثنا سهل بن صالح قال قال حدثنا أبو داود ويعقوب قالا أخبرنا شعبة عن علقمة بن مرثد عن سويد بن غفلة قال قال علي في المصاحف لو لم يصنعه عثمان لصنعته [ قال أبو داود « * » عن رجل عن سويد ] .
>
> [39] Abd Allah narrated to us, he said, Sahl ibn Salih narrated to us, he said, he said, Abu Dawud and Yaqub narrated to us, both said, Shuba informed us, from Alqama ibn Marthad, from Suwayd ibn Ghafala, who said.
>
> > Ali said about the codices, “If Uthman had not done it, I would have done it.”
>
> [Abu Dawud said, from a man, from Suwayd.]

Suwayd ibn Ghafala reports that Ali ﵇ said of the codices, "If Uthman had not done it, I would have done it." Ibn Abi Dawud notes that Abu Dawud's version of the chain has an unnamed man before Suwayd. If the report is sound, Ali's ﵇ words endorse Uthman's unification of the codices.

## The Earliest Manuscripts

- **Source:** University of Birmingham news release, 22 July 2015; van Putten, BSOAS 82 (2019), pp.271-288; Sadeghi and Bergmann, Arabica 57 (2010), pp.343-436
- **Speaker:** the University of Birmingham; Marijn van Putten; Behnam Sadeghi and Uwe Bergmann
- **Claim:** the earliest dated copies fall close to the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime, and van Putten argues that fourteen early manuscripts descend from one written archetype

Radiocarbon analysis dated the parchment of the two Birmingham leaves to between 568 and 645 CE, with 95.4 per cent accuracy. The leaves carry parts of suras 18 to 20 in Hijazi, an early form of Arabic script. Marijn van Putten examined how fourteen early manuscripts spell ni'mat in the phrase "the grace of God". Each manuscript uses the same one of two possible spellings at the same places. He argues that only a single written archetype explains this agreement. On his argument, a project to codify the text took place in the first Islamic century. Sadeghi and Bergmann describe a manuscript from the first half of the seventh century CE. Its text does not belong to the Uthmanic tradition. They report it as the only known manuscript of that kind. These studies support an early written standard text. They do not show what the Companions' earlier copies contained.

## The Scholars of the School

- **Source:** al-Saduq, al-I'tiqadat, p.86
- **Speaker:** Shaykh al-Saduq (d.381 AH)
- **Claim:** the Qur'an is what lies between the two covers, and whoever attributes more to the Imamis lies

> [!tip]- al-Saduq, al-I'tiqadat, p.86
> اعتقادنا أن القرآن الذي أنزله الله تعالى على نبيه محمد ﵌ هو ما بين الدفتين ، وهو ما في أيدي الناس ، ليس بأكثر من ذلك ، ومبلغ سوره عند الناس مائة وأربع عشرة سورة . وعندنا أن الضحى وألم نشرح سورة واحدة ، ولايلاف وألم تر كيف سورة واحدة (1) . ومن نسب إلينا أنا نقول إنه أكثر من ذلك فهو كاذب .
>
> Our belief is that the Quran which God Almighty sent down to His Prophet Muhammad is what lies between the two covers, and it is what is in people's hands. It is not more than that. The number of its surahs among the people is one hundred and fourteen. We hold that al-Duha and Alam Nashrah are one surah, and that Li-Ilaf and Alam Tara Kayfa are one surah. Whoever attributes to us the claim that it is more than that is a liar.

Al-Saduq's creed says the Qur'an God sent down is what lies between the two covers, and no more. He gives the people's count of suras as 114. He adds that the Imamis count al-Duha with al-Sharh, and al-Fil with Quraysh, as single suras. That ruling changes the count of suras and leaves the text the same.

- **Source:** al-Mufid, al-Masa'il al-Sarawiyya, pp.78-79 and p.81; Awa'il al-Maqalat, pp.82-83
- **Speaker:** Shaykh al-Mufid (d.413 AH)
- **Claim:** al-Mufid gave two answers on omission, and in Awa'il al-Maqalat he inclined to the view that only interpretation was removed

> [!warning]- al-Mufid, al-Masa'il al-Sarawiyya, pp.78-79
> المسألة التاسعة : صيانة القرآن من التحريف ما قولة - أدام الله تعالى حراسته (1) - في القرآن : أهو ما بين الدفتين ، الذي في أيدي الناس ، أم هل ضاع مما أنزل الله تعالى على نبيه منه شئ ، أم لا ؟ وهل هو ما جمعه أمير المؤمنين ﵇ ، أم ما جمعه عثمان بن عفان على ما يذكره المخالفون ؟ الجواب : لا شك (2) أن الذي بين الدفتين من القرآن جميعه (3) كلام الله تعالى وتنزيله ، وليس فيه شئ من كلام البشر ، وهو جمهور المنزل . والباقي مما أنزله (4) الله تعالى (5) عند المستحفظ للشريعة ، المستودع
> للأحكام ، لم يضع (1) منه شئ (2) . وإن كان الذي جمع ما بين الدفتين الآن لم يجعله في جملة ما جمع لأسباب (3) دعته إلى ذلك ، منها : قصوره عن معرفة بعضه . ومنها : شكه فيه وعدم تيقنه (4) . ومنها : ما تعمد إخراجه منه . وقد جمع أمير المؤمنين ﵇ القرآن المنزل من أوله إلى آخره ، وألفه بحسب ما وجب من تأليفه ، فقدم المكي على المدني ، والمنسوخ على الناسخ ، ووضع كل شئ منه في محله (5) . فلذلك قاد جعفر بن محمد الصادق ﵉ : " أما والله لو قرئ القرآن كما أنزل لألفيتمونا فيه مسمين كما سمي من كان قبلنا " (6) .
>
> Ninth question, the protection of the Quran from alteration. What is the opinion of the shaykh, may God Almighty prolong his guardianship, about the Quran? Is it what lies between the two covers, which is in people's hands, or has some of what God Almighty sent down to His Prophet been lost, or not? And is it what the Commander of the Faithful collected, or what Uthman ibn Affan collected, as the opponents say?
>
> The answer is that there is no doubt that what lies between the two covers, all of it, is the speech of God Almighty and His revelation, and that nothing in it is the speech of human beings. It is the majority of what was revealed. The rest of what God Almighty revealed is with the one entrusted to preserve the law and to whom the rulings are committed, and none of it has been lost. This is so even though the one who collected what lies between the two covers did not include it all in what he collected, for reasons that led him to that. Among them were his limited knowledge of some of it, his doubt about some of it and his lack of certainty about it, and his deliberate exclusion of some of it.
>
> The Commander of the Faithful collected the revealed Quran from its beginning to its end and arranged it as its arrangement required. He placed the Meccan before the Medinan and the abrogated before the abrogating, and put everything in its proper place. For that reason Jafar ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq said, “By God, if the Quran were recited as it was revealed, you would find us named in it, just as those before us were named.”

> [!tip]- al-Mufid, al-Masa'il al-Sarawiyya, p.81
> غير أن الخبر قد صح عن أئمتنا ﵈ أنهم أمروا بقراءة ما بين الدفتين ، وأن لا (1) يتعداه إلا زيادة فيه ولا نقصان منه حتى يقوم القائم ﵇ فيقرأ للناس (2) القرآن على ما أنزله الله تعالى وجمعه أمير المؤمنين ﵇ (3) .
>
> However, the report has been established as sound from our Imams that they commanded the recitation of what lies between the two covers, and that one should not go beyond it, whether by adding to it or by subtracting from it, until the Riser rises and recites to the people the Quran as God Almighty revealed it and as the Commander of the Faithful collected it.

> [!tip]- al-Mufid, Awa'il al-Maqalat, pp.82-83
> وأما النقصان فإن العقول لا تحيله ولا تمنع من وقوعه ، وقد امتحنت مقالة من ادعاه ، وكلمت عليه المعتزلة وغيرهم طويلا فلم اظفر منهم بحجة اعتمدها في فساده . وقد قال جماعة من أهل الإمامة إنه لم ينقص من كلمة ولا من آية ولا من سورة ولكن حذف ما كان مثبتا في مصحف أمير المؤمنين ( ع ) من تأويله وتفسير معانيه على حقيقة تنزيله وذلك كان ثابتا منزلا وإن لم يكن من جملة كلام الله تعالى الذي هو القرآن المعجز ، وقد يسمى تأويل القرآن قرآنا قال الله تعالى : ( ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه وقل رب زدني علما ) فسمى تأويل القرآن قرآنا ، وهذا ما ليس فيه بين أهل التفسير اختلاف . وعندي أن هذا القول أشبه من مقال من ادعى نقصان كلم من نفس القرآن على الحقيقة دون التأويل ، وإليه أميل والله أسأل توفيقه للصواب . وأما الزيادة فيه فمقطوع على فسادها من وجه ويجوز صحتها من وجه ، فالوجه الذي أقطع على فساده أن يمكن لأحد من الخلق زيادة مقدار سورة فيه على حد يلتبس به عند أحد من الفصحاء ، وأما الوجه المجوز فهو أن يزاد فيه الكلمة والكلمتان والحرف والحرفان وما أشبه ذلك مما لا يبلغ حد الاعجاز ، ويكون ملتبسا عند أكثر الفصحاء بكلم القرآن ، غير أنه لا بد متى وقع ذلك من أن
> يدل الله عليه ، ويوضح لعباده عن الحق فيه ، ولست أقطع على كون ذلك بل أميل إلى عدمه وسلامة القرآن عنه ، ومعي بذلك حديث عن الصادق جعفر بن محمد (ع) ، وهذا المذهب بخلاف ما سمعناه عن بني نوبخت - ﵏ - من الزيادة في القرآن والنقصان فيه ، وقد ذهب إليه جماعة من متكلمي الإمامية وأهل الفقه منهم والاعتبار .
>
> As for omission, reason does not rule it out or prevent it from happening. I have examined the claim of those who asserted it, and I have spoken at length about it with the Mu'tazila and others, but I found in them no argument that I could rely on to show it false. A group of the Imamis have said that no word, verse or chapter was left out. What was removed, they say, is what had been written in the codex of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, namely its interpretation and the explanation of its meanings according to the truth of its revelation. That material was established and sent down, even though it was not part of the speech of God Most High that is the inimitable Quran.
>
> The interpretation of the Quran can also be called Quran. God Most High said, "Do not hasten with the Quran before its revelation is completed to you, and say, 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge.'" So He called the interpretation of the Quran "Quran," and the scholars of exegesis do not disagree about this. In my view this position is closer to the truth than the statement of those who claimed that actual words were lost from the Quran itself, rather than from its interpretation. I incline toward it, and I ask God for success in reaching what is correct.
>
> As for addition to the Quran, one kind is certainly false and another kind is possible. The kind I am certain is false is that any human being could add the length of a chapter to it in such a way that it would be confused with the Quran in the judgment of any eloquent speaker. The kind that is possible is that a word or two words, or a letter or two letters, or something similar that does not reach the level of inimitability, was added to it and was mistaken for Quranic words by most eloquent speakers. Even so, if that had happened, God would necessarily have pointed it out and made the truth about it clear to His servants. I am not certain that it happened. I incline instead toward its not having happened and toward the Quran being free of it, and I have a report from al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, that supports this.
>
> This position differs from what we heard from the Banu Nawbakht, may God have mercy on them, about addition to the Quran and omission from it. A group of Imami theologians, including their jurists and scholars of reflection, have held to it.

In al-Sarawiyya al-Mufid says everything between the covers is God's speech and the majority of what was sent down. He says the rest is with the guardian of the law, who is entrusted with the rulings, and none of it is lost. He names three reasons the compiler left it out, namely limited knowledge, doubt and deliberate exclusion. He adds that the Imams ﵈ commanded recitation of what lies between the covers until al-Qa'im ﵇ rises.

In Awa'il al-Maqalat al-Mufid says reason allows omission. He found no argument against it that he could rely on. He reports a group of Imamis who deny the loss of any word, verse or sura. They hold that what was removed was the interpretation recorded in Ali's ﵇ codex. Al-Mufid calls their view closer to the truth and inclines toward it. He rules out the addition of a sura's length, and he allows that a word or a letter could be added. He says that God would make any such addition known, and he inclines to deny that it occurred. The sources quoted give no order in which al-Mufid wrote the two works.

- **Source:** al-Murtada, al-Dhakhira fi Ilm al-Kalam, pp.361-362; al-Tabrisi, Majma' al-Bayan, vol.1, pp.42-43
- **Speaker:** al-Sharif al-Murtada (d.436 AH); Amin al-Islam al-Tabrisi (d.548 AH)
- **Claim:** knowledge of the Qur'an's transmission is like knowledge of great cities and events

> [!tip]- al-Murtada, al-Dhakhira, pp.361-362
> فان قيل : كيف يكون أحد الامرين كالآخر والامامية تدّعي تغييرا في القرآن ونقصانا ، وكذلك حشوية أصحاب الحديث ؟ قلنا : قد بيّنا صحة نقل القرآن في المسائل الطرابلسيات (3) ، وأنه غير
> منقوص ولا مبدّل ولا مغيّر ، وأن العلم بأن هذا القرآن الذي في أيدينا هو الذي ظهر على يد رسول اللّه « ص » كالعلم بالبلدان والحوادث الكبار والوقائع العظام ، والكتب المصنفة المشهورة ، والاشعار المدونة . وذكرنا أن العناية اشتدت بالقرآن والدواعي توفرت على نقله وحراسته وبلغت إلى حدّ لم يبلغه في نقل الحوادث والوقائع والكتب المصنفة ، لأن القرآن معجز النبوة ، وأصل العلم بالشريعة والاحكام الدينية . وكل شيء دعا إلى نقل جميع ما تقدم حاصل فيه ، ويستبدّ بدواع إلى النقل ليست في الحوادث وما أشبهها ، وأن علماء المتكلمين بلغوا في ضبطه وحمايته ، وان عرفوا كل شيء اختلف (1) فيه من اعرابه والقراءات المختلفة في حروفه حتى فرّقوا بين ما روي وعرف ، وبين ما لم يذكر ولم يسطر . فكيف يجوز أن يكون مغيّرا أو منقوصا مع هذه العناية الصادقة والضبط الشديد ؟
>
> If it is asked how one of the two matters can be like the other, when the Imamis claim alteration and diminution in the Quran, and so do the Hashwiyya among the hadith folk, we say that we have already explained the soundness of the transmission of the Quran in al-Masa'il al-Tarabulusiyyat. We showed that it is not diminished, replaced, or altered. We also showed that knowledge that this Quran in our hands is what appeared at the hands of the Messenger of God is like knowledge of countries, great events, major incidents, famous compiled books, and recorded poems.
>
> We mentioned also that care for the Quran was intense, and that the motives to transmit and guard it were abundant, to a degree not reached in the transmission of events, incidents, and compiled books. The reason is that the Quran is the miracle that proves prophethood and the foundation of knowledge of the Law and of religious rulings. Everything that prompted the transmission of all those earlier things is present in it, and it alone has motives for transmission that events and the like do not have. The scholars among the theologians went so far in preserving and protecting it that they even knew everything disputed in it, such as its grammatical inflection and the different readings of its letters, until they distinguished between what was narrated and known and what was not mentioned or written down. So how can it be altered or diminished, given this genuine care and strict preservation?

Al-Murtada answers an objector who says the Imamis, like the hashwiyya among the traditionists, claim change and loss in the Qur'an. Hashwiyya is the name the objector gives to a group among the hadith folk. Al-Murtada says knowledge of the Qur'an's transmission is like knowledge of great cities and famous events. He adds that the theologians among the scholars knew everything disputed in it, including its inflection and its readings. He asks how the Qur'an could be altered or diminished under such care.

In the introduction to Majma' al-Bayan, al-Tabrisi sets aside the discussion of addition to and loss from the Qur'an as unsuitable for exegesis.

> [!tip]- al-Tabrisi, Majma' al-Bayan, vol.1, pp.42-43
> ومن ذلك : الكلام في زيادة القرآن ونقصانه فإنه لا يليق بالتفسير . فأما الزيادة
> فيه : فمجمع على بطلانه . وأما النقصان منه : فقد روى جماعة من أصحابنا ، وقوم من حشوية العامة ، أن في القرآن تغييرا أو نقصانا ، والصحيح من مذهب أصحابنا خلافه
>
> Of this kind is the discussion of increase and decrease in the Quran, which is unsuitable for exegesis. As for increase in it, its invalidity is unanimously agreed. As for decrease from it, a group of our companions and a group of the Hashwiyya of the general body of Muslims (al-'amma) have narrated that the Quran contains alteration or diminution. The sound position of our companions is the opposite.

Al-Tabrisi calls addition invalid by consensus. He reports that some Imamis, and a band of the hashwiyya among the general body of Muslims, narrated loss. He calls the denial of loss the sound position of his school. His passage reports the loss view without naming the scholars who held it.

- **Source:** al-Khoei, al-Bayan, p.259
- **Speaker:** al-Khoei
- **Claim:** the claim of tahrif is a fable

> [!tip]- al-Khoei, al-Bayan, p.259
> ومما ذكرناه : قد تبين للقارئ أن حديث تحريف القرآن حديث خرافة وخيال ، لا يقول به إلا من ضعف عقله ، أو من لم يتأمل في أطرافه حق التأمل ، أو من ألجأه إليه يجب القول به . والحب يعمي ويصم ، وأما العاقل المنصف المتدبر فلا يشك في بطلانه وخرافته .
>
> From what we have mentioned, it has become clear to the reader that the talk of the Qur'an's alteration is a superstitious tale and a fantasy. No one holds it except one whose reason is weak, or one who has not reflected on its aspects with the reflection they deserve, or one whom love of holding the view drives to it. Love blinds and deafens. But the sensible, fair-minded person who reflects has no doubt that it is false and a superstitious tale.

Al-Khoei closes his discussion by calling tahrif a fable. He says only a weak or unreflecting mind holds it, or one whom love of the view drives to it. The printed al-Bayan reads yajib, "must", at that point. Other works that quote the passage read hubb, "love", which matches al-Khoei's next sentence, "Love blinds and deafens".

- **Source:** al-Khomeini, Anwar al-Hidaya fi al-Ta'liqa ala al-Kifaya, vol.1, pp.207-208
- **Speaker:** Sayyid Ruhollah al-Khomeini (d.1409 AH)
- **Claim:** the verifying scholars of both groups deny tahrif, and Fasl al-Khitab cites reports the early scholars had set aside

> [!tip]- al-Khomeini, Anwar al-Hidaya, vol.1, pp.207-208
> أمّا الأولى : فلمنع وقوع التحريف فيه جدّاً ، كما هو مذهب المحقّقين من علماء العامّة والخاصّة ، والمعتبرين من الفريقين ، وإن شئت شطراً من الكلام في هذا المقام فارجع إلى مقدّمة تفسير آلاء الرحمن للعلّامة البلاغي المعاصر ﵋ (2) . وأزيدك توضيحاً : أنّه لو كان الأمر كما توهّم صاحب «فصل الخطاب» الذي كان كتبه لا يفيد علماً ولا عملًا ، وإنّما هو إيراد روايات أعرض عنها الأصحاب ، واختلاط ضعاف بين الروايات بعد تنزيهها عنها أولو الألباب من قدماء أصحابنا كالمحمّدين الثلاثة المتقدّمين ﵏ . هذا حال كتب روايته غالباً ك «المستدرك» ، ولا تسأل عن سائر كتبه المشحونة بالقصص والحكايات الغريبة التي غالبها بالهزل أشبه منه بالجدّ ، وهو ﵀ شخص صالح متتبّع ، إلّاأنّ اشتياقه لجمع الضعاف والغرائب والعجائب وما لا يقبلها العقل السليم والرأي المستقيم ، أكثر من الكلام النافع ، والعجب من معاصريه من أهل اليقظة ! كيف ذهلوا وغفلوا حتّى وقع ما وقع ممّا بكت عليه السماوات ، وكادت تتدكدك على الأرض ؟ !
> وبالجملة : لو كان الأمر كما ذكره هذا وأشباهه ، من كون الكتاب الإلهي مشحوناً بذكر أهل البيت وفضلهم ، وذكر أمير المؤمنين وإثبات وصايته وإمامته ، فلِمَ لم يحتجّ بواحد من تلك الآيات النازلة والبراهين القاطعة من الكتاب الإلهي أميرُالمؤمنين ، وفاطمة ، والحسن ، والحسين ﵈ وسلمان ، وأبوذرّ ، ومقداد ، وعمّار ، وسائر الأصحاب الذين لا يزالون يحتجّون على خلافته ﵇ (1) ؟ ! ولمَ تشبّث ﵇ بالأحاديث النبوية (2) ، والقرآن بين أظهرهم ؟ !
>
> As for the first, it is because the occurrence of distortion in it is utterly ruled out, as is the position of the verifying scholars among the general body of Muslims (al-'amma) and the particular group, and of the reliable authorities of both camps. If you want a portion of the discussion on this point, turn to the introduction of the Quran commentary Ala al-Rahman by the great contemporary scholar al-Balaghi. I add a further clarification for you. If the matter were as the author of Fasl al-Khitab imagined, whose books give neither knowledge nor practical benefit, and are only a presentation of reports that the associates turned away from, and a mixing of weak reports among the reports, after people of understanding among our early scholars, such as the three earlier Muhammads, had cleared them of these weak ones.
>
> This is the condition of his books of narration for the most part, such as al-Mustadrak. Do not ask about the rest of his books, which are crammed with strange stories and tales, most of which resemble jest more than earnest. He was a righteous and diligent researcher, except that his eagerness to gather weak, strange and wondrous reports, which sound reason and upright judgment do not accept, was greater than his eagerness for useful discourse. It is astonishing that his contemporaries among the people of alertness were so stunned and heedless that what happened did happen, the thing over which the heavens wept and almost crumbled onto the earth!
>
> In short, if the matter were as he and his like have stated, that the divine Book is crammed with mention of the Ahl al-Bayt and their merit, and with mention of the Commander of the Faithful and proof of his designation as successor and his imamate, then why did none of those revealed verses and decisive proofs from the divine Book get cited as argument by the Commander of the Faithful, Fatima, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, or by Salman, Abu Dharr, al-Miqdad, Ammar, and the rest of the Companions who kept arguing for his caliphate? And why did he hold fast to the prophetic traditions while the Quran was in their midst?

Al-Khomeini says the verifying scholars among the general body of Muslims (al-'amma) and among the particular group (al-khassa), meaning the Shia, deny tahrif. He says Fasl al-Khitab, al-Nuri's collection of reports on tahrif, cites reports that the associates (al-ashab, the school's scholars) turned away from. He adds that early scholars such as the three Muhammads had already cleared the reports of such weak items. Imami scholars give that name to al-Kulayni, al-Saduq and al-Tusi. He calls al-Nuri righteous and diligent, and too eager for weak and strange material. On the next page he tests the claim of the author of Fasl al-Khitab "and his like" against the history of the dispute over succession. Suppose the Book were full of the Household's merits and of Ali's ﵇ appointment. He asks why Ali ﵇, Fatimah ﵍, al-Hasan ﵇ and al-Husayn ﵇ never argued from those verses. He asks the same of Salman, Abu Dharr, al-Miqdad and Ammar. He also asks why Ali ﵇ relied on the Prophet's ﷺ hadiths while the Qur'an was among them.

> [!tip]- al-Sistani, Istifta'at, p.131, no.489
> 489 . السؤال : لقد قرأت كثيرا في ما ينشر على الانترنت عن موضوع تحريف القرآن ، حيث ينسبونه إلى الشيعة ويستدلون بأدلة من المذهب الشيعي ، فلا أعلم مدى صحة هذه الأقاويل ؟ الجواب : دعوى باطلة أجيب عليها من قبل علماء الشيعة مرات عديدة وهم يكررون القول الباطل وعقيدتنا أن القرآن المنزل من الله تعالى على النبي الأكرم - ﵌ - هو نفس القرآن الموجود لدى المسلمين حاليا من دون زيادة ولا نقيصة .
>
> 489. Question. I have read a great deal of what is published on the internet about the subject of the distortion of the Qur'an. They attribute it to the Shia and cite evidence from the Shia school, and I do not know how valid these claims are.
>
> Answer. It is a false claim. Shia scholars have answered it many times, yet they keep repeating the false statement. Our belief is that the Qur'an sent down by God Almighty upon the Noble Prophet is the very Qur'an that Muslims have today, without addition or deficiency.

Al-Sistani is asked about internet claims that attribute tahrif to the Shia. He calls the claim false. He says the Qur'an God sent down is the Qur'an Muslims have today, without addition or deficiency.

- **Source:** al-Fayd al-Kashani, al-Safi, vol.1, pp.52-58
- **Speaker:** al-Fayd al-Kashani (d.1091 AH)
- **Claim:** the reports show the Qur'an in hand is incomplete, and the whole survives with its people

> [!warning]- al-Fayd al-Kashani, al-Safi, vol.1, p.52
> أقول : المستفاد من مجمع هذه الأخبار وغيرها من الروايات من طريق أهل البيت (عيهم السلام) إن القرآن الذي بين أظهرنا ليس بتمامه كما انزل على محمد (﵌) منه ما هو خلاف ما أنزل الله ومنه ما هو مغير ومحرف وإنه قد حذف عنه أشياء كثيرة منها اسم علي (﵇) في كثير من المواضع ومنها غير ذلك وأنه ليس أيضا على الترتيب المرضي عند الله وعند رسوله (﵌) .
>
> I say. What is gathered from the whole of these reports and from other narrations by way of the Ahl al-Bayt is that the Qur'an among us is not complete as it was sent down to Muhammad. Part of it is contrary to what God sent down, and part of it is altered and distorted. Many things have been removed from it, among them the name of Ali in many places, and other things besides. It is also not in the order that is pleasing to God and to His Messenger.

> [!tip]- al-Fayd al-Kashani, al-Safi, vol.1, p.54
> أقول : ويرد على هذا كله إشكال وهو أنه على هذا التقدير لم يبق لنا اعتماد على شئ من القرآن إذ على هذا يحتمل كل آية منه أن يكون محرفا ومغيرا ويكون على خلاف ما أنزل الله فلم يبق لنا في القرآن حجة أصلا فتنتفي فائدته وفائدة الأمر باتباعه والوصية بالتمسك به إلى غير ذلك ، وأيضا قال الله ﷿ : وإنه لكتاب عزيز لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه . وقال : إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون فكيف يتطرق إليه التحريف والتغيير ، وأيضا قد استفاض عن النبي (﵌) والأئمة (﵈) حديث عرض الخبر المروي على كتاب الله ليعلم صحته بموافقته له وفساده بمخالفته فإذا كان القرآن الذي بأيدينا محرفا فما فائدة العرض مع أن خبر التحريف مخالف لكتاب الله مكذب له فيجب رده والحكم بفساده أو تأويله .
>
> I say that an objection arises against all of this. On this assumption, we are left with nothing in the Quran that we can rely on. For on this view every verse in it could be altered and changed, and could differ from what God sent down. Then nothing in the Quran would remain a proof for us at all, so its benefit would be lost. The benefit of the command to follow it and of the instruction to hold fast to it would be lost too, and so on.
>
> Also, God, mighty and majestic, said, "And it is indeed a mighty Book. Falsehood cannot come at it from before it or from behind it." And He said, "It is We who sent down the Reminder, and it is We who will guard it." So how could alteration or change reach it?
>
> Also, the hadith about presenting a transmitted report to the Book of God is widely reported from the Prophet and the Imams. By it, the soundness of a report is known through its agreement with the Book, and its falseness through its disagreement. If the Quran in our hands were altered, what would be the use of this presentation? Moreover, the report of alteration contradicts the Book of God and denies it. So it must be rejected and judged false, or else interpreted.

> [!tip]- al-Fayd al-Kashani, al-Safi, vol.1, p.55
> ولا يبعد أيضا أن يقال إن بعض المحذوفات كان من قبيل التفسير والبيان ولم يكن من أجزاء القرآن فيكون التبديل من حيث المعنى أي حرفوه وغيروه في تفسيره وتأويله أعني حملوه على خلاف ما هو به ، فمعنى قولهم (﵈) كذا نزلت أن المراد به ذلك لا أنها نزلت مع هذه الزيادة في لفظها فحذف منها ذلك اللفظ .
>
> It is also not far-fetched to say that some of the omitted material was explanation and clarification, and was not part of the Quran. In that case the substitution is in the meaning. That is, they altered and changed the Quran in its explanation and interpretation, by which I mean they applied it contrary to what it really means. So the saying of the Imams, "It was revealed thus," means that the intended sense is that one. It does not mean that the verse was revealed with this addition in its wording, and that this wording was then removed from it.

> [!warning]- al-Fayd al-Kashani, al-Safi, vol.1, p.58
> أقول : يكفي في وجوده في كل عصر وجوده جميعا كما أنزله الله محفوظا عند أهله ووجود ما احتجنا إليه منه عندنا وإن لم نقدر على الباقي كما أن الإمام (﵇) كذلك فان الثقلين سيان في ذلك .
>
> I say, for its existence in every age it is enough that all of it exists, just as God sent it down, preserved with its people, and that what we need of it is with us, even if we are unable to reach the rest. The Imam is the same in this respect, for the two weighty things are alike in that.

Al-Fayd reads the reports as showing that the Qur'an in hand is incomplete, partly altered and out of order. He counts Ali's ﵇ name among the things removed. He lists three objections to that reading. No verse could be relied on, and Qur'an 15:9 and 41:42 would be contradicted. Qur'an 41:42 says falsehood cannot reach the Book. The rule of judging reports by the Book would also lose its use. He allows that some omitted material was explanation, so that "it was revealed thus" gives the intended sense. He concludes that the whole Qur'an exists, preserved with "its people" (ahlihi), a phrase for which he names no group. The part the community needs is in its hands, even if it cannot reach the rest. He likens the Qur'an to the Imam, who also exists beyond the community's reach. Al-Mufid's Sarawiyya places the rest of the revelation with the guardian of the law, which resembles this answer.

## Glossary

- **shawadhdh.** Irregular readings, reported outside the accepted readings.
- **tanzil.** Revelation, the act of sending down or the text sent down. Al-Tabataba'i reads "it was revealed thus" in many reports as the explanation that accompanied the revelation.
- **kuttab.** Plural of katib, writer or scribe.

## Final Verdict

> [!summary] Final Verdict
> Imami scholars from al-Saduq to al-Sistani hold that the Qur'an between the two covers is the Qur'an God sent down. Al-Majlisi and al-Fayd al-Kashani read some reports as evidence of loss, and al-Mufid allows omission by the compiler. These positions show that some Imami scholars accepted or allowed omission. They do not make alteration the doctrine of the Imamiyya.

blocks.text: The Preserved Qur'an

Premise 1. Ibn Hazm charged the Imamiyya with holding that the Qur'an was changed, with words added and many removed. He exempted one Imami and two companions. Al-Safadi quotes the charge in his entry on al-Sharif al-Murtada. His quotation names the exempted man Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa, which is al-Murtada's name. Premise 2. The Qur'an uses tahrif for moving words from their places and meanings. Al-Khoei names the loss of revealed text as the sense of tahrif that Muslims dispute. Premise 3. Al-Kafi carries reports of a larger revelation and of verses Jibril brought "in this form" with a name added. It also carries a report of a scribal error in Qur'an 5:95. Sunni books carry reports in which Ibn Abbas calls words of the codex a scribe's error. Premise 4. The Imams ﵈ told their followers to judge reports by the Qur'an. They also told them to recite as the people recite until al-Qa'im rises. Al-Tusi classes the reports of loss as solitary reports, which yield neither certain knowledge nor grounds for action. Premise 5. Al-Saduq, al-Murtada, al-Khoei, al-Tabataba'i, al-Khomeini and al-Sistani hold that the Qur'an in Muslim hands is the Qur'an God sent down. Al-Tabrisi calls that the sound view of the school, and al-Tusi calls it the view more fitting for the sound position of his school. Al-Majlisi, and al-Fayd al-Kashani in al-Safi, read some reports as evidence of loss. Conclusion. Imami scholars including al-Saduq, al-Murtada, al-Khoei, al-Tabataba'i, al-Khomeini and al-Sistani affirm the received Qur'an, and some Imami scholars accepted reports of omission. Sunni books carry reports of scribal error, which Sunni scholars accepted, interpreted or rejected. Al-Tusi classed the Imami reports of loss as solitary, and scholars of both schools disputed what the reports show. Ibn Hazm's charge presents that dispute as the doctrine of the Imamiyya.

blocks.text: The Charge Ibn Hazm Recorded

Source: Ibn Hazm, al-Fisal fi al-Milal wa al-Ahwa' wa al-Nihal, vol.4, p.182; al-Safadi, al-Wafi bil-Wafayat, vol.21, pp.2-3 Speaker: Ibn Hazm al-Andalusi (d.456 AH); Salah al-Din al-Safadi (d.764 AH) Claim: all Imamiyya hold the Qur'an was altered, except one named Imami and his two companions

Ibn Hazm, al-Fisal, vol.4, p.182 ومن قول الإمامية كلها قديما وحديثا ان القرآن مبدل زيد فيه ما ليس منه ونقص منه كثير وبدل منه كثير حاشا علي ابن الحسن ابن موسى بن محمد بن إبراهيم بن موسى بن جعفر بن محمد بن علي بن الحسن ابن علي بن أبي طالب وكان أماميا يظاهر بالاعتزال مع ذلك فإنه كان ينكر هذا القول ويكفر من قاله وكذلك صاحباه أبو يعلى ميلاد الطوسي وأبو القاسم الرازي It is the view of all the Imamites, early and late, that the Qur'an has been altered, that material not part of it was added to it, and that much was removed from it and much was changed in it. The one exception is Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Musa ibn Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib. He was an Imamite who openly sided with Mu'tazilism, and yet he rejected this view and declared anyone who held it an unbeliever. His two companions, Abu Yala Milad al-Tusi and Abu al-Qasim al-Razi, did the same.

Ibn Hazm, an Andalusian scholar, surveys religions and sects in al-Fisal. He attributes the view of an altered Qur'an to all the Imamiyya, the Imami Shia, early and late. He exempts one Imami with Mu'tazili leanings. The printed al-Fisal names him Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Musa and traces his descent to Musa ibn Ja'far. Ibn Hazm reports that this man rejected the view and called its holders unbelievers. He reports the same of two companions, Abu Ya'la Milad al-Tusi and Abu al-Qasim al-Razi.

al-Safadi, al-Wafi bil-Wafayat, vol.21, pp.2-3 الشريف المرتضى علي بن الحسين بين موسى بن محمد بن موسى بن إبراهيم بن موسى بن جعفر بن محمد بن علي بن الحسين بن علي بن أبي طالب أبو القاسم المرتضى علم الهدى نقيب العلويين أخو الشريف الرضي ولد سنة خمس وخمسين وثلاث مائة وتوفي سنة ست وثلاثين وأربع مائة وكان فاضلا ماهرا أديبا متكلما له مصنفات جمة على مذهب الشيعة قال الخطيب كتبت عنه وكان رأسا في الاعتزال كثير الاطلاع والجدال قال ابن حزم في الملل والنحل ومن قول الإمامية كلها قديما وحديثا أن القرآن مبدل زيد فيه ونقص منه حاشا علي بن الحسين بن موسى وكان إماميا فيه تظاهر بالاعتزال ومع ذلك فإنه كان ينكر هذا) القول وكفر من قاله وكذلك صاحباه أبو يعلى الطوسي وأبو القاسم الرازي Al-Sharif al-Murtada Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Ibrahim ibn Musa ibn Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu al-Qasim al-Murtada, Alam al-Huda, was the marshal (naqib) of the Alawids, the descendants of Ali, and the brother of al-Sharif al-Radi. He was born in the year 355 and died in the year 436. He was a distinguished and skilled scholar, a man of letters and a theologian, and he wrote many works according to the doctrine of the Shia. Al-Khatib said, "I wrote down reports from him. He was a leader in the Mutazilite school, with wide learning and a great deal of debate." Ibn Hazm said in al-Milal wa-l-Nihal, "It is the position of all the Imamis, past and present, that the Quran has been altered, that something was added to it and something was removed from it, except Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa. He was an Imami who made a show of Mutazilism. Even so, he rejected this claim and declared anyone who made it to be an unbeliever. So did his two companions, Abu Yala al-Tusi and Abu al-Qasim al-Razi."

Al-Safadi, a biographer of the eighth century AH, quotes this passage in his entry on al-Sharif al-Murtada. The entry opens with al-Murtada's lineage, Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa, traced to Musa ibn Ja'far. In the quotation, Ibn Hazm exempts a man of that same name, so al-Safadi treats the exempted man as al-Murtada. The printed al-Fisal gives the lineage in a different form. It has al-Hasan where al-Safadi has al-Husayn, at the start and near the end of the chain. It also lacks one Musa between Muhammad and Ibrahim. The identification of the exempted man with al-Murtada therefore rests on al-Safadi's quotation of Ibn Hazm.
What Tahrif Means

Source: al-Jawhari, al-Sihah, vol.4, p.31; Ibn Manzur, Lisan al-Arab, vol.9, p.43 Speaker: two classical lexicographers Claim: tahrif of speech is changing it, and the Qur'an uses the verb for changing meanings

al-Jawhari, al-Sihah, vol.4, p.31 وتحريف الكلام عن مواضعه : تغييره . وتحريف القلم : قطه محرفا . ويقال : انحرف عنه وتحرف واحرورف ، أي مال وعدل . Tahrif of speech from its places means changing it. Tahrif of the pen means cutting it at a slant. One says “inharafa from him,” “taharrafa,” and “ihrawrafa,” meaning that he inclined away and turned aside.

Ibn Manzur, Lisan al-Arab, vol.9, p.43 وتَحْرِيفُ الكَلِم عن مواضِعِه : تغييره . والتحريف في القرآن والكلمة : تغيير الحرفِ عن معناه والكلمة عن معناها وهي قريبة الشبه كما كانت اليهود تُغَيِّرُ مَعانَي التوراة بالأَشباه ، فوصَفَهم اللَّه بفعلهم فقال تعالى : يُحَرِّفُون الكَلِمَ عن مواضعه . To distort words away from their places is to change them. Distortion in the Qur'an and in a word means changing a letter away from its meaning, or a word away from its meaning, while keeping a close resemblance to it. The Jews used to change the meanings of the Torah in this way, by means of look-alikes. God described them by their deed in His words, "They distort words from their places."

Al-Jawhari defines the tahrif of speech as changing it from its places. Ibn Manzur says the Jews changed the meanings of the Torah by look-alikes. He quotes the Qur'an's words "they distort words from their places", which occur in Qur'an 4:46 and 5:13.
Verse: Qur'an 4:46 Claim: some of the Jews distort words from their places

Qur'an 4:46 مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلْكَلِمَ عَن مَّوَاضِعِهِۦ وَيَقُولُونَ سَمِعْنَا وَعَصَيْنَا وَٱسْمَعْ غَيْرَ مُسْمَعٍۢ وَرَٰعِنَا لَيًّۢا بِأَلْسِنَتِهِمْ وَطَعْنًۭا فِى ٱلدِّينِ ۚ وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ قَالُوا۟ سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا وَٱسْمَعْ وَٱنظُرْنَا لَكَانَ خَيْرًۭا لَّهُمْ وَأَقْوَمَ وَلَٰكِن لَّعَنَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُفْرِهِمْ فَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا mina alladhina hadu yuharrifuna al-kalima 'an mawadi'ihi wa-yaquluna sami'na wa-'asayna wa-isma' ghayra musma'in wa-ra'ina layyan bi-alsinatihim wa-ta'nan fi al-din, wa-law annahum qalu sami'na wa-ata'na wa-isma' wa-unzurna la-kana khayran lahum wa-aqwama wa-lakin la'anahumu Allahu bi-kufrihim fa-la yu'minuna illa qalilan Among those who are Jews are some who distort words from their proper places. They say, “We hear and we disobey,” and “Hear, without being made to hear,” and “Ra'ina,” twisting their tongues and slandering the religion. Had they said, “We hear and we obey,” and “Hear,” and “Look at us,” it would have been better for them and more upright. But God has cursed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except a little.

The Qur'an uses the verb four times, in Qur'an 2:75, 4:46, 5:13 and 5:41. Each verse describes people who alter the sense or the place of words in an earlier scripture. None of the four verses applies the verb to the Qur'an.
Source: al-Khoei, al-Bayan fi Tafsir al-Qur'an, pp.197 and 200 Speaker: Sayyid Abu al-Qasim al-Khoei (d.1413 AH) Claim: tahrif has several senses, and loss of text is the one in dispute among Muslims

al-Khoei, al-Bayan, p.197 1 - معنى التحريف : يطلق لفظ التحريف ويراد منه عدة معان على سبيل الاشتراك ، فبعض منها واقع في القرآن باتفاق من المسلمين ، وبعض منها لم يقع فيه باتفاق منهم أيضا ، وبعض منها وقع الخلاف بينهم . واليك تفصيل ذلك (1) : الأول : " نقل الشئ عن موضعه وتحويله إلى غيره " ومنه قوله تعالى : " من الذين هادوا يحرفون الكلم عن مواضعه 4 : 46 " . ولا خلاف بين المسلمين في وقوع مثل هذا التحريف في كتاب الله فإن كل من فسر القرآن بغير حقيقته ، وحمله على غير معناه فقد حرفه . وترى كثيرا من أهل البدع ، والمذاهب الفاسدة قد حرفوا القرآن بتأويلهم آياته على آرائهم وأهوائهم . وقد ورد المنع عن التحريف بهذا المعنى ، وذم فاعله في عدة من الروايات . 1. The meaning of tahrif. The word tahrif is used for several meanings as a shared term. Some of these meanings occur in the Qur'an by the agreement of the Muslims, some do not occur in it, also by their agreement, and about some of them the Muslims disagree. Here are the details. The first meaning is “moving a thing from its place and turning it into something else.” To this belongs the saying of the Exalted, “Among those who are Jews are some who distort words from their places” 4:46. There is no disagreement among the Muslims that this kind of tahrif occurs in the Book of God. Anyone who explains the Qur'an other than according to its reality, and applies it to a meaning other than its own, has distorted it. You will see many people of innovation and of corrupt schools who have distorted the Qur'an by interpreting its verses to fit their own opinions and desires. The prohibition of tahrif in this sense, and the condemnation of the one who does it, have come down in a number of reports.

al-Khoei, al-Bayan, p.200 الخامس : " التحريف بالزيادة بمعنى أن بعض المصحف الذي بأيدينا ليس من الكلام المنزل " . والتحريف بهذا المعنى باطل بإجماع المسلمين ، بل هو مما علم بطلانه بالضرورة . السادس : " التحريف بالنقيصة ، بمعنى أن المصحف الذي بأيدينا لا يشتمل على جميع القرآن الذي نزل من السماء ، فقد ضاع بعضه على الناس " . والتحريف بهذا المعنى هو الذي وقع فيه الخلاف فأثبته قوم ونفاه آخرون . The fifth meaning is “tahrif by addition, meaning that part of the codex in our hands is not part of the revealed speech.” Tahrif in this sense is false by the consensus of the Muslims. Its falsity is in fact known by necessity. The sixth meaning is “tahrif by omission, meaning that the codex in our hands does not contain all of the Qur'an that was sent down from heaven, so that some of it was lost to the people.” This is the sense of tahrif about which the disagreement occurred. One group affirmed it and others denied it.

Al-Khoei sorts the senses of tahrif by whether Muslims agree they occurred. His first sense is moving a thing from its place, and he applies it to interpreting a verse against its meaning. He says all Muslims agree that this kind of tahrif occurred. His fifth sense is addition of material that is not revealed speech, which he calls false by consensus. His sixth sense is omission, and he names it as the sense in dispute. The passages quoted here leave out his second to fourth senses. A report that uses the word tahrif may therefore mean a false interpretation. To support a charge of loss, a report has to speak of lost text.

Two positions below conflict with al-Khoei's claim of consensus on addition. Al-Mufid allows that a word or a letter could be added to the Qur'an. Al-Mazandarani reads the report on Qur'an 5:95 as a copyist's added letter.
The Guarantee of Qur'an 15:9
Verse: Qur'an 15:9 Claim: God sent down the Reminder and guards it

Qur'an 15:9 إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا ٱلذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ inna nahnu nazzalna al-dhikra wa-inna lahu la-hafizun Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its guardians.

Source: al-Tabataba'i, al-Mizan fi Tafsir al-Qur'an, vol.12, p.107 Speaker: Allama Muhammad Husayn al-Tabataba'i (d.1402 AH) Claim: the Qur'an in hand carries every attribute God gave it, so it is the Qur'an sent down

al-Tabataba'i, al-Mizan, vol.12, p.107 فقد تبين مما فصلناه ان القرآن الذي أنزله الله على نبيه ﵌ ووصفه بأنه ذكر محفوظ على ما انزل مصون بصيانة الهية عن الزيادة والنقيصة والتغيير كما وعد الله نبيه فيه . وخلاصة الحجة ان القرآن أنزله الله على نبيه ووصفه في آيات كثيرة بأوصاف خاصة لو كان تغير في شئ من هذه الأوصاف بزيادة أو نقيصة أو تغيير في لفظ أو ترتيب مؤثر فقد آثار تلك الصفة قطعا لكنا نجد القرآن الذي بأيدينا واجدا لاثار تلك الصفات المعدودة على أتم ما يمكن وأحسن ما يكون فلم يقع فيه تحريف يسلبه شيئا من صفاته فالذي بأيدينا منه هو القرآن المنزل على النبي ﵌ بعينه فلو فرض سقوط شئ منه أو تغير في اعراب أو حرف أو ترتيب وجب ان يكون في أمر لا يؤثر في شئ من أوصافه كالاعجاز وارتفاع الاختلاف والهداية والنورية والذكرية والهيمنة على سائر الكتب السماوية إلى غير ذلك وذلك كآية مكررة ساقطة أو اختلاف في نقطة أو اعراب ونحوها . What we have set out shows that the Qur'an which God sent down to his Prophet, and which he described as a preserved Reminder, remains as it was sent down. It is protected by divine safeguarding from addition, omission and alteration, as God promised his Prophet in it. The summary of the argument is this. God sent the Qur'an down to his Prophet and described it in many verses with particular attributes. If any of these attributes had changed through addition, omission, or a change in a word or in an order that affects it, the traces of that attribute would certainly have been affected. Yet we find that the Qur'an in our hands carries the traces of those enumerated attributes to the fullest extent possible and in the best form. So no tahrif has occurred in it that strips it of any of its attributes. What we have of it is therefore the very Qur'an that was sent down to the Prophet. If we suppose that something dropped out of it, or that a vowel ending, a letter or an order changed, then it must have been in a matter that affects none of its attributes. Those attributes include its inimitability, the absence of discrepancy in it, its guidance, its luminosity, its being a reminder, and its authority over the other heavenly books, and so on. An example is a repeated verse that dropped out, or a difference in a dot or a vowel ending, and the like.

Al-Tabataba'i reasons from the Qur'an's attributes to its text. God described the Qur'an as inimitable, free of discrepancy, guiding and luminous. If addition, omission or a change of wording or order had altered those attributes, their traces would show the change. The Qur'an in hand carries those traces in full, so he concludes it is the Qur'an sent down. A dropped repeated verse, or a difference in a dot or a vowel, would leave the attributes intact. He says any loss, if one supposes it, would have to be of that kind.
Reports in al-Kafi

Source: al-Kulayni, al-Kafi, vol.2, p.634, no.28, the last report of Kitab Fadl al-Qur'an; al-Kafi is cited throughout by the printed pages of the Dar al-Kutub al-Islamiyya edition Speaker: Imam al-Sadiq ﵇, through Hisham ibn Salim Dating: compiled by al-Kulayni (d.329 AH) Claim: the Qur'an Jibril brought to Muhammad ﷺ was seventeen thousand verses
The report's seventeen thousand verses exceed the verse count of the Qur'an in hand.

Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.2, p.634, no.28 28 - علي بن الحكم ، عن هشام بن سالم (2) ، عن أبي عبد الله (﵇) قال : إن القرآن الذي جاء به جبرئيل (﵇) إلى محمد (﵌) سبعة عشر ألف آية (3) . 28. Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abd Allah, who said. “The Qur'an that Gabriel brought to Muhammad was seventeen thousand verses.”
Al-Saduq gives the same figure and assigns the excess to revelation that is not Qur'an.

al-Saduq, al-I'tiqadat, pp.86-87 بل نقول : إنه قد نزل الوحي الذي ليس بقرآن ، ما لو جمع إلى القرآن لكان مبلغه مقدار سبعة عشر ألف آية . We say, moreover, that revelation has come down that is not Qur'an, and that if it were gathered together with the Qur'an, its total would amount to seventeen thousand verses.

Source: al-Majlisi, Mir'at al-Uqul, quoted with a reply in al-Milani, al-Tahqiq fi Nafy al-Tahrif, pp.86-88 Speaker: al-Allama al-Majlisi (d.1110 AH), answered by Sayyid Ali al-Milani Claim: this report and many sound reports state loss, and their meaning is mutawatir

al-Majlisi in al-Milani, al-Tahqiq fi Nafy al-Tahrif, pp.86-88 2 - الشيخ المجلسي في كتابه ( مرآة العقول ) فإنّه قال بعد حديث قال إنّه موثق : « ولا يخفى أنّ هذا الخبر وكثير من الأخبار الصحيحة صريحة في نقص القرآن وتغييره . وعندي أنّ الأخبار في هذا الباب متواترة معنىً ، وطرح جميعها يوجب رفع الاعتماد على الأخبار رأساً ، بل ظنّي أنّ الأخبار في هذا الباب لا تقصر عن أخبار الإمامة ، فكيف يثبتونها بالخبر » . ويردّه ما ذكره هو في « بحار الأنوار » وقد تقدّم نصّة . على أنّ قوله : « وكثير من الأخبار الصحيحة صريحة في نقص القرآن » غريب ، فإنّ السيد المرتضى قال : « نقلوا أخباراً ضعيفة ظنّوا صحتها لا يرجع بمثلها عن المعلوم المقطوع على صحته » . كما أنكر صحتها الطوسي شيخ الطائفة والمحدّث الكاشاني ، بل جاء في العبارة التي نقلناها عن بحاره « إنّ الأخبار التي جاءت بذلك أخبار آحاد لا يقطع على الله تعالى بصحّتها » . ومن قبلهم قال شيخ المحدّثين ما نصّه : « إعتقادنا أنّ القرآن الذين أنزله الله على نبيّه ﵌ هو ما بين الدفّتين وما في أيدي الناس ، ليس بأكثر من ذاك . . . ومن نسب إلينا أنّا نقول إنّه أكثر من ذلك فهو كاذب » . ولو كانت أحاديث النقيصة صحيحة ومقبولة لما قال الصدوق ذلك كما لا يخفى . وأما قوله : « وطرح جميعها يوجب رفع الاعتماد على الأخبار رأساً » ففيه : إنّ قبول جميعها أيضاً يوجب رفع الاعتماد على الأحاديث رأساً ، على أنّه رحمة الله قد حكم في أكثر الأحاديث المخرّجة في « الكافي » والمفيدة نقص القرآن إمّا بالضعف وإمّا بالإرسال ، كما تقدّم ذلك كلّه . ومن العجيب قوله : « بل ظنّي . . . » إذ إثبات الإمامية ليس دليلة منحصراً بالأحاديث حتى يقال ذلك ، وكيف أنّ تلك الأحاديث لا تقصر عن أحاديث الإمامة ؟ وهل يقصد الكثرة في الورود ؟ أو القوة في الدلالة ؟ أو الصحة في الأسانيد ؟ 2. Al-Shaykh al-Majlisi, in his book Mir'at al-'Uqul, said after a hadith that he called reliable, "It is not hidden that this report and many sound reports are explicit about the diminution and alteration of the Quran. In my view the reports on this subject are mutawatir in meaning, and rejecting all of them would remove reliance on reports altogether. Rather, I think the reports on this subject fall no shorter than the reports on the Imamate, so how can they establish the Imamate by a report?" What he himself mentioned in Bihar al-Anwar refutes this, and its text has already been given. Moreover, his statement "many sound reports are explicit about the diminution of the Quran" is strange, because al-Sayyid al-Murtada said, "They transmitted weak reports that they thought were sound, and one does not turn away from what is known and certain to be sound because of the like of these." Al-Tusi, the Shaykh of the sect, and the hadith scholar al-Kashani likewise denied their soundness. Indeed, the passage we quoted from his Bihar says, "The reports that came about this are solitary reports (ahad), and their soundness cannot be affirmed with certainty about God Most High." Before them, the Shaykh of the hadith scholars said, in these words, "Our belief is that the Quran which God sent down to His Prophet is what is between the two covers and in the hands of the people, and it is no more than that... Whoever attributes to us that we say it is more than that is a liar." Had the hadiths of diminution been sound and accepted, al-Saduq would not have said this, as is clear. As for his statement "rejecting all of them would remove reliance on reports altogether," the reply is that accepting all of them would also remove reliance on hadiths altogether. Moreover, may God have mercy on him, he judged most of the hadiths cited in al-Kafi that indicate diminution of the Quran to be either weak or mursal, as all of that has been shown earlier. His statement "Rather, I think..." is also remarkable, since the proof of the Imamate is not confined to hadiths, so that this could be said. And how do those hadiths fall no shorter than the hadiths of the Imamate? Does he mean abundance in transmission, strength in indication, or soundness in the chains of transmission?

Al-Milani quotes al-Majlisi's comment on a report that al-Majlisi graded muwaththaq, reliable through trustworthy narrators who include non-Imamis. Al-Majlisi then calls the reports of loss mutawatir in meaning. Mutawatir means reported by so many routes that the shared meaning is certain. He judges them at least equal to the reports on the imamate.

Al-Milani answers that al-Majlisi's Bihar al-Anwar calls such reports solitary. He cites al-Murtada, al-Tusi, al-Fayd and al-Saduq against the claim of soundness. He adds that al-Majlisi graded most of the al-Kafi reports of loss weak or mursal. A mursal report has a gap in its chain. Al-Milani asks whether that equality refers to number, strength of meaning or soundness of chains.
Source: al-Kafi, vol.2, p.633, no.23 Speaker: Imam al-Sadiq ﵇, through Salim ibn Salama Claim: a man is told to stop a non-standard reading and to recite as the people recite until al-Qa'im rises

Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.2, p.633, no.23 23 - محمد بن يحيى ، عن محمد بن الحسين ، عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي هاشم ، عن سالم بن سلمة قال : قرأ رجل على أبي عبد الله (﵇) وأنا أستمع حروفا من القرآن ليس على ما يقرؤها الناس ، فقال أبو عبد الله (﵇) : كف عن هذه القراءة اقرأ كما يقرأ الناس حتى يقوم القائم فإذا قام القائم (﵇) قرأ كتاب الله ﷿ على حده وأخرج المصحف الذي كتبه علي (﵇) وقال : أخرجه علي (﵇) إلى الناس حين فرغ منه وكتبه فقال لهم : هذا كتاب الله ﷿ كما أنزله [الله] على محمد (﵌) وقد جمعته من اللوحين فقالوا : هو ذا عندنا مصحف جامع فيه القرآن لا حاجة لنا فيه ، فقال أما والله ما ترونه بعد يومكم هذا أبدا ، إنما كان علي أن أخبركم حين جمعته لتقرؤوه . 23. Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Salim ibn Salama, who said. A man recited to Abu Abd Allah, while I was listening, some letters of the Qur'an that were not as the people recite them. Abu Abd Allah said, “Stop this recitation. Recite as the people recite until the Qa'im rises. When the Qa'im rises, he will recite the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, by itself, and he will bring out the codex that Ali wrote.” And he said, “Ali brought it out to the people when he had finished it and written it. He said to them, ‘This is the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, as [God] sent it down to Muhammad, and I have gathered it from the two tablets.’ They said, ‘Here with us is a codex that contains the whole Qur'an, and we have no need of it.’ He said, ‘By God, you will never see it after this day of yours. It was only my duty to inform you, when I had gathered it, so that you would recite it.’”

Imam al-Sadiq ﵇ stops the man's reading and tells him to recite as the people recite. The instruction holds until al-Qa'im, the Riser from the Prophet's ﷺ house, rises. The Imam ﵇ says al-Qa'im will bring out the codex Ali ﵇ wrote. He recounts that Ali ﵇ offered that codex as the Book sent down to Muhammad ﷺ. The people answered that their own codex held the whole Qur'an. The report sets Ali's ﵇ codex apart from the circulating copy, and it does not say how the two differed.
Source: al-Kafi, vol.1, p.228, no.1 Speaker: Imam al-Baqir ﵇, through Jabir Claim: whoever claims to have gathered the whole Qur'an as it was revealed is a liar, except Ali ﵇ and the Imams after him

Imam al-Baqir, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.228, no.1 (باب) (انه لم يجمع القرآن كله الا الأئمة ﵈ وانهم) (يعلمون علمه كله) 1 - محمد بن يحيى ، عن أحمد بن محمد ، عن ابن محبوب ، عن عمرو بن أبي المقدام عن جابر قال : سمعت أبا جعفر ﵇ يقول : ما ادعى أحد من الناس أنه جمع القرآن كله كما أنزل إلا كذاب ، وما جمعه وحفظه كما نزله الله تعالى إلا علي بن أبي طالب ﵇ والأئمة من بعده ﵈ . Chapter. That no one collected the whole Quran except the Imams, and that they know all of its knowledge. 1 - Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Jabir, who said that he heard Abu Ja'far say, “No one among the people claims that he collected the whole Quran as it was sent down, except a liar. No one collected it and memorized it as God Most High sent it down except Ali ibn Abi Talib and the Imams after him.”

The chapter heading says that only the Imams gathered the whole Qur'an and that "they know all of its knowledge". Jabir's report says Ali ﵇ and the Imams after him gathered and memorized it "as God Most High sent it down". The report gives no account of what the people's copy lacked.

Source: al-Kafi, vol.1, p.417, no.26, in the chapter of points and fragments from the tanzil on wilaya, vol.1, pp.412-436 Speaker: Jabir, by the chain of the preceding report in that chapter Claim: Jibril brought Qur'an 2:23 with words about Ali ﵇

Jabir, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.417, no.26 26 - وبهذا الاسناد ، عن محمد بن سنان ، عن عمار بن مروان ، عن منخل ، عن جابر ، قال : نزل جبرئيل ﵇ بهذه الآية على محمد هكذا : " وإن كنتم في ريب مما نزلنا على عبدنا (في علي) فأتوا بسورة من مثله (3) " . 26 - Through this same chain, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Munakhkhal, from Jabir, who said, Gabriel came down to Muhammad with this verse in this form, “If you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant (concerning Ali), then bring a surah like it.”

Reports of this form add a name to a verse and say Jibril brought the verse "in this form". Al-Kulayni gathered them in a chapter on wilaya, the authority of the Imams. Al-Tabataba'i reads such wording as the explanation that accompanied the revelation, as quoted below.
