Source: al-Khoei, al-Bayan, p.226; al-Muhammadi, Salamat al-Qur'an min al-Tahrif, p.120; al-Khoei, Mu'jam Rijal al-Hadith, vol.3, p.71 Speaker: al-Khoei; Fath Allah al-Muhammadi; al-Najashi, quoted by al-Khoei Claim: many such reports have weak chains, a large share come from al-Sayyari, and some come by reliable routes

al-Khoei, al-Bayan, p.226 والجواب : أن هذه الروايات لا دلالة فيها على وقوع التحريف في القرآن بالمعنى المتنازع فيه ، وتوضيح ذلك : أن كثيرا من الروايات ، وإن كانت ضعيفة السند ، فإن جملة منها نقلت من كتاب أحمد بن محمد السياري ، الذي اتفق علماء الرجال على فساد مذهبه ، وأنه يقول بالتناسخ ، ومن علي بن أحمد الكوفي الذي ذكر علماء الرجال أنه كذاب ، وأنه فاسد المذهب إلا أن كثرة الروايات تورث القطع بصدور بعضها عن المعصومين ﵈ ولا أقل من الاطمئنان بذلك ، وفيها ما روي بطريق معتبر فلا حاجة بنا إلى التكلم في سند كل رواية بخصوصها . The answer is that these reports give no indication that distortion occurred in the Quran in the sense under dispute. To explain this, many of the reports have weak chains of transmission. A number of them were transmitted from the book of Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Sayyari, whose doctrine the scholars of biographical evaluation agreed was corrupt, and who held the belief in transmigration of souls. Others were transmitted from Ali ibn Ahmad al-Kufi, whom the scholars of biographical evaluation described as a liar with a corrupt doctrine. Nevertheless, the large number of reports produces certainty that some of them were issued by the infallible Imams, and at the very least it produces confidence in that. Among them are reports narrated through a reliable route. So we have no need to discuss the chain of each report individually.

al-Muhammadi, Salamat al-Qur'an min al-Tahrif, p.120 لأن مجموع الروايات التي نقلها المحدث النوري - ويزعم أنها اختصت بكتب الإمامية - يصل إلى 1602 رواية موزعة على النحو الآتي : * 350 رواية ( يعنى حدود ثلث الروايات التي جمعها ) من كتاب القراءات لأحمد بن محمد السياري ، وهذا الكتاب لا قيمة له عند الإمامية ومؤلفه ضعيف الحديث عند الفريقين (2) . The total of the reports that the hadith scholar al-Nuri transmitted, which he claims are particular to the books of the Imamis, reaches 1602 reports, distributed as follows. There are 350 reports, meaning about a third of the reports he collected, from the Book of Recitations by Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Sayyari. This book has no value among the Imamis, and its author is weak in hadith according to both groups.

al-Najashi in al-Khoei, Mu'jam Rijal al-Hadith, vol.3, p.71 874 - أحمد بن محمد بن سيار : = أحمد بن محمد البصري . = أحمد بن محمد السياري . قال النجاشي : " أحمد بن محمد بن سيار أبو عبد الله الكاتب بصري ، كان من كتاب آل طاهر ، في زمن أبي محمد ﵇ ، ويعرف بالسياري ، ضعيف الحديث ، فاسد المذهب - ذكر ذلك لنا : الحسين بن عبيد الله - مجفو الرواية ، كثير المراسيل ، له كتب ، وقع إلينا منها : كتاب ثواب القرآن ، كتاب الطب ، كتاب القراءات ، كتاب النوادر ، كتاب الغارات ، أخبرنا الحسين بن عبيد الله ، قال : حدثنا أحمد بن محمد بن يحيى ، عن أبيه ، قال : حدثني السياري ، إلا ما كان من غلو وتخليط " . 874. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar, who is also Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Basri and Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Sayyari. Al-Najashi said, "Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar, Abu Abd Allah the scribe, was from Basra. He was one of the secretaries of the Al Tahir in the time of Abu Muhammad, and he is known as al-Sayyari. He is weak in hadith and corrupt in doctrine, as al-Husayn ibn Ubayd Allah told us. His transmission is shunned, and he has many mursal reports. He has books, of which these reached us. The Book of the Reward of the Quran, the Book of Medicine, the Book of Recitations, the Book of Rare Reports, and the Book of the Raids. Al-Husayn ibn Ubayd Allah informed us and said, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us from his father, who said, al-Sayyari narrated to me, except for what contained exaggeration (ghuluw) and confusion."

Al-Khoei says many reports of tahrif have weak chains. He traces a number of them to the book of Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Sayyari and others to Ali ibn Ahmad al-Kufi. Al-Najashi calls al-Sayyari weak in hadith and corrupt in doctrine, with many mursal reports. Al-Muhammadi counts 350 of the 1,602 reports gathered by the hadith scholar al-Nuri as coming from al-Sayyari's Book of Recitations. Al-Khoei grants that the number of reports makes it certain that some came from the Imams ﵈. He holds that none of them indicates tahrif in the disputed sense, the loss of text.
How the School Weighs a Solitary Report

Source: al-Tusi, al-Tibyan fi Tafsir al-Qur'an, vol.1, p.77 Speaker: Shaykh al-Ta'ifa al-Tusi (d.460 AH) Claim: reports of loss are solitary, yield neither knowledge nor grounds for action, and are best set aside

al-Tusi, al-Tibyan, vol.1, p.77 وأما الكلام في زيادته ونقصانه فمما لا يليق به أيضا ، لان الزيادة فيه مجمع على بطلانها والنقصان منه ، فالظاهر أيضا من مذهب المسلمين خلافه ، وهو الأليق بالصحيح من مذهبنا وهو الذي نصره المرتضى (ره) ، وهو الظاهر في الروايات غير أنه رويت روايات كثيره ، من جهة الخاصة والعامة ، بنقصان كثير من آي القرآن ، ونقل شئ منه من موضع إلى موضع ، طريقها الآحاد التي لا توجب علما ولا عملا ، والأولى الاعراض عنها ، وترك التشاغل بها ، لأنه يمكن تأويلها ولو صحت لما كان ذلك طعنا على ما هو موجود بين الدفتين ، فان ذلك معلوم صحته ، لا يعترضه أحد من الأمة ولا يدفعه ورواياتنا متناصرة بالحث على قراءته والتمسك بما فيه ، ورد ما يرد من اختلاف الاخبار في الفروع إليه . The discussion of the Quran's increase and decrease is also unsuitable here. Increase in it is unanimously held to be invalid. As for decrease from it, the apparent position of the Muslims is the opposite. That is also the view more fitting for the sound position of our school, and it is the view that al-Murtada, may God have mercy on him, supported, and it is the apparent meaning of the reports. Nevertheless, many reports have been narrated, from our own side (al-khassa) and from the general body of Muslims (al-'amma), that many verses of the Quran were diminished and that some of it was moved from one place to another. These reports come by solitary chains (ahad), which establish neither knowledge nor practice. It is better to turn away from them and to leave off occupying oneself with them, because they can be interpreted. Even if they were sound, that would not be a criticism of what exists between the two covers, because the soundness of that is known, no one in the community objects to it, and no one rejects it. Our reports agree in urging its recitation and holding fast to what is in it, and in referring back to it whatever differences arise among the reports on matters of detail.

Al-Tusi calls addition invalid by consensus. He calls the denial of loss the apparent position of Muslims and the view more fitting for the sound position of his school. He grants that narrators of his school and of the general body of Muslims transmit many reports of loss and of moved verses. He classes them as solitary reports, which yield neither certain knowledge nor grounds for action. He adds that even a sound report of this kind would not challenge the text between the covers.

Source: al-Kafi, vol.1, p.69, no.5; al-Hurr al-Amili, Wasa'il al-Shi'a, vol.27, p.118, no.33362 Speaker: Imam al-Sadiq ﵇, quoting the Prophet ﷺ; and Imam al-Sadiq ﵇, through Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abd Allah Claim: a report that contradicts the Book of God is rejected

Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.69, no.5 5 - محمد بن إسماعيل ، عن الفضل بن شاذان ، عن ابن أبي عمير ، عن هشام بن الحكم وغيره ، عن أبي عبد الله ﵇ قال : خطب النبي ﵌ بمنى فقال : أيها الناس ما جاء كم عني يوافق كتاب الله فأنا قلته وما جاء كم يخالف كتاب الله فلم أقله . 5 - Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam and others, from Abu Abd Allah, who said, The Prophet gave a sermon at Mina and said, “O people, whatever comes to you from me that agrees with the Book of God, I said it. Whatever comes to you that contradicts the Book of God, I did not say it.”

Imam al-Sadiq, Wasa'il al-Shi'a, vol.27, p.118, no.33362 (33362) 29 - سعيد بن هبة الله الراوندي في (رسالته) التي ألفها في أحوال أحاديث أصحابنا وإثبات صحتها ، عن محمد ، وعلي ابني علي بن عبد الصمد ، عن أبيهما ، عن أبي البركات علي بن الحسين ، عن أبي جعفر ابن بابويه ، عن أبيه ، عن سعد بن عبد الله عن أيوب بن نوح ، عن محمد ابن أبي عمير ، عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي عبد الله قال : قال الصادق (﵇) : إذا ورد عليكم حديثان مختلفان فاعرضوهما على كتاب الله ، فما وافق كتاب الله فخذوه ، وما خالف كتاب الله فردوه ، فإن لم تجدوهما في كتاب الله فاعرضوهما على أخبار العامة ، فما وافق أخبارهم فذروه ، وما خالف أخبراهم فخذوه . (33362) 29. Sa'id ibn Hibat Allah al-Rawandi, in his treatise that he wrote on the conditions of the hadiths of our companions and the proof of their soundness, from Muhammad and Ali, the two sons of Ali ibn Abd al-Samad, from their father, from Abu al-Barakat Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Ja'far ibn Babawayh, from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abd Allah, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abd Allah, who said. Al-Sadiq said, "When two differing hadiths reach you, present them to the Book of God. Take what agrees with the Book of God and reject what contradicts the Book of God. If you do not find them in the Book of God, present them to the reports of the general body of Muslims (al-'amma). Leave what agrees with their reports, and take what contradicts their reports."

The Mina sermon makes the Book the test for any report from the Prophet ﷺ. The Wasa'il report makes it the test between two differing hadiths. A report that the Book was altered contradicts that Book, so it fails the test. Al-Fayd al-Kashani applies this rule to the reports of alteration in al-Safi, quoted in the section on the scholars of the school.

Source: al-Kafi, vol.2, pp.630-631, nos.12, 13 and 15 Speaker: Imam al-Baqir ﵇ and Imam al-Sadiq ﵇ Claim: the Qur'an is one, sent down by One, and differences come from the narrators; recite as you were taught

Imam al-Baqir, al-Kafi, vol.2, p.630, no.12 12 - الحسين بن محمد ، عن علي بن محمد ، عن الوشاء ، عن جميل بن دراج ، عن محمد بن مسلم ، عن زرارة ، عن أبي جعفر (﵇) قال : إن القرآن واحد نزل من عند واحد ولكن الاختلاف يجيئ من قبل الرواة . 12 - al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far, who said, “The Quran is one, sent down from One. But the disagreement comes from the side of the transmitters.”

Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.2, p.630, no.13 13 - علي بن إبراهيم ، عن أبيه ، عن ابن أبي عمير ، عن عمر بن أذينة ، عن الفضيل بن يسار قال : قلت لأبي عبد الله (﵇) : إن الناس يقولون : إن القرآن نزل على سبعة أحرف ، فقال : كذبوا أعداء الله ولكنه نزل على حرف واحد من عند الواحد (1) . 13 - Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said, I said to Abu Abd Allah, “The people say that the Quran was sent down in seven ahruf.” He said, “The enemies of God have lied. Rather, it was sent down in one harf, from the One.”

Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.2, p.631, no.15 15 - عدة من أصحابنا ، عن سهل بن زياد ، عن علي بن الحكم ، ، عن عبد الله ابن جندب ، عن سفيان بن السمط قال : سألت أبا عبد الله (﵇) : عن تنزيل القرآن قال : اقرؤوا كما علمتم . 15 - A group of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abd Allah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Samt, who said, I asked Abu Abd Allah about the sending down of the Quran. He said, “Recite as you were taught.”

Imam al-Baqir ﵇ says the Qur'an is one and the disagreement comes from the transmitters. Imam al-Sadiq ﵇ denies that the Qur'an came down in seven ahruf, modes of reading, and says it came down in one. Asked about the Qur'an's revelation, he answers, "Recite as you were taught."
Source: Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, al-Musnad, vol.8, p.470, no.5057 Speaker: Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ Claim: two men taught different readings are told to recite as they were taught
Sunni books report the same words from the Prophet ﷺ.

Ibn Mas'ud, Musnad Abi Ya'la, vol.8, p.470, no.5057 (5057) حدثنا أبو كريب حدثنا أبو بكر بن عياش عن عاصم عن زر عن عبد الله قال اختصم رجلان في سورة فقال هذا أقرأني رسول الله ﵌ وقال هذا أقرأني رسول الله فأتيا النبي ﵌ فأخبر بذلك قال فتغير وجهه فقال إقرؤوا كما علمتم فذكر فيه كلاما ثم قال فإنما هلك من كان قبلكم باختلافهم على أنبيائهم (5057) Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Asim, from Zirr, from Abd Allah, who said, Two men disputed over a surah. One said, “The Messenger of God taught me to recite it,” and the other said, “The Messenger of God taught me to recite it.” They came to the Prophet and he was told of this. He said that his face changed, and he said, “Recite as you were taught.” Then he mentioned some words about it, and then said, “Those before you were destroyed only because of their disagreement with their prophets.”

In Ibn Mas'ud's report, two men each say the Prophet ﷺ taught them a sura. The Prophet ﷺ tells both to recite as they were taught. Each man keeps the reading he was taught. In Salim's report, the Imam ﵇ tells the man to recite as the people recite until al-Qa'im rises. The Prophet's ﷺ instruction leaves two readings in place, and the Imam's ﵇ instruction names one, the people's reading.
Source: al-Tabataba'i, al-Mizan, vol.12, p.108 Speaker: al-Tabataba'i Claim: the Imams ﵈ argued from the Qur'an as it stands, and "it was revealed thus" means explanation

al-Tabataba'i, al-Mizan, vol.12, p.108 وكذا الاخبار التي تتضمن تمسك أئمة أهل البيت ﵈ بمختلف الآيات القرآنية في كل باب على ما يوافق القرآن الموجود عندنا حتى في الموارد التي فيها آحاد من الروايات بالتحريف وهذا أحسن شاهد على أن المراد في كثير من روايات التحريف من قولهم ﵈ كذا نزل هو التفسير بحسب التنزيل في مقابل البطن والتأويل . وكذا الروايات الواردة عن أمير المؤمنين وسائر الأئمة من ذريته ﵈ في إن ما بأيدي الناس قرآن نازل من عند الله سبحانه وان كان غير ما الفه علي ﵇ من المصحف ولم يشركوه ﵇ في التأليف في زمن أبى بكر ولا في زمن عثمان ومن هذا الباب قولهم ﵈ لشيعتهم : اقرؤوا كما قرء الناس ومقتضى هذه الروايات ان لو كان القرآن الدائر بين الناس مخالفا لما الفه علي ﵇ في شئ فإنما يخالفه في ترتيب السور أو في ترتيب بعض الآيات التي لا يؤثر اختلال ترتيبها في مدلولها شيئا ولا في الأوصاف التي وصف الله سبحانه بها القرآن النازل من عنده ما يختل به آثارها . فمجموع هذه الروايات على اختلاف أصنافها يدل دلالة قاطعة على أن الذي بأيدينا من القرآن هو القرآن النازل على النبي ﵌ من غير أن يفقد شيئا من أوصافه الكريمة وآثارها وبركاتها . Likewise there are the reports that include the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt holding to various Qur'anic verses on every subject, in agreement with the Qur'an we have, even in the cases where there are isolated reports of alteration. This is the best evidence that what is meant in many of the alteration reports, in their saying "It was revealed thus," is explanation according to the revelation, as distinct from the inner meaning and the interpretation. Likewise there are the reports from the Commander of the Faithful and the rest of the Imams from his descendants, saying that what is in the people's hands is a Qur'an sent down from God, Glorified, even though it differs from the codex that Ali compiled, and that they did not involve him in the compilation, either in the time of Abu Bakr or in the time of Uthman. To this category belongs their saying to their Shia, "Recite as the people recite." The implication of these reports is that if the Qur'an circulating among the people differs in anything from what Ali compiled, it differs only in the order of the surahs, or in the order of some verses whose disordering has no effect on their meaning. It does not differ in the attributes with which God, Glorified, described the Qur'an sent down from Him, so as to impair their effects. So these reports taken together, despite their different kinds, indicate conclusively that the Qur'an in our hands is the Qur'an sent down upon the Prophet, without having lost any of its noble attributes, its effects, or its blessings.

Al-Tabataba'i draws on three groups of reports. In the first, the Imams ﵈ cite verses on every subject in agreement with the Qur'an in hand. He takes this to show that "it was revealed thus" in many reports means the explanation that came with revelation. In the second, the Imams ﵈ call the people's Qur'an revealed by God, although it differs from Ali's ﵇ codex. The third is their instruction to recite as the people recite. He concludes that any difference from Ali's ﵇ codex lies only in the order of the suras or of some verses, whose reordering leaves the meaning unchanged.
Hammad's Report on Qur'an 5:95
Verse: Qur'an 5:95 Claim: two just men among you judge the equivalent of game killed in the state of ihram

Qur'an 5:95 يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَقْتُلُوا۟ ٱلصَّيْدَ وَأَنتُمْ حُرُمٌۭ ۚ وَمَن قَتَلَهُۥ مِنكُم مُّتَعَمِّدًۭا فَجَزَآءٌۭ مِّثْلُ مَا قَتَلَ مِنَ ٱلنَّعَمِ يَحْكُمُ بِهِۦ ذَوَا عَدْلٍۢ مِّنكُمْ هَدْيًۢا بَٰلِغَ ٱلْكَعْبَةِ أَوْ كَفَّٰرَةٌۭ طَعَامُ مَسَٰكِينَ أَوْ عَدْلُ ذَٰلِكَ صِيَامًۭا لِّيَذُوقَ وَبَالَ أَمْرِهِۦ ۗ عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَمَّا سَلَفَ ۚ وَمَنْ عَادَ فَيَنتَقِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِنْهُ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌۭ ذُو ٱنتِقَامٍ ya ayyuha alladhina amanu la taqtulu al-sayda wa-antum hurumun, wa-man qatalahu minkum muta'ammidan fa-jaza'un mithlu ma qatala mina al-na'ami yahkumu bihi dhawa 'adlin minkum hadyan baligha al-ka'bati aw kaffaratun ta'amu masakina aw 'adlu dhalika siyaman li-yadhuqa wabala amrihi, 'afa Allahu 'amma salaf, wa-man 'ada fa-yantaqimu Allahu minhu, wa-Allahu 'azizun dhu intiqam O you who believe, do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram. Whoever of you kills it intentionally, the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from the livestock, as two men of justice among you judge, as an offering reaching the Kaaba; or an expiation by feeding poor people; or the equivalent of that in fasting, so that he may taste the consequence of his deed. God has pardoned what is past. But whoever returns, God will take retribution from him. And God is Almighty, Lord of retribution.

Source: al-Kafi, vol.8, p.205, no.247, in al-Rawda Speaker: Imam al-Sadiq ﵇, through Hammad ibn Uthman Claim: the dual dhawa 'adl, "two just men", is "among the things in which the kuttab erred", and the reading is dhu 'adl, "one just man"

Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.8, p.205, no.247 247 - علي بن إبراهيم ، عن أبيه ، عن ابن أبي عمير ، عن حماد بن عثمان قال : تلوت عند أبي عبد الله (﵇) " ذوا عدل منكم (2) " فقال " ذو عدل منكم " هذا مما أخطأت فيه الكتاب . 247. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said. I recited in the presence of Abu Abd Allah, "two just men from among you." He said, "'A just man from among you.' This is one of the things the scribes got wrong."
Hammad recites the dual, and the Imam ﵇ answers with the singular and attributes the dual to the kuttab. The report concerns one letter, the alif that makes "one just man" into "two just men".

al-Tabrisi, Majma' al-Bayan, vol.3, p.416 وروي في الشواذ قراءة أبي عبد الرحمن (فجزاء) منون (مثل) منصوب . وقراءة محمد بن علي الباقر ﵇ وجعفر بن محمد الصادق ﵇ : " يحكم به ذو عدل منكم " . Among the irregular readings, there is reported the reading of Abu Abd al-Rahman, who read “penalty” with tanwin and “equivalent” in the accusative. There is also the reading of Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir and Jafar ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq, “A man of justice among you judges by it.”
Al-Tabrisi records the singular as the reading of al-Baqir ﵇ and al-Sadiq ﵇. He lists it among the shawadhdh, readings reported outside the accepted readings.

Imam al-Baqir, Tafsir al-Ayyashi, vol.1, p.351, no.200 200 - عن زرارة قال : سمعت أبا جعفر ﵇ يقول : " يحكم به ذوا عدل منكم " قال : ذلك رسول الله ﵌ والامام من بعده ، فإذا حكم به الامام فحسبك 200 - From Zurara, who said, I heard Abu Jafar say, “Two men of justice among you judge by it.” He said, “That is the Messenger of God and the Imam after him. When the Imam has judged by it, that is enough for you.”
In Zurara's report Imam al-Baqir ﵇ recites the dual. He names the two just men as the Messenger ﷺ and the Imam after him. Al-Tabrisi and Zurara therefore differ on what al-Baqir ﵇ recited.

al-Mazandarani, Sharh Furu' al-Kafi, vol.5, p.199 ونسبة الخطأ إليهم لتعميمهم العدلين . هذا هو المشهور في تفسير هذا الكلام ، والأظهر أنّ المراد بالكتّاب نُسّاخ القرآن ، يعني أنّ المنزل كان ذو عدل بلفظ المفرد ، والتثنية من غلطهم . The attribution of error to them is because they made the “two men of justice” general. This is the well-known view in the interpretation of this statement. The clearer view is that what is meant by the “scribes” is the copyists of the Qur’an. That is, what was revealed was “a man of justice” in the singular form, and the dual form comes from their mistake.

al-Tabataba'i, Tafsir al-Bayan fi al-Muwafaqa bayn al-Hadith wa al-Qur'an, vol.3, p.336 أقول : لفظ الكتّاب بضم الكاف وتشديد التاء المنقوطة ، جمع كاتب يريدان ﵉ كتّاب المصحف I say, the word al-kuttab, with a damma on the kaf and a doubled dotted ta, is the plural of katib (scribe). The two Imams, al-Baqir and al-Sadiq, mean the scribes of the codex (mushaf).

al-Fayd al-Kashani, al-Wafi, vol.26, p.422 بيان : لعل المراد أنه أريد بذي العدل في الآية الإمام المعصوم ، وقد مضى في كتاب الحج . Explanation. Perhaps what is meant is that the “man of justice” in the verse refers to the infallible Imam. This has already been covered in the Book of Pilgrimage.

al-Gulpaygani, Taqrirat al-Hajj, vol.3, p.43 هذا مما أخطأت به الكتاب (1) . أقول : قوله ﵇ وكذا قول الباقر ﵇ : هذا مما أخطأت به الكتاب المراد من ذلك أن الألف في قوله تعالى " ذوا عدل " زيادة ، قد زاد الكتاب فيه خطأ والصحيح أنه ذو عدل بدون الألف والمراد بذي العدل هو النبي ﵆ أو الإمام الذي بعده . ولكن عن تفسير العياشي عن زرارة قال : سمعت أبا جعفر يقول : " يحكم به ذوا عدل منكم " قال : ذلك رسول الله ﵌ والإمام من بعده ، فإذا حكم به الإمام فحسبك (2) . فيظهر من الرواية أن التثنية في ذوا عدل صحيحة والمراد منهما السول والإمام صلوات الله عليهما وعلى آلهما “This is one of the things in which the scribes made mistakes.” I say that his statement, and likewise the statement of al-Baqir, “This is one of the things in which the scribes made mistakes,” means that the alif in the words of the Most High, “two men of justice,” is an addition. The scribes added it by mistake, and the correct form is “a man of justice” without the alif. The “man of justice” means the Prophet, or the Imam after him. But it is reported in the Tafsir of al-Ayyashi, from Zurara, who said, “I heard Abu Jafar say, ‘Two men of justice among you judge by it.’ He said, ‘That is the Messenger of God and the Imam after him. When the Imam has judged by it, that is enough for you.’” It appears from this report that the dual in “two men of justice” is correct, and that what is meant by the two is the Messenger and the Imam, may God’s blessings be upon them both and upon their family.

On the common reading that al-Mazandarani reports, the kuttab erred by giving "two just men" a general application. Al-Mazandarani prefers a second reading, in which the kuttab were copyists and the revealed word was singular. Al-Tabataba'i also takes the kuttab to be the scribes of the codex. Al-Fayd suggests that the one just man is the infallible Imam. Al-Gulpaygani first reads the alif as a scribe's addition. He then judges the dual correct on the strength of Zurara's report. On the copyist reading, the report alleges a scribal error in the codex.
Parallel Reports in Sunni Books

Source: al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak ala al-Sahihayn, vol.2, p.396 Speaker: Ibn Abbas, through Mujahid Dating: al-Hakim (d.405 AH) grades it sahih on the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim Claim: the word tasta'nisu in Qur'an 24:27 is a scribe's error for tasta'dhinu

Ibn Abbas, al-Mustadrak, vol.2, p.396 (حدثنا) أبو علي الحافظ أنبأ عبدان الأهوازي ثنا عمرو بن محمد الناقد ثنا محمد بن يوسف ثنا سفيان عن شعبة عن جعفر بن اياس عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس ﵄ في قوله تعالى لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم حتى تستأنسوا قال أخطأ الكاتب حتى تستأذنوا هذا حديث صحيح على شرط الشيخين ولم يخرجاه . Abu Ali al-Hafiz narrated to us. Abdan al-Ahwazi informed us. Amr ibn Muhammad al-Naqid narrated to us. Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us. Sufyan narrated to us, from Shuba, from Jafar ibn Iyas, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, concerning the saying of the Most High, “Do not enter houses other than your own until you become at ease,” he said, “The scribe made a mistake. It is ‘until you ask permission.’” This hadith is sound by the standard of the two Shaykhs, although they did not record it.

Source: Ibn Abi Hatim, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Azim, vol.8, pp.154-155, no.14560 Speaker: Ibn Abbas, through Ata' Claim: "the likeness of His light" in Qur'an 24:35 is a scribe's error for "the light of the believer"

Ibn Abbas, Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim, vol.8, pp.154-155, no.14560 [14560] حدثنا علي بن الحسين ، ثنا نصر بن علي ، أخبرني أبي عن شبل بن عباد عن قيس بن سعد ، عن عطاء عن ابن عباس : (اللَّه نُورُ السَّماواتِ والأَرْضِ مَثَلُ ( نُورِه ) * قال : هي خطأ من الكاتب هو أعظم من أن يكون نوره مثل نور المشكاة قال : مثل نور المؤمن كمشكاة . [14560] Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us. Nasr ibn Ali narrated to us. My father informed me, from Shibl ibn Abbad, from Qays ibn Sad, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, “God is the Light of the heavens and the earth; the likeness of His light.” He said, “It is a mistake by the scribe. He is too great for His light to be like the light of a niche.” He said, “The likeness of the believer’s light is like a niche.”

Abu Shahba quotes the exegete Abu Hayyan, who calls whoever reports the 24:27 statement from Ibn Abbas a heretic. Ibn Ashtah, quoted by al-Suyuti, explains the error as a poor choice among the seven ahruf. Ma'rifat, an Imami scholar, reviews ten such reports of early scribal error. He says they must be interpreted or rejected.

Abu Shahba, al-Madkhal, p.365, quoting Abu Hayyan 1 - أن هذا القول غير صحيح في نسبته إلى ابن عباس وهو مدسوس عليه ، دسه الملاحدة والزنادقة ، قال أبو حيان ما نصه : إن من روى عن ابن عباس أنه قال ذلك فهو طاعن في الإسلام ملحد في الدين ، وابن عباس بريء من ذلك القول . 1. This statement is not correctly attributed to Ibn Abbas. It was falsely inserted into his words, and the heretics and the zindiqs inserted it. Abu Hayyan said, in these exact words, "Whoever reports from Ibn Abbas that he said this is attacking Islam and is a heretic in religion, and Ibn Abbas is innocent of that statement."

Ibn Ashtah, in al-Suyuti, al-Itqan, vol.1, p.557 وقد أجاب ابن أشتة عن هذه الآثار كلّها بأنّ المراد أخطئوا في الاختيار ، وما هو الأولى لجمع الناس عليه من الأحرف السبعة ، لا أنّ الذي كتب خطأ خارج عن القرآن . Ibn Ashtah answered all of these reports by saying that what is meant is that they made a mistake in choosing, from among the seven ahruf, the one that was best for bringing people together. He did not mean that what was written was an error lying outside the Quran.

Ma'rifat, al-Tamhid fi Ulum al-Qur'an, vol.1, p.370 أمّا نفس المحتوى وصحّة ما تضمّنته من تبديل نصّ المصحف الشريف ، فهذا شيء لا نكاد نصدّقه البتة . لأنّه هوالتحريف الذي أجمعت الأُمّة الإسلاميّة على عدم تسرّبه إلى كتاب اللّه العزيز الحميد : «إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحافِظُونَ» . (5) فلابدّ من الأخذ في تأويلها إلى وجه معقول أو رفضها رأسا . (6) As for the content itself, and the soundness of what it contains about altering the text of the noble Mushaf, this is something we can hardly ever believe. It is the very distortion that the Muslim community agreed has never seeped into the Book of God, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, "Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its guardians." (Quran 15:9) So one must either interpret these reports in some reasonable way or reject them outright.
Al-Hakim graded the 24:27 report sahih by the standard of al-Bukhari and Muslim.
The Mushaf of Fatimah

Source: Abu Mansur al-Azhari, Tahdhib al-Lugha, vol.4, p.149; Murtada al-Askari, al-Mushaf fi al-Riwayat wa al-Athar, p.10 Speaker: al-Layth, quoted by al-Azhari; al-Askari Claim: a mushaf is any bound collection of written pages
The Kafi reports speak of a Mushaf of Fatimah ﵍. The word mushaf means any bound collection of pages, as the two sources below define it.

al-Layth, in al-Azhari, Tahdhib al-Lugha, vol.4, p.149 قال : وإنما سُمِّي المُصْحَفُ مُصْحَفاً لأنه أُصْحِفَ أي جعل جامعاً للصُّحُف المكتوبة بين الدَّفَّتَيْن . He said that the mushaf is called a mushaf because it was "ushifa", meaning that it was made a collection of the written sheets between the two covers.
al-Askari, al-Mushaf fi al-Riwayat wa al-Athar, p.10 إنّ المصحف اسم لكلّ كتاب مجلد قرآناً كان أم غير قرآن . The mushaf is a name for every bound book, whether it is a Quran or not a Quran.
Al-Layth defines the mushaf as written sheets gathered between two covers. Al-Askari concludes that the word names any bound book, Qur'an or not.

Source: al-Kafi, vol.1, pp.238-240, chapter on al-Sahifa, al-Jafr, al-Jami'a and the Mushaf of Fatimah, nos.1-3 Speaker: Imam al-Sadiq ﵇, through Abu Basir, Hammad ibn Uthman and al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Ala' Claim: the Mushaf of Fatimah ﵍ holds no letter of the Qur'an

Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.239, no.1 ثم سكت ساعة ثم قال : وإن عندنا لمصحف فاطمة ﵍ وما يدريهم ما مصحف فاطمة ﵍ ؟ قال : قلت : وما مصحف فاطمة ﵍ ؟ قال : مصحف فيه مثل قرآنكم هذا ثلاث مرات ، والله ما فيه من قرآنكم حرف واحد ، قال : قلت : هذا والله العلم قال : إنه لعلم وما هو بذاك . Then he was silent for a while, and then he said, "We also have the Mushaf of Fatima. And what do they know of the Mushaf of Fatima?" He said, "I said, 'And what is the Mushaf of Fatima?'" He said, "It is a mushaf containing three times the like of this Quran of yours. By God, there is not a single letter of your Quran in it." He said, "I said, 'This, by God, is knowledge.'" He said, "It is knowledge, but it is not that."

Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.240, no.2 2 - عدة من أصحابنا ، عن أحمد بن محمد ، عن عمر بن عبد العزيز ، عن حماد بن عثمان قال : سمعت أبا عبد الله ﵇ يقول : تظهر الزنادقة في سنة ثمان وعشرين ومائة وذلك أني نظرت في مصحف فاطمة ﵍ ، قال : قلت : وما مصحف فاطمة ؟ قال : إن الله تعالى لما قبض نبيه ﵌ دخل على فاطمة ﵍ من وفاته من الحزن ما لا يعلمه إلا الله ﷿ فأرسل الله إليها ملكا يسلي غمها ويحدثها ، فشكت ذلك (1) إلى أمير المؤمنين ﵇ فقال : إذا أحسست بذلك وسمعت الصوت قولي لي فأعلمته بذلك فجعل أمير المؤمنين ﵇ يكتب كلما سمع حتى أثبت من ذلك مصحفا قال : ثم قال : أما إنه ليس فيه شئ من الحلال والحرام ولكن فيه علم ما يكون . 2. A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said that he heard Abu Abd Allah say, "The heretics will appear in the year one hundred and twenty-eight, and that is because I looked in the Mushaf of Fatima." He said, "I said, 'And what is the Mushaf of Fatima?'" He said, "When God the Exalted took back His Prophet, there came upon Fatima, because of his death, a grief that only God the Mighty and Majestic knows. So God sent her an angel to console her in her sorrow and to speak with her. She complained of this to the Commander of the Believers, and he said, 'When you sense that and hear the voice, tell me.' She told him about it, and the Commander of the Believers began to write down everything he heard, until he had put together a mushaf from it." He said, "Then he said, 'It contains nothing of the lawful and the unlawful, but it contains knowledge of what will happen.'"

Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.240, no.3 3 - عدة من أصحابنا ، عن أحمد بن محمد ، عن علي بن الحكم ، عن الحسين ابن أبي العلاء قال : سمعت أبا عبد الله ﵇ يقول : إن عندي الجفر الأبيض ، قال : قلت : فأي شئ فيه ؟ قال : زبور داود ، وتوراة موسى ، وإنجيل عيسى ، وصحف إبراهيم ﵈ والحلال والحرام ، ومصحف فاطمة ، ما أزعم أن فيه قرآنا ، وفيه ما يحتاج الناس إلينا ولا نحتاج إلى أحد حتى فيه الجلدة ، ونصف الجلدة ، وربع الجلدة وأرش الخدش . 3. A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Ala, who said that he heard Abu Abd Allah say, "I have the White Jafr." He said, "I said, 'And what is in it?'" He said, "The Psalms of David, the Torah of Moses, the Gospel of Jesus, the scrolls of Abraham, the lawful and the unlawful, and the Mushaf of Fatima. I do not claim that it contains a Quran. It contains what people need from us, while we need nothing from anyone. It even contains the lash, the half lash, the quarter lash, and the compensation for a scratch."

In the first report Imam al-Sadiq ﵇ says the book is three times the size of the Qur'an. He swears it holds no letter of the Qur'an. In the second, an angel consoles Fatimah ﵍ after the Prophet's ﷺ death, and Ali ﵇ writes down what she hears. The Imam ﵇ says the book holds no law and holds knowledge of what will happen. In the third, he lists the Mushaf of Fatimah ﵍ among the contents of the White Jafr. He adds, "I do not claim that it contains a Qur'an."
Ali's Codex and His Teaching

Source: al-Kafi, vol.1, p.64, no.1, in the chapter on the difference of hadith, vol.1, pp.62-64 Speaker: Imam Ali ﵇, through Sulaym ibn Qays Claim: Ali ﵇ wrote every verse in his own hand, and the Prophet ﷺ taught him its interpretation, abrogation and scope

Imam Ali, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.64, no.1 فما نزلت على رسول الله ﵌ آية من القرآن إلا أقرأنيها وأملاها علي فكتبتها بخطي وعلمني تأويلها وتفسيرها وناسخها ومنسوخها ، ومحكمها ومتشابهها ، وخاصها وعامها ، ودعا الله أن يعطيني فهمها ، وحفظها ، فما نسيت آية من كتاب الله ولا علما أملاه علي وكتبته ، منذ دعا الله لي بما دعا ، وما ترك شيئا علمه الله من حلال ولا حرام ، ولا أمر ولا نهي كان أو يكون ولا كتاب منزل على أحد قبله من طاعة أو معصية إلا علمنيه وحفظته ، فلم أنس حرفا واحدا No verse of the Quran was sent down to the Messenger of God except that he had me recite it and dictated it to me, and I wrote it in my own hand. He taught me its interpretation (ta'wil) and its explanation (tafsir), its abrogating and abrogated verses, its decisive and ambiguous verses, and its particular and general verses. He prayed to God to give me understanding of it and memory of it. So I have not forgotten a verse of the Book of God, nor any knowledge that he dictated to me and I wrote down, since he prayed to God for me as he prayed. He left nothing that God had taught him, whether permitted or forbidden, command or prohibition, what has been or what will be, or any book sent down to anyone before him, whether of obedience or of disobedience, except that he taught it to me and I memorized it. I did not forget a single letter.

Imam Ali ﵇ says the Prophet ﷺ dictated every revealed verse to him and he wrote it in his own hand. He says the Prophet ﷺ also taught him each verse's interpretation, its abrogating and abrogated verses, and its decisive and ambiguous verses. He adds that the Prophet ﷺ prayed for his memory and that he forgot nothing.

Source: al-Tabrisi, al-Ihtijaj, vol.1, p.281 Speaker: Imam Ali ﵇, in the report of Ishaq ibn Musa from Imam al-Kazim ﵇ Claim: Ali ﵇ gathered the Qur'an after the Prophet's ﷺ burial and the people refused it

Imam Ali, al-Ihtijaj, vol.1, p.281 فلما توفي رسول الله ﵌ اشتغلت بدفنه والفراغ من شأنه ثم آليت يمينا (1) أني لا أرتدي إلا للصلاة حتى أجمع القرآن ففعلت ، ثم أخذته وجئت به فأعرضته عليهم قالوا : لا حاجة لنا به When the Messenger of God died, I was occupied with burying him and finishing his affairs. Then I swore an oath that I would not put on my cloak except for prayer until I had collected the Quran, and I did so. Then I took it, brought it, and presented it to them. They said, "We have no need of it."

Imam Ali ﵇ says he gathered the Qur'an after burying the Prophet ﷺ and the people refused it. The report of Salim ibn Salama gives the same refusal. Neither report says how Ali's ﵇ copy differed. Al-Mufid inclines to the view that the removed material was Ali's ﵇ interpretation. Al-Tabataba'i places any difference in the order of suras or of some verses.

Source: Nahj al-Balagha, sermon 176, p.252, and sermon 156, p.219, Subhi Salih numbering Speaker: Imam Ali ﵇, without an isnad Claim: this Qur'an guides without misleading, and the Book of God is the firm rope

Imam Ali, Nahj al-Balagha, sermon 176, p.252 واعْلَمُوا أَنَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ هُوَ النَّاصِحُ الَّذِي لَا يَغُشُّ - والْهَادِي الَّذِي لَا يُضِلُّ والْمُحَدِّثُ الَّذِي لَا يَكْذِبُ Know that this Quran is the adviser who does not deceive, the guide who does not lead astray, and the speaker who does not lie.

Imam Ali, Nahj al-Balagha, sermon 156, p.219 وعَلَيْكُمْ بِكِتَابِ اللَّه - فَإِنَّه الْحَبْلُ الْمَتِينُ والنُّورُ الْمُبِينُ - والشِّفَاءُ النَّافِعُ والرِّيُّ النَّاقِعُ - والْعِصْمَةُ لِلْمُتَمَسِّكِ والنَّجَاةُ لِلْمُتَعَلِّقِ - لَا يَعْوَجُّ فَيُقَامَ ولَا يَزِيغُ فَيُسْتَعْتَبَ - ولَا تُخْلِقُه كَثْرَةُ الرَّدِّ ووُلُوجُ السَّمْعِ - مَنْ قَالَ بِه صَدَقَ ومَنْ عَمِلَ بِه سَبَقَ Hold fast to the Book of God, for it is the firm rope and the clear light, the beneficial cure and the quenching drink, a protection for whoever holds to it and a rescue for whoever clings to it. It does not bend, so that it would need straightening, and it does not swerve, so that it would need to be turned back. Repeated recitation and constant hearing do not wear it out. Whoever speaks by it speaks truly, and whoever acts by it takes the lead.

Sermon 176 calls "this Qur'an" an adviser who does not deceive and a guide who does not lead astray. Sermon 156 tells its hearers to hold fast to the Book of God as the firm rope. Nahj al-Balagha gives both sermons without a chain of transmission.
Ali's Reading in the Printed Mushaf

Source: al-Dhahabi, Ma'rifat al-Qurra' al-Kibar, vol.1, p.208 Speaker: Asim and Hafs ibn Sulayman, as reported by al-Dhahabi (d.748 AH) Claim: Hafs read through Asim and Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami to Ali ﵇

al-Dhahabi, Ma'rifat al-Qurra' al-Kibar, vol.1, p.208 وروى جماعة ، عن عمرو بن الصباح ، عن حفص الغاضري ، عن عاصم ، عن أبي عبد الرحمن ، عن علي بالقراءة . وذكر عاصم أنه لم يخالف أبا عبد الرحمن في شيء من قراءته ، وأن أبا عبد الرحمن لم يخالف عليا في شيء من قراءته . A group transmitted from Amr ibn al-Sabbah, from Hafs al-Ghadiri, from Asim, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from Ali, concerning the recitation. Asim mentioned that he never differed from Abu Abd al-Rahman in any part of his recitation, and that Abu Abd al-Rahman never differed from Ali in any part of his recitation.

Hafs, in al-Dhahabi, Ma'rifat al-Qurra' al-Kibar, vol.1, p.208 ويروى عن حفص بن سليمان ، قال : قال لي عاصم : ما كان من القراءة التي قرأت بها على أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي ، فهي التي أقرأتك بها ، وما كان من القراءة التي أقرأت بها أبا بكر بن عياش ، فهي القراءة التي عرضتها على زرّ بن حبيش ، عن ابن مسعود . It is reported from Hafs ibn Sulayman, who said. Asim said to me, “Whatever recitation I recited to Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, that is the one I taught you. And whatever recitation I taught Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, that is the recitation I presented to Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ibn Masud.”

Asim says he never departed from al-Sulami's reading, and al-Sulami never departed from Ali's ﵇. Asim taught Hafs the reading he had recited to al-Sulami. He taught Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, known as Shu'ba, the reading he had presented to Zirr ibn Hubaysh from Ibn Mas'ud. By these reports, the Hafs reading descends through al-Sulami from Ali ﵇.

the introduction to the Cairo printing, in al-Tabrizi, Tanzih al-Shi'a al-Ithnay Ashariyya, vol.1, p.41 تعريف بهذا المصحف الشريف كتب هذا المصحف وضبط على ما يوافق رواية حفص بن سليمان بن المغيرة الأسدي الكوفي بقراءة عاصم بن أبي النجود الكوفي التابعي ، عن أبي عبد الرحمن عبد الله بن حبيب السلمي ، عن عثمان بن عفان ، وعلي بن أبي طالب ﵇ ، وزيد بن ثابت ، وأبي بن كعب ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه (وآله) وسلم . Introduction to this noble Quran codex. This codex was written and vocalized in agreement with the transmission of Hafs ibn Sulayman ibn al-Mughira al-Asadi al-Kufi, from the recitation of Asim ibn Abi al-Najud al-Kufi, a Follower, from Abu Abd al-Rahman Abd Allah ibn Habib al-Sulami, from Uthman ibn Affan, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Zayd ibn Thabit and Ubayy ibn Kab, from the Prophet.
The introduction to the Cairo printing of the Qur'an, quoted by al-Tabrizi, says the printing follows Hafs from Asim. It traces Asim's reading through al-Sulami to four Companions, Ali ﵇ among them.

Source: Ibn Mihran, al-Mabsut fi al-Qira'at al-Ashr, p.440; al-Shawkani, Fath al-Qadir, vol.2, p.183 Speaker: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash; al-Shawkani Claim: readings from Ali ﵇ survive inside the canonical readings

Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, in Ibn Mihran, al-Mabsut, p.440 واختار أبو بكر بن عياش {عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ} خفيفة الراء أيضا . وهو من الحروف العشرة التي ذكرت أنه قال : " أنا أدخلتها من قراءة علي - ﵁ - في قراءة عاصم حتى استخلصت قراءته " . يعني قراءة علي بن أبي طالب ﵇ . Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash also chose the reading "he acknowledged part of it" with a light ra. It is one of the ten readings concerning which I mentioned that he said, "I introduced them from the reading of Ali into the reading of Asim, until I had distilled his reading." He means the reading of Ali ibn Abi Talib.

al-Shawkani, Fath al-Qadir, vol.2, p.183 قرأ حمزة والكسائي " فارقوا دينهم " وهي قراءة علي بن أبي طالب : أي تركوا دينهم وخرجوا عنه . وقرأ الباقون فرقوا بالتشديد إلا النخعي فإنه قرأ بالتخفيف . Hamza and al-Kisai read “they parted from their religion,” which is also the reading of Ali ibn Abi Talib, meaning that they left their religion and went out from it. The other reciters read “they divided their religion,” with the doubled letter, except al-Nakhai, who read it with the light form.

Shu'ba says he brought ten readings from Ali's ﵇ reading into his reading of Asim. One of them is 'arafa with a light ra in Qur'an 66:3. The printed text of al-Mabsut gives both readings the same vocalization, including the doubling mark, so only Ibn Mihran's words "light" and "doubled" tell them apart. Al-Shawkani reports that Hamza and al-Kisa'i read faraqu in Qur'an 6:159, and he names it Ali's ﵇ reading. These reports place readings attributed to Ali ﵇ inside the canonical readings of Asim, Hamza and al-Kisa'i.
Collection in the Imami Sources

Source: al-Majlisi, Bihar al-Anwar, vol.89, pp.77-78, quoting al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi through Jami' al-Usul Speaker: Zayd ibn Thabit Claim: Zayd gathered the Qur'an for Abu Bakr from scraps of parchment, palm stalks, thin stones and the memories of men
Al-Majlisi's Bihar al-Anwar carries the Sunni account of how the Qur'an was collected. He copied Zayd ibn Thabit's report and labels it as al-Bukhari's and al-Tirmidhi's.

Zayd ibn Thabit, in al-Majlisi, Bihar al-Anwar, vol.89, pp.77-78 أقول : روى البخاري والترمذي في صحيحيهما وذكره في جامع الأصول في حرف التاء في باب ترتيب القرآن وتأليفه وجمعه ، عن زيد بن ثابت قال : أرسل إلى أبو بكر بعد مقتل أهل اليمامة فإذا عمر جالس عنده ، فقال أبو بكر : إن عمر جاءني فقال : إن القتل قد استحر يوم اليمامة بقراء القرآن ، وإني أخشى أن يستحر القتل بالقراء في كل المواطن ، فيذهب من القرآن كثير وإني أرى أن تذهب بجمع القرآن ، قال : قلت لعمر : وكيف أفعل شيئا لم يفعله رسول الله ﵌ فقال عمر : هو والله خير ، فلم يزل يراجعني في ذلك حتى شرح الله صدري للذي شرح له صدر عمر ، ورأيت في ذلك الذي رأي عمر ، قال زيد : فقال لي أبو بكر : إنك رجل شاب عاقل ، لا نتهمك ، قد كنت تكتب الوحي لرسول الله ﵌ فتتبع القرآن فأجمعه ، قال زيد : فوالله لو كلفني نقل جبل من الجبال ، ما كان أثقل على مما أمرني به من جمع القرآن . قال : قلت : كيف تفعلان شيئا لم يفعله رسول الله ؟ فقال أبو بكر : هو والله خير ، قال : فلم يزل أبو بكر يراجعني - وفي رواية أخرى فلم يزل عمر يراجعني - حتى شرح الله صدري للذي شرح له صدر أبي بكر قال : فتتبعت القرآن : أجمعه من الرقاع والعسب واللخاف وصدور الرجال حتى وجدت آخر سورة التوبة مع خزيمة أو أبي خزيمة الأنصاري لم أجدها مع أحد غيره " لقد جائكم رسول من أنفسكم عزيز عليه " خاتمة براءة . قال : فكانت الصحف عند أبي بكر حتى توفاه الله ثم عند عمر حتى توفاه الله ، ثم حفصة بنت عمر ، قال بعض الرواة : فيه اللخاف يعني الخزف ، قال في جامع الأصول : أخرجه البخاري والترمذي . I say that al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi reported in their two Sahih collections, and it is also mentioned in Jami al-Usul under the letter ta, in the chapter on the arrangement, composition and collection of the Quran, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said Abu Bakr sent for me after the killing of the people of Yamama, and Umar was sitting with him. Abu Bakr said, "Umar came to me and said, 'Killing has become fierce on the day of Yamama among the reciters of the Quran, and I fear that killing will become fierce among the reciters in every place, so that much of the Quran goes. I think you should go about the collection of the Quran.' I said to Umar, 'How can I do something the Messenger of God did not do?' Umar said, 'By God, it is good.' He kept going back to me about it until God opened my chest to what he had opened Umar's chest to, and I came to hold on that matter the view that Umar held." Zayd said, "Abu Bakr then said to me, 'You are a young and intelligent man, and we do not suspect you. You used to write down the revelation for the Messenger of God, so seek out the Quran and collect it.'" Zayd said, "By God, if he had charged me with moving one of the mountains, it would not have been heavier on me than what he commanded me to do in collecting the Quran." He said, "I said, 'How can you two do something the Messenger of God did not do?' Abu Bakr said, 'By God, it is good.'" He said, "Abu Bakr kept going back to me about it (in another narration, Umar kept going back to me) until God opened my chest to what he had opened Abu Bakr's chest to." He said, "So I sought out the Quran, collecting it from scraps of parchment, palm stalks, thin stones (lakhaf) and the chests of men, until I found the end of Surat al-Tawba with Khuzayma, or Abu Khuzayma, the Ansari. I did not find it with anyone else, 'A messenger has come to you from among yourselves, it is grievous to him...', the closing verses of Bara'a." He said, "The sheets then remained with Abu Bakr until God took him, then with Umar until God took him, then with Hafsa, the daughter of Umar." Some of the transmitters said that in this report lakhaf means pottery. He said in Jami al-Usul that al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi transmitted it.

In Zayd's account, the killing on the day of Yamama has been heavy among the Qur'an reciters. Umar fears that much of the Qur'an will be lost and urges Abu Bakr to collect it. Abu Bakr then asks Zayd to gather the Qur'an. He gathers it from scraps of parchment, palm stalks, thin stones and men's memories. A narrator glosses the word for thin stones, lakhaf, as pottery.

Uthman, in al-Askari, al-Qur'an al-Karim wa Riwayat al-Madrasatayn, vol.1, p.211 في مسند أحمد بسنده عن ابن عباس أنه قال في حديثه عن الخليفة عثمان أنّه قال : إن رسول اللّه ( ص ) كان مما يأتي عليه الزمان ينزل عليه من السور ذوات العدد ، وكان إذا أنزل عليه الشيء يدعو بعض من يكتب عنده ، يقول : ضعوا هذا في السورة التي يذكر فيها كذا وكذا ، وينزل عليه الآيات فيقول : ضعوا هذه الآيات في السورة التي يذكر فيها كذا وكذا ، وينزل عليه الآية فيقول : ضعوا هذه الآية في السورة التي يذكر فيها كذا وكذا (9) . In the Musnad of Ahmad, with its chain of transmission, from Ibn Abbas, who said in his report about the caliph Uthman that he said. “Time would often pass for the Messenger of God while a number of surahs were being revealed to him. Whenever something was revealed to him, he would call one of those who wrote for him and say, ‘Put this in the surah in which such and such is mentioned.’ Verses would be revealed to him and he would say, ‘Put these verses in the surah in which such and such is mentioned.’ A verse would be revealed to him and he would say, ‘Put this verse in the surah in which such and such is mentioned.’”

Al-Askari cites Musnad Ahmad, where Ibn Abbas reports Uthman's account. The Prophet ﷺ told his scribes to place each revealed verse in a named sura. By this report, the Prophet ﷺ assigned verses to their suras.
Source: Ibn Abi Dawud, Kitab al-Masahif, p.67, no.39 Speaker: Imam Ali ﵇, through Suwayd ibn Ghafala Claim: had Uthman not done it with the codices, Ali ﵇ would have

Imam Ali, Ibn Abi Dawud, Kitab al-Masahif, p.67, no.39 [ 39 ] حدثنا (39) عبد اللّه قال حدثنا سهل بن صالح قال قال حدثنا أبو داود ويعقوب قالا أخبرنا شعبة عن علقمة بن مرثد عن سويد بن غفلة قال قال علي في المصاحف لو لم يصنعه عثمان لصنعته [ قال أبو داود « * » عن رجل عن سويد ] . [39] Abd Allah narrated to us, he said, Sahl ibn Salih narrated to us, he said, he said, Abu Dawud and Yaqub narrated to us, both said, Shuba informed us, from Alqama ibn Marthad, from Suwayd ibn Ghafala, who said. Ali said about the codices, “If Uthman had not done it, I would have done it.” [Abu Dawud said, from a man, from Suwayd.]

Suwayd ibn Ghafala reports that Ali ﵇ said of the codices, "If Uthman had not done it, I would have done it." Ibn Abi Dawud notes that Abu Dawud's version of the chain has an unnamed man before Suwayd. If the report is sound, Ali's ﵇ words endorse Uthman's unification of the codices.
The Earliest Manuscripts

Source: University of Birmingham news release, 22 July 2015; van Putten, BSOAS 82 (2019), pp.271-288; Sadeghi and Bergmann, Arabica 57 (2010), pp.343-436 Speaker: the University of Birmingham; Marijn van Putten; Behnam Sadeghi and Uwe Bergmann Claim: the earliest dated copies fall close to the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime, and van Putten argues that fourteen early manuscripts descend from one written archetype

Radiocarbon analysis dated the parchment of the two Birmingham leaves to between 568 and 645 CE, with 95.4 per cent accuracy. The leaves carry parts of suras 18 to 20 in Hijazi, an early form of Arabic script. Marijn van Putten examined how fourteen early manuscripts spell ni'mat in the phrase "the grace of God". Each manuscript uses the same one of two possible spellings at the same places. He argues that only a single written archetype explains this agreement. On his argument, a project to codify the text took place in the first Islamic century. Sadeghi and Bergmann describe a manuscript from the first half of the seventh century CE. Its text does not belong to the Uthmanic tradition. They report it as the only known manuscript of that kind. These studies support an early written standard text. They do not show what the Companions' earlier copies contained.
The Scholars of the School
Source: al-Saduq, al-I'tiqadat, p.86 Speaker: Shaykh al-Saduq (d.381 AH) Claim: the Qur'an is what lies between the two covers, and whoever attributes more to the Imamis lies

al-Saduq, al-I'tiqadat, p.86 اعتقادنا أن القرآن الذي أنزله الله تعالى على نبيه محمد ﵌ هو ما بين الدفتين ، وهو ما في أيدي الناس ، ليس بأكثر من ذلك ، ومبلغ سوره عند الناس مائة وأربع عشرة سورة . وعندنا أن الضحى وألم نشرح سورة واحدة ، ولايلاف وألم تر كيف سورة واحدة (1) . ومن نسب إلينا أنا نقول إنه أكثر من ذلك فهو كاذب . Our belief is that the Quran which God Almighty sent down to His Prophet Muhammad is what lies between the two covers, and it is what is in people's hands. It is not more than that. The number of its surahs among the people is one hundred and fourteen. We hold that al-Duha and Alam Nashrah are one surah, and that Li-Ilaf and Alam Tara Kayfa are one surah. Whoever attributes to us the claim that it is more than that is a liar.

Al-Saduq's creed says the Qur'an God sent down is what lies between the two covers, and no more. He gives the people's count of suras as 114. He adds that the Imamis count al-Duha with al-Sharh, and al-Fil with Quraysh, as single suras. That ruling changes the count of suras and leaves the text the same.

Source: al-Mufid, al-Masa'il al-Sarawiyya, pp.78-79 and p.81; Awa'il al-Maqalat, pp.82-83 Speaker: Shaykh al-Mufid (d.413 AH) Claim: al-Mufid gave two answers on omission, and in Awa'il al-Maqalat he inclined to the view that only interpretation was removed

al-Mufid, al-Masa'il al-Sarawiyya, pp.78-79 المسألة التاسعة : صيانة القرآن من التحريف ما قولة - أدام الله تعالى حراسته (1) - في القرآن : أهو ما بين الدفتين ، الذي في أيدي الناس ، أم هل ضاع مما أنزل الله تعالى على نبيه منه شئ ، أم لا ؟ وهل هو ما جمعه أمير المؤمنين ﵇ ، أم ما جمعه عثمان بن عفان على ما يذكره المخالفون ؟ الجواب : لا شك (2) أن الذي بين الدفتين من القرآن جميعه (3) كلام الله تعالى وتنزيله ، وليس فيه شئ من كلام البشر ، وهو جمهور المنزل . والباقي مما أنزله (4) الله تعالى (5) عند المستحفظ للشريعة ، المستودع للأحكام ، لم يضع (1) منه شئ (2) . وإن كان الذي جمع ما بين الدفتين الآن لم يجعله في جملة ما جمع لأسباب (3) دعته إلى ذلك ، منها : قصوره عن معرفة بعضه . ومنها : شكه فيه وعدم تيقنه (4) . ومنها : ما تعمد إخراجه منه . وقد جمع أمير المؤمنين ﵇ القرآن المنزل من أوله إلى آخره ، وألفه بحسب ما وجب من تأليفه ، فقدم المكي على المدني ، والمنسوخ على الناسخ ، ووضع كل شئ منه في محله (5) . فلذلك قاد جعفر بن محمد الصادق ﵉ : " أما والله لو قرئ القرآن كما أنزل لألفيتمونا فيه مسمين كما سمي من كان قبلنا " (6) . Ninth question, the protection of the Quran from alteration. What is the opinion of the shaykh, may God Almighty prolong his guardianship, about the Quran? Is it what lies between the two covers, which is in people's hands, or has some of what God Almighty sent down to His Prophet been lost, or not? And is it what the Commander of the Faithful collected, or what Uthman ibn Affan collected, as the opponents say? The answer is that there is no doubt that what lies between the two covers, all of it, is the speech of God Almighty and His revelation, and that nothing in it is the speech of human beings. It is the majority of what was revealed. The rest of what God Almighty revealed is with the one entrusted to preserve the law and to whom the rulings are committed, and none of it has been lost. This is so even though the one who collected what lies between the two covers did not include it all in what he collected, for reasons that led him to that. Among them were his limited knowledge of some of it, his doubt about some of it and his lack of certainty about it, and his deliberate exclusion of some of it. The Commander of the Faithful collected the revealed Quran from its beginning to its end and arranged it as its arrangement required. He placed the Meccan before the Medinan and the abrogated before the abrogating, and put everything in its proper place. For that reason Jafar ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq said, “By God, if the Quran were recited as it was revealed, you would find us named in it, just as those before us were named.”

al-Mufid, al-Masa'il al-Sarawiyya, p.81 غير أن الخبر قد صح عن أئمتنا ﵈ أنهم أمروا بقراءة ما بين الدفتين ، وأن لا (1) يتعداه إلا زيادة فيه ولا نقصان منه حتى يقوم القائم ﵇ فيقرأ للناس (2) القرآن على ما أنزله الله تعالى وجمعه أمير المؤمنين ﵇ (3) . However, the report has been established as sound from our Imams that they commanded the recitation of what lies between the two covers, and that one should not go beyond it, whether by adding to it or by subtracting from it, until the Riser rises and recites to the people the Quran as God Almighty revealed it and as the Commander of the Faithful collected it.

al-Mufid, Awa'il al-Maqalat, pp.82-83 وأما النقصان فإن العقول لا تحيله ولا تمنع من وقوعه ، وقد امتحنت مقالة من ادعاه ، وكلمت عليه المعتزلة وغيرهم طويلا فلم اظفر منهم بحجة اعتمدها في فساده . وقد قال جماعة من أهل الإمامة إنه لم ينقص من كلمة ولا من آية ولا من سورة ولكن حذف ما كان مثبتا في مصحف أمير المؤمنين ( ع ) من تأويله وتفسير معانيه على حقيقة تنزيله وذلك كان ثابتا منزلا وإن لم يكن من جملة كلام الله تعالى الذي هو القرآن المعجز ، وقد يسمى تأويل القرآن قرآنا قال الله تعالى : ( ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه وقل رب زدني علما ) فسمى تأويل القرآن قرآنا ، وهذا ما ليس فيه بين أهل التفسير اختلاف . وعندي أن هذا القول أشبه من مقال من ادعى نقصان كلم من نفس القرآن على الحقيقة دون التأويل ، وإليه أميل والله أسأل توفيقه للصواب . وأما الزيادة فيه فمقطوع على فسادها من وجه ويجوز صحتها من وجه ، فالوجه الذي أقطع على فساده أن يمكن لأحد من الخلق زيادة مقدار سورة فيه على حد يلتبس به عند أحد من الفصحاء ، وأما الوجه المجوز فهو أن يزاد فيه الكلمة والكلمتان والحرف والحرفان وما أشبه ذلك مما لا يبلغ حد الاعجاز ، ويكون ملتبسا عند أكثر الفصحاء بكلم القرآن ، غير أنه لا بد متى وقع ذلك من أن يدل الله عليه ، ويوضح لعباده عن الحق فيه ، ولست أقطع على كون ذلك بل أميل إلى عدمه وسلامة القرآن عنه ، ومعي بذلك حديث عن الصادق جعفر بن محمد (ع) ، وهذا المذهب بخلاف ما سمعناه عن بني نوبخت - ﵏ - من الزيادة في القرآن والنقصان فيه ، وقد ذهب إليه جماعة من متكلمي الإمامية وأهل الفقه منهم والاعتبار . As for omission, reason does not rule it out or prevent it from happening. I have examined the claim of those who asserted it, and I have spoken at length about it with the Mu'tazila and others, but I found in them no argument that I could rely on to show it false. A group of the Imamis have said that no word, verse or chapter was left out. What was removed, they say, is what had been written in the codex of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, namely its interpretation and the explanation of its meanings according to the truth of its revelation. That material was established and sent down, even though it was not part of the speech of God Most High that is the inimitable Quran. The interpretation of the Quran can also be called Quran. God Most High said, "Do not hasten with the Quran before its revelation is completed to you, and say, 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge.'" So He called the interpretation of the Quran "Quran," and the scholars of exegesis do not disagree about this. In my view this position is closer to the truth than the statement of those who claimed that actual words were lost from the Quran itself, rather than from its interpretation. I incline toward it, and I ask God for success in reaching what is correct. As for addition to the Quran, one kind is certainly false and another kind is possible. The kind I am certain is false is that any human being could add the length of a chapter to it in such a way that it would be confused with the Quran in the judgment of any eloquent speaker. The kind that is possible is that a word or two words, or a letter or two letters, or something similar that does not reach the level of inimitability, was added to it and was mistaken for Quranic words by most eloquent speakers. Even so, if that had happened, God would necessarily have pointed it out and made the truth about it clear to His servants. I am not certain that it happened. I incline instead toward its not having happened and toward the Quran being free of it, and I have a report from al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, that supports this. This position differs from what we heard from the Banu Nawbakht, may God have mercy on them, about addition to the Quran and omission from it. A group of Imami theologians, including their jurists and scholars of reflection, have held to it.

In al-Sarawiyya al-Mufid says everything between the covers is God's speech and the majority of what was sent down. He says the rest is with the guardian of the law, who is entrusted with the rulings, and none of it is lost. He names three reasons the compiler left it out, namely limited knowledge, doubt and deliberate exclusion. He adds that the Imams ﵈ commanded recitation of what lies between the covers until al-Qa'im ﵇ rises.

In Awa'il al-Maqalat al-Mufid says reason allows omission. He found no argument against it that he could rely on. He reports a group of Imamis who deny the loss of any word, verse or sura. They hold that what was removed was the interpretation recorded in Ali's ﵇ codex. Al-Mufid calls their view closer to the truth and inclines toward it. He rules out the addition of a sura's length, and he allows that a word or a letter could be added. He says that God would make any such addition known, and he inclines to deny that it occurred. The sources quoted give no order in which al-Mufid wrote the two works.

Source: al-Murtada, al-Dhakhira fi Ilm al-Kalam, pp.361-362; al-Tabrisi, Majma' al-Bayan, vol.1, pp.42-43 Speaker: al-Sharif al-Murtada (d.436 AH); Amin al-Islam al-Tabrisi (d.548 AH) Claim: knowledge of the Qur'an's transmission is like knowledge of great cities and events

al-Murtada, al-Dhakhira, pp.361-362 فان قيل : كيف يكون أحد الامرين كالآخر والامامية تدّعي تغييرا في القرآن ونقصانا ، وكذلك حشوية أصحاب الحديث ؟ قلنا : قد بيّنا صحة نقل القرآن في المسائل الطرابلسيات (3) ، وأنه غير منقوص ولا مبدّل ولا مغيّر ، وأن العلم بأن هذا القرآن الذي في أيدينا هو الذي ظهر على يد رسول اللّه « ص » كالعلم بالبلدان والحوادث الكبار والوقائع العظام ، والكتب المصنفة المشهورة ، والاشعار المدونة . وذكرنا أن العناية اشتدت بالقرآن والدواعي توفرت على نقله وحراسته وبلغت إلى حدّ لم يبلغه في نقل الحوادث والوقائع والكتب المصنفة ، لأن القرآن معجز النبوة ، وأصل العلم بالشريعة والاحكام الدينية . وكل شيء دعا إلى نقل جميع ما تقدم حاصل فيه ، ويستبدّ بدواع إلى النقل ليست في الحوادث وما أشبهها ، وأن علماء المتكلمين بلغوا في ضبطه وحمايته ، وان عرفوا كل شيء اختلف (1) فيه من اعرابه والقراءات المختلفة في حروفه حتى فرّقوا بين ما روي وعرف ، وبين ما لم يذكر ولم يسطر . فكيف يجوز أن يكون مغيّرا أو منقوصا مع هذه العناية الصادقة والضبط الشديد ؟ If it is asked how one of the two matters can be like the other, when the Imamis claim alteration and diminution in the Quran, and so do the Hashwiyya among the hadith folk, we say that we have already explained the soundness of the transmission of the Quran in al-Masa'il al-Tarabulusiyyat. We showed that it is not diminished, replaced, or altered. We also showed that knowledge that this Quran in our hands is what appeared at the hands of the Messenger of God is like knowledge of countries, great events, major incidents, famous compiled books, and recorded poems. We mentioned also that care for the Quran was intense, and that the motives to transmit and guard it were abundant, to a degree not reached in the transmission of events, incidents, and compiled books. The reason is that the Quran is the miracle that proves prophethood and the foundation of knowledge of the Law and of religious rulings. Everything that prompted the transmission of all those earlier things is present in it, and it alone has motives for transmission that events and the like do not have. The scholars among the theologians went so far in preserving and protecting it that they even knew everything disputed in it, such as its grammatical inflection and the different readings of its letters, until they distinguished between what was narrated and known and what was not mentioned or written down. So how can it be altered or diminished, given this genuine care and strict preservation?

Al-Murtada answers an objector who says the Imamis, like the hashwiyya among the traditionists, claim change and loss in the Qur'an. Hashwiyya is the name the objector gives to a group among the hadith folk. Al-Murtada says knowledge of the Qur'an's transmission is like knowledge of great cities and famous events. He adds that the theologians among the scholars knew everything disputed in it, including its inflection and its readings. He asks how the Qur'an could be altered or diminished under such care.
In the introduction to Majma' al-Bayan, al-Tabrisi sets aside the discussion of addition to and loss from the Qur'an as unsuitable for exegesis.

al-Tabrisi, Majma' al-Bayan, vol.1, pp.42-43 ومن ذلك : الكلام في زيادة القرآن ونقصانه فإنه لا يليق بالتفسير . فأما الزيادة فيه : فمجمع على بطلانه . وأما النقصان منه : فقد روى جماعة من أصحابنا ، وقوم من حشوية العامة ، أن في القرآن تغييرا أو نقصانا ، والصحيح من مذهب أصحابنا خلافه Of this kind is the discussion of increase and decrease in the Quran, which is unsuitable for exegesis. As for increase in it, its invalidity is unanimously agreed. As for decrease from it, a group of our companions and a group of the Hashwiyya of the general body of Muslims (al-'amma) have narrated that the Quran contains alteration or diminution. The sound position of our companions is the opposite.

Al-Tabrisi calls addition invalid by consensus. He reports that some Imamis, and a band of the hashwiyya among the general body of Muslims, narrated loss. He calls the denial of loss the sound position of his school. His passage reports the loss view without naming the scholars who held it.
Source: al-Khoei, al-Bayan, p.259 Speaker: al-Khoei Claim: the claim of tahrif is a fable

al-Khoei, al-Bayan, p.259 ومما ذكرناه : قد تبين للقارئ أن حديث تحريف القرآن حديث خرافة وخيال ، لا يقول به إلا من ضعف عقله ، أو من لم يتأمل في أطرافه حق التأمل ، أو من ألجأه إليه يجب القول به . والحب يعمي ويصم ، وأما العاقل المنصف المتدبر فلا يشك في بطلانه وخرافته . From what we have mentioned, it has become clear to the reader that the talk of the Qur'an's alteration is a superstitious tale and a fantasy. No one holds it except one whose reason is weak, or one who has not reflected on its aspects with the reflection they deserve, or one whom love of holding the view drives to it. Love blinds and deafens. But the sensible, fair-minded person who reflects has no doubt that it is false and a superstitious tale.

Al-Khoei closes his discussion by calling tahrif a fable. He says only a weak or unreflecting mind holds it, or one whom love of the view drives to it. The printed al-Bayan reads yajib, "must", at that point. Other works that quote the passage read hubb, "love", which matches al-Khoei's next sentence, "Love blinds and deafens".

Source: al-Khomeini, Anwar al-Hidaya fi al-Ta'liqa ala al-Kifaya, vol.1, pp.207-208 Speaker: Sayyid Ruhollah al-Khomeini (d.1409 AH) Claim: the verifying scholars of both groups deny tahrif, and Fasl al-Khitab cites reports the early scholars had set aside

al-Khomeini, Anwar al-Hidaya, vol.1, pp.207-208 أمّا الأولى : فلمنع وقوع التحريف فيه جدّاً ، كما هو مذهب المحقّقين من علماء العامّة والخاصّة ، والمعتبرين من الفريقين ، وإن شئت شطراً من الكلام في هذا المقام فارجع إلى مقدّمة تفسير آلاء الرحمن للعلّامة البلاغي المعاصر ﵋ (2) . وأزيدك توضيحاً : أنّه لو كان الأمر كما توهّم صاحب «فصل الخطاب» الذي كان كتبه لا يفيد علماً ولا عملًا ، وإنّما هو إيراد روايات أعرض عنها الأصحاب ، واختلاط ضعاف بين الروايات بعد تنزيهها عنها أولو الألباب من قدماء أصحابنا كالمحمّدين الثلاثة المتقدّمين ﵏ . هذا حال كتب روايته غالباً ك «المستدرك» ، ولا تسأل عن سائر كتبه المشحونة بالقصص والحكايات الغريبة التي غالبها بالهزل أشبه منه بالجدّ ، وهو ﵀ شخص صالح متتبّع ، إلّاأنّ اشتياقه لجمع الضعاف والغرائب والعجائب وما لا يقبلها العقل السليم والرأي المستقيم ، أكثر من الكلام النافع ، والعجب من معاصريه من أهل اليقظة ! كيف ذهلوا وغفلوا حتّى وقع ما وقع ممّا بكت عليه السماوات ، وكادت تتدكدك على الأرض ؟ ! وبالجملة : لو كان الأمر كما ذكره هذا وأشباهه ، من كون الكتاب الإلهي مشحوناً بذكر أهل البيت وفضلهم ، وذكر أمير المؤمنين وإثبات وصايته وإمامته ، فلِمَ لم يحتجّ بواحد من تلك الآيات النازلة والبراهين القاطعة من الكتاب الإلهي أميرُالمؤمنين ، وفاطمة ، والحسن ، والحسين ﵈ وسلمان ، وأبوذرّ ، ومقداد ، وعمّار ، وسائر الأصحاب الذين لا يزالون يحتجّون على خلافته ﵇ (1) ؟ ! ولمَ تشبّث ﵇ بالأحاديث النبوية (2) ، والقرآن بين أظهرهم ؟ ! As for the first, it is because the occurrence of distortion in it is utterly ruled out, as is the position of the verifying scholars among the general body of Muslims (al-'amma) and the particular group, and of the reliable authorities of both camps. If you want a portion of the discussion on this point, turn to the introduction of the Quran commentary Ala al-Rahman by the great contemporary scholar al-Balaghi. I add a further clarification for you. If the matter were as the author of Fasl al-Khitab imagined, whose books give neither knowledge nor practical benefit, and are only a presentation of reports that the associates turned away from, and a mixing of weak reports among the reports, after people of understanding among our early scholars, such as the three earlier Muhammads, had cleared them of these weak ones. This is the condition of his books of narration for the most part, such as al-Mustadrak. Do not ask about the rest of his books, which are crammed with strange stories and tales, most of which resemble jest more than earnest. He was a righteous and diligent researcher, except that his eagerness to gather weak, strange and wondrous reports, which sound reason and upright judgment do not accept, was greater than his eagerness for useful discourse. It is astonishing that his contemporaries among the people of alertness were so stunned and heedless that what happened did happen, the thing over which the heavens wept and almost crumbled onto the earth! In short, if the matter were as he and his like have stated, that the divine Book is crammed with mention of the Ahl al-Bayt and their merit, and with mention of the Commander of the Faithful and proof of his designation as successor and his imamate, then why did none of those revealed verses and decisive proofs from the divine Book get cited as argument by the Commander of the Faithful, Fatima, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, or by Salman, Abu Dharr, al-Miqdad, Ammar, and the rest of the Companions who kept arguing for his caliphate? And why did he hold fast to the prophetic traditions while the Quran was in their midst?

Al-Khomeini says the verifying scholars among the general body of Muslims (al-'amma) and among the particular group (al-khassa), meaning the Shia, deny tahrif. He says Fasl al-Khitab, al-Nuri's collection of reports on tahrif, cites reports that the associates (al-ashab, the school's scholars) turned away from. He adds that early scholars such as the three Muhammads had already cleared the reports of such weak items. Imami scholars give that name to al-Kulayni, al-Saduq and al-Tusi. He calls al-Nuri righteous and diligent, and too eager for weak and strange material. On the next page he tests the claim of the author of Fasl al-Khitab "and his like" against the history of the dispute over succession. Suppose the Book were full of the Household's merits and of Ali's ﵇ appointment. He asks why Ali ﵇, Fatimah ﵍, al-Hasan ﵇ and al-Husayn ﵇ never argued from those verses. He asks the same of Salman, Abu Dharr, al-Miqdad and Ammar. He also asks why Ali ﵇ relied on the Prophet's ﷺ hadiths while the Qur'an was among them.

al-Sistani, Istifta'at, p.131, no.489 489 . السؤال : لقد قرأت كثيرا في ما ينشر على الانترنت عن موضوع تحريف القرآن ، حيث ينسبونه إلى الشيعة ويستدلون بأدلة من المذهب الشيعي ، فلا أعلم مدى صحة هذه الأقاويل ؟ الجواب : دعوى باطلة أجيب عليها من قبل علماء الشيعة مرات عديدة وهم يكررون القول الباطل وعقيدتنا أن القرآن المنزل من الله تعالى على النبي الأكرم - ﵌ - هو نفس القرآن الموجود لدى المسلمين حاليا من دون زيادة ولا نقيصة . 489. Question. I have read a great deal of what is published on the internet about the subject of the distortion of the Qur'an. They attribute it to the Shia and cite evidence from the Shia school, and I do not know how valid these claims are. Answer. It is a false claim. Shia scholars have answered it many times, yet they keep repeating the false statement. Our belief is that the Qur'an sent down by God Almighty upon the Noble Prophet is the very Qur'an that Muslims have today, without addition or deficiency.

Al-Sistani is asked about internet claims that attribute tahrif to the Shia. He calls the claim false. He says the Qur'an God sent down is the Qur'an Muslims have today, without addition or deficiency.
Source: al-Fayd al-Kashani, al-Safi, vol.1, pp.52-58 Speaker: al-Fayd al-Kashani (d.1091 AH) Claim: the reports show the Qur'an in hand is incomplete, and the whole survives with its people

al-Fayd al-Kashani, al-Safi, vol.1, p.52 أقول : المستفاد من مجمع هذه الأخبار وغيرها من الروايات من طريق أهل البيت (عيهم السلام) إن القرآن الذي بين أظهرنا ليس بتمامه كما انزل على محمد (﵌) منه ما هو خلاف ما أنزل الله ومنه ما هو مغير ومحرف وإنه قد حذف عنه أشياء كثيرة منها اسم علي (﵇) في كثير من المواضع ومنها غير ذلك وأنه ليس أيضا على الترتيب المرضي عند الله وعند رسوله (﵌) . I say. What is gathered from the whole of these reports and from other narrations by way of the Ahl al-Bayt is that the Qur'an among us is not complete as it was sent down to Muhammad. Part of it is contrary to what God sent down, and part of it is altered and distorted. Many things have been removed from it, among them the name of Ali in many places, and other things besides. It is also not in the order that is pleasing to God and to His Messenger.

al-Fayd al-Kashani, al-Safi, vol.1, p.54 أقول : ويرد على هذا كله إشكال وهو أنه على هذا التقدير لم يبق لنا اعتماد على شئ من القرآن إذ على هذا يحتمل كل آية منه أن يكون محرفا ومغيرا ويكون على خلاف ما أنزل الله فلم يبق لنا في القرآن حجة أصلا فتنتفي فائدته وفائدة الأمر باتباعه والوصية بالتمسك به إلى غير ذلك ، وأيضا قال الله ﷿ : وإنه لكتاب عزيز لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه . وقال : إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون فكيف يتطرق إليه التحريف والتغيير ، وأيضا قد استفاض عن النبي (﵌) والأئمة (﵈) حديث عرض الخبر المروي على كتاب الله ليعلم صحته بموافقته له وفساده بمخالفته فإذا كان القرآن الذي بأيدينا محرفا فما فائدة العرض مع أن خبر التحريف مخالف لكتاب الله مكذب له فيجب رده والحكم بفساده أو تأويله . I say that an objection arises against all of this. On this assumption, we are left with nothing in the Quran that we can rely on. For on this view every verse in it could be altered and changed, and could differ from what God sent down. Then nothing in the Quran would remain a proof for us at all, so its benefit would be lost. The benefit of the command to follow it and of the instruction to hold fast to it would be lost too, and so on. Also, God, mighty and majestic, said, "And it is indeed a mighty Book. Falsehood cannot come at it from before it or from behind it." And He said, "It is We who sent down the Reminder, and it is We who will guard it." So how could alteration or change reach it? Also, the hadith about presenting a transmitted report to the Book of God is widely reported from the Prophet and the Imams. By it, the soundness of a report is known through its agreement with the Book, and its falseness through its disagreement. If the Quran in our hands were altered, what would be the use of this presentation? Moreover, the report of alteration contradicts the Book of God and denies it. So it must be rejected and judged false, or else interpreted.

al-Fayd al-Kashani, al-Safi, vol.1, p.55 ولا يبعد أيضا أن يقال إن بعض المحذوفات كان من قبيل التفسير والبيان ولم يكن من أجزاء القرآن فيكون التبديل من حيث المعنى أي حرفوه وغيروه في تفسيره وتأويله أعني حملوه على خلاف ما هو به ، فمعنى قولهم (﵈) كذا نزلت أن المراد به ذلك لا أنها نزلت مع هذه الزيادة في لفظها فحذف منها ذلك اللفظ . It is also not far-fetched to say that some of the omitted material was explanation and clarification, and was not part of the Quran. In that case the substitution is in the meaning. That is, they altered and changed the Quran in its explanation and interpretation, by which I mean they applied it contrary to what it really means. So the saying of the Imams, "It was revealed thus," means that the intended sense is that one. It does not mean that the verse was revealed with this addition in its wording, and that this wording was then removed from it.

al-Fayd al-Kashani, al-Safi, vol.1, p.58 أقول : يكفي في وجوده في كل عصر وجوده جميعا كما أنزله الله محفوظا عند أهله ووجود ما احتجنا إليه منه عندنا وإن لم نقدر على الباقي كما أن الإمام (﵇) كذلك فان الثقلين سيان في ذلك . I say, for its existence in every age it is enough that all of it exists, just as God sent it down, preserved with its people, and that what we need of it is with us, even if we are unable to reach the rest. The Imam is the same in this respect, for the two weighty things are alike in that.

Al-Fayd reads the reports as showing that the Qur'an in hand is incomplete, partly altered and out of order. He counts Ali's ﵇ name among the things removed. He lists three objections to that reading. No verse could be relied on, and Qur'an 15:9 and 41:42 would be contradicted. Qur'an 41:42 says falsehood cannot reach the Book. The rule of judging reports by the Book would also lose its use. He allows that some omitted material was explanation, so that "it was revealed thus" gives the intended sense. He concludes that the whole Qur'an exists, preserved with "its people" (ahlihi), a phrase for which he names no group. The part the community needs is in its hands, even if it cannot reach the rest. He likens the Qur'an to the Imam, who also exists beyond the community's reach. Al-Mufid's Sarawiyya places the rest of the revelation with the guardian of the law, which resembles this answer.
Glossary

shawadhdh. Irregular readings, reported outside the accepted readings. tanzil. Revelation, the act of sending down or the text sent down. Al-Tabataba'i reads "it was revealed thus" in many reports as the explanation that accompanied the revelation. kuttab. Plural of katib, writer or scribe.
Final Verdict

Final Verdict Imami scholars from al-Saduq to al-Sistani hold that the Qur'an between the two covers is the Qur'an God sent down. Al-Majlisi and al-Fayd al-Kashani read some reports as evidence of loss, and al-Mufid allows omission by the compiler. These positions show that some Imami scholars accepted or allowed omission. They do not make alteration the doctrine of the Imamiyya.
