n0007.caption: Ibn Hazm, al-Fisal, vol.4, p.182
paragraphs: ومن قول الإمامية كلها قديما وحديثا ان القرآن مبدل زيد فيه ما ليس منه ونقص منه كثير وبدل منه كثير حاشا علي ابن الحسن ابن موسى بن محمد بن إبراهيم بن موسى بن جعفر بن محمد بن علي بن الحسن ابن علي بن أبي طالب وكان أماميا يظاهر بالاعتزال مع ذلك فإنه كان ينكر هذا القول ويكفر من قاله وكذلك صاحباه أبو يعلى ميلاد الطوسي وأبو القاسم الرازي

It is the view of all the Imamites, early and late, that the Qur'an has been altered, that material not part of it was added to it, and that much was removed from it and much was changed in it. The one exception is Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Musa ibn Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib. He was an Imamite who openly sided with Mu'tazilism, and yet he rejected this view and declared anyone who held it an unbeliever. His two companions, Abu Yala Milad al-Tusi and Abu al-Qasim al-Razi, did the same.

n0009.caption: al-Safadi, al-Wafi bil-Wafayat, vol.21, pp.2-3
paragraphs: الشريف المرتضى علي بن الحسين بين موسى بن محمد بن موسى بن إبراهيم بن موسى بن جعفر بن محمد بن علي بن الحسين بن علي بن أبي طالب أبو القاسم المرتضى علم الهدى نقيب العلويين أخو الشريف الرضي ولد سنة خمس وخمسين وثلاث مائة وتوفي سنة ست وثلاثين وأربع مائة وكان فاضلا ماهرا أديبا متكلما له مصنفات جمة على مذهب الشيعة قال الخطيب كتبت عنه وكان رأسا في الاعتزال كثير الاطلاع والجدال قال ابن حزم في الملل والنحل ومن قول الإمامية كلها قديما وحديثا أن القرآن مبدل زيد فيه ونقص منه حاشا علي بن الحسين بن موسى وكان إماميا فيه تظاهر بالاعتزال ومع ذلك فإنه كان ينكر هذا) القول وكفر من قاله وكذلك صاحباه أبو يعلى الطوسي وأبو القاسم الرازي

Al-Sharif al-Murtada Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Ibrahim ibn Musa ibn Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu al-Qasim al-Murtada, Alam al-Huda, was the marshal (naqib) of the Alawids, the descendants of Ali, and the brother of al-Sharif al-Radi. He was born in the year 355 and died in the year 436. He was a distinguished and skilled scholar, a man of letters and a theologian, and he wrote many works according to the doctrine of the Shia. Al-Khatib said, "I wrote down reports from him. He was a leader in the Mutazilite school, with wide learning and a great deal of debate." Ibn Hazm said in al-Milal wa-l-Nihal, "It is the position of all the Imamis, past and present, that the Quran has been altered, that something was added to it and something was removed from it, except Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa. He was an Imami who made a show of Mutazilism. Even so, he rejected this claim and declared anyone who made it to be an unbeliever. So did his two companions, Abu Yala al-Tusi and Abu al-Qasim al-Razi."

n0013.caption: al-Jawhari, al-Sihah, vol.4, p.31
paragraphs: وتحريف الكلام عن مواضعه : تغييره . وتحريف القلم : قطه محرفا . ويقال : انحرف عنه وتحرف واحرورف ، أي مال وعدل .

Tahrif of speech from its places means changing it. Tahrif of the pen means cutting it at a slant. One says “inharafa from him,” “taharrafa,” and “ihrawrafa,” meaning that he inclined away and turned aside.

n0014.caption: Ibn Manzur, Lisan al-Arab, vol.9, p.43
paragraphs: وتَحْرِيفُ الكَلِم عن مواضِعِه : تغييره . والتحريف في القرآن والكلمة : تغيير الحرفِ عن معناه والكلمة عن معناها وهي قريبة الشبه كما كانت اليهود تُغَيِّرُ مَعانَي التوراة بالأَشباه ، فوصَفَهم اللَّه بفعلهم فقال تعالى : يُحَرِّفُون الكَلِمَ عن مواضعه .

To distort words away from their places is to change them. Distortion in the Qur'an and in a word means changing a letter away from its meaning, or a word away from its meaning, while keeping a close resemblance to it. The Jews used to change the meanings of the Torah in this way, by means of look-alikes. God described them by their deed in His words, "They distort words from their places."

n0017.caption: Qur'an 4:46
paragraphs: مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلْكَلِمَ عَن مَّوَاضِعِهِۦ وَيَقُولُونَ سَمِعْنَا وَعَصَيْنَا وَٱسْمَعْ غَيْرَ مُسْمَعٍۢ وَرَٰعِنَا لَيًّۢا بِأَلْسِنَتِهِمْ وَطَعْنًۭا فِى ٱلدِّينِ ۚ وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ قَالُوا۟ سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا وَٱسْمَعْ وَٱنظُرْنَا لَكَانَ خَيْرًۭا لَّهُمْ وَأَقْوَمَ وَلَٰكِن لَّعَنَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُفْرِهِمْ فَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا

mina alladhina hadu yuharrifuna al-kalima 'an mawadi'ihi wa-yaquluna sami'na wa-'asayna wa-isma' ghayra musma'in wa-ra'ina layyan bi-alsinatihim wa-ta'nan fi al-din, wa-law annahum qalu sami'na wa-ata'na wa-isma' wa-unzurna la-kana khayran lahum wa-aqwama wa-lakin la'anahumu Allahu bi-kufrihim fa-la yu'minuna illa qalilan

Among those who are Jews are some who distort words from their proper places. They say, “We hear and we disobey,” and “Hear, without being made to hear,” and “Ra'ina,” twisting their tongues and slandering the religion. Had they said, “We hear and we obey,” and “Hear,” and “Look at us,” it would have been better for them and more upright. But God has cursed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except a little.

n0020.caption: al-Khoei, al-Bayan, p.197
paragraphs: 1 - معنى التحريف : يطلق لفظ التحريف ويراد منه عدة معان على سبيل الاشتراك ، فبعض منها واقع في القرآن باتفاق من المسلمين ، وبعض منها لم يقع فيه باتفاق منهم أيضا ، وبعض منها وقع الخلاف بينهم . واليك تفصيل ذلك (1) : الأول : " نقل الشئ عن موضعه وتحويله إلى غيره " ومنه قوله تعالى : " من الذين هادوا يحرفون الكلم عن مواضعه 4 : 46 " . ولا خلاف بين المسلمين في وقوع مثل هذا التحريف في كتاب الله فإن كل من فسر القرآن بغير حقيقته ، وحمله على غير معناه فقد حرفه . وترى كثيرا من أهل البدع ، والمذاهب الفاسدة قد حرفوا القرآن بتأويلهم آياته على آرائهم وأهوائهم . وقد ورد المنع عن التحريف بهذا المعنى ، وذم فاعله في عدة من الروايات .

1. The meaning of tahrif. The word tahrif is used for several meanings as a shared term. Some of these meanings occur in the Qur'an by the agreement of the Muslims, some do not occur in it, also by their agreement, and about some of them the Muslims disagree. Here are the details.

The first meaning is “moving a thing from its place and turning it into something else.” To this belongs the saying of the Exalted, “Among those who are Jews are some who distort words from their places” 4:46. There is no disagreement among the Muslims that this kind of tahrif occurs in the Book of God. Anyone who explains the Qur'an other than according to its reality, and applies it to a meaning other than its own, has distorted it. You will see many people of innovation and of corrupt schools who have distorted the Qur'an by interpreting its verses to fit their own opinions and desires. The prohibition of tahrif in this sense, and the condemnation of the one who does it, have come down in a number of reports.

n0021.caption: al-Khoei, al-Bayan, p.200
paragraphs: الخامس : " التحريف بالزيادة بمعنى أن بعض المصحف الذي بأيدينا ليس من الكلام المنزل " . والتحريف بهذا المعنى باطل بإجماع المسلمين ، بل هو مما علم بطلانه بالضرورة . السادس : " التحريف بالنقيصة ، بمعنى أن المصحف الذي بأيدينا لا يشتمل على جميع القرآن الذي نزل من السماء ، فقد ضاع بعضه على الناس " . والتحريف بهذا المعنى هو الذي وقع فيه الخلاف فأثبته قوم ونفاه آخرون .

The fifth meaning is “tahrif by addition, meaning that part of the codex in our hands is not part of the revealed speech.” Tahrif in this sense is false by the consensus of the Muslims. Its falsity is in fact known by necessity.

The sixth meaning is “tahrif by omission, meaning that the codex in our hands does not contain all of the Qur'an that was sent down from heaven, so that some of it was lost to the people.” This is the sense of tahrif about which the disagreement occurred. One group affirmed it and others denied it.

n0026.caption: Qur'an 15:9
paragraphs: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا ٱلذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ
inna nahnu nazzalna al-dhikra wa-inna lahu la-hafizun
Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its guardians.

n0028.caption: al-Tabataba'i, al-Mizan, vol.12, p.107
paragraphs: فقد تبين مما فصلناه ان القرآن الذي أنزله الله على نبيه ﵌ ووصفه بأنه ذكر محفوظ على ما انزل مصون بصيانة الهية عن الزيادة والنقيصة والتغيير كما وعد الله نبيه فيه . وخلاصة الحجة ان القرآن أنزله الله على نبيه ووصفه في آيات كثيرة بأوصاف خاصة لو كان تغير في شئ من هذه الأوصاف بزيادة أو نقيصة أو تغيير في لفظ أو ترتيب مؤثر فقد آثار تلك الصفة قطعا لكنا نجد القرآن الذي بأيدينا واجدا لاثار تلك الصفات المعدودة على أتم ما يمكن وأحسن ما يكون فلم يقع فيه تحريف يسلبه شيئا من صفاته فالذي بأيدينا منه هو القرآن المنزل على النبي ﵌ بعينه فلو فرض سقوط شئ منه أو تغير في اعراب أو حرف أو ترتيب وجب ان يكون في أمر لا يؤثر في شئ من أوصافه كالاعجاز وارتفاع الاختلاف والهداية والنورية والذكرية والهيمنة على سائر الكتب السماوية إلى غير ذلك وذلك كآية مكررة ساقطة أو اختلاف في نقطة أو اعراب ونحوها .

What we have set out shows that the Qur'an which God sent down to his Prophet, and which he described as a preserved Reminder, remains as it was sent down. It is protected by divine safeguarding from addition, omission and alteration, as God promised his Prophet in it.

The summary of the argument is this. God sent the Qur'an down to his Prophet and described it in many verses with particular attributes. If any of these attributes had changed through addition, omission, or a change in a word or in an order that affects it, the traces of that attribute would certainly have been affected. Yet we find that the Qur'an in our hands carries the traces of those enumerated attributes to the fullest extent possible and in the best form. So no tahrif has occurred in it that strips it of any of its attributes. What we have of it is therefore the very Qur'an that was sent down to the Prophet.

If we suppose that something dropped out of it, or that a vowel ending, a letter or an order changed, then it must have been in a matter that affects none of its attributes. Those attributes include its inimitability, the absence of discrepancy in it, its guidance, its luminosity, its being a reminder, and its authority over the other heavenly books, and so on. An example is a repeated verse that dropped out, or a difference in a dot or a vowel ending, and the like.

n0033.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.2, p.634, no.28
paragraphs: 28 - علي بن الحكم ، عن هشام بن سالم (2) ، عن أبي عبد الله (﵇) قال : إن القرآن الذي جاء به جبرئيل (﵇) إلى محمد (﵌) سبعة عشر ألف آية (3) .
28. Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abd Allah, who said.
“The Qur'an that Gabriel brought to Muhammad was seventeen thousand verses.”

n0035.caption: al-Saduq, al-I'tiqadat, pp.86-87
paragraphs: بل نقول : إنه قد نزل الوحي الذي ليس بقرآن ، ما لو جمع إلى القرآن لكان مبلغه مقدار سبعة عشر ألف آية .
We say, moreover, that revelation has come down that is not Qur'an, and that if it were gathered together with the Qur'an, its total would amount to seventeen thousand verses.

n0037.caption: al-Majlisi in al-Milani, al-Tahqiq fi Nafy al-Tahrif, pp.86-88
paragraphs: 2 - الشيخ المجلسي في كتابه ( مرآة العقول ) فإنّه قال بعد حديث قال إنّه موثق : « ولا يخفى أنّ هذا الخبر وكثير من الأخبار الصحيحة صريحة في نقص القرآن وتغييره . وعندي أنّ الأخبار في هذا الباب متواترة معنىً ، وطرح جميعها يوجب رفع الاعتماد على الأخبار رأساً ، بل ظنّي أنّ الأخبار في هذا الباب لا تقصر عن أخبار الإمامة ، فكيف يثبتونها بالخبر » . ويردّه ما ذكره هو في « بحار الأنوار » وقد تقدّم نصّة . على أنّ قوله : « وكثير من الأخبار الصحيحة صريحة في نقص القرآن » غريب ، فإنّ السيد المرتضى قال : « نقلوا أخباراً ضعيفة ظنّوا صحتها لا يرجع بمثلها عن المعلوم المقطوع على صحته » . كما أنكر صحتها الطوسي شيخ الطائفة والمحدّث الكاشاني ، بل جاء في العبارة التي نقلناها عن بحاره « إنّ الأخبار التي جاءت بذلك أخبار آحاد لا يقطع على الله تعالى بصحّتها » . ومن قبلهم قال شيخ المحدّثين ما نصّه : « إعتقادنا أنّ القرآن الذين أنزله الله على نبيّه ﵌ هو ما بين الدفّتين وما في أيدي الناس ، ليس بأكثر من ذاك . . . ومن نسب إلينا أنّا نقول إنّه أكثر من ذلك فهو كاذب » . ولو كانت أحاديث النقيصة صحيحة ومقبولة لما قال الصدوق ذلك كما لا يخفى . وأما قوله : « وطرح جميعها يوجب رفع الاعتماد على الأخبار رأساً » ففيه : إنّ قبول جميعها أيضاً يوجب رفع الاعتماد على الأحاديث رأساً ، على أنّه رحمة الله قد حكم في أكثر الأحاديث المخرّجة في « الكافي » والمفيدة نقص القرآن إمّا بالضعف وإمّا بالإرسال ، كما تقدّم ذلك كلّه . ومن العجيب قوله : « بل ظنّي . . . » إذ إثبات الإمامية ليس دليلة منحصراً بالأحاديث حتى يقال ذلك ، وكيف أنّ تلك الأحاديث لا تقصر عن أحاديث الإمامة ؟ وهل يقصد الكثرة في الورود ؟ أو القوة في الدلالة ؟ أو الصحة في الأسانيد ؟

2. Al-Shaykh al-Majlisi, in his book Mir'at al-'Uqul, said after a hadith that he called reliable, "It is not hidden that this report and many sound reports are explicit about the diminution and alteration of the Quran. In my view the reports on this subject are mutawatir in meaning, and rejecting all of them would remove reliance on reports altogether. Rather, I think the reports on this subject fall no shorter than the reports on the Imamate, so how can they establish the Imamate by a report?" What he himself mentioned in Bihar al-Anwar refutes this, and its text has already been given.

Moreover, his statement "many sound reports are explicit about the diminution of the Quran" is strange, because al-Sayyid al-Murtada said, "They transmitted weak reports that they thought were sound, and one does not turn away from what is known and certain to be sound because of the like of these." Al-Tusi, the Shaykh of the sect, and the hadith scholar al-Kashani likewise denied their soundness. Indeed, the passage we quoted from his Bihar says, "The reports that came about this are solitary reports (ahad), and their soundness cannot be affirmed with certainty about God Most High." Before them, the Shaykh of the hadith scholars said, in these words, "Our belief is that the Quran which God sent down to His Prophet is what is between the two covers and in the hands of the people, and it is no more than that... Whoever attributes to us that we say it is more than that is a liar." Had the hadiths of diminution been sound and accepted, al-Saduq would not have said this, as is clear.

As for his statement "rejecting all of them would remove reliance on reports altogether," the reply is that accepting all of them would also remove reliance on hadiths altogether. Moreover, may God have mercy on him, he judged most of the hadiths cited in al-Kafi that indicate diminution of the Quran to be either weak or mursal, as all of that has been shown earlier. His statement "Rather, I think..." is also remarkable, since the proof of the Imamate is not confined to hadiths, so that this could be said. And how do those hadiths fall no shorter than the hadiths of the Imamate? Does he mean abundance in transmission, strength in indication, or soundness in the chains of transmission?

n0041.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.2, p.633, no.23
paragraphs: 23 - محمد بن يحيى ، عن محمد بن الحسين ، عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي هاشم ، عن سالم بن سلمة قال : قرأ رجل على أبي عبد الله (﵇) وأنا أستمع حروفا من القرآن ليس على ما يقرؤها الناس ، فقال أبو عبد الله (﵇) : كف عن هذه القراءة اقرأ كما يقرأ الناس حتى يقوم القائم فإذا قام القائم (﵇) قرأ كتاب الله ﷿ على حده وأخرج المصحف الذي كتبه علي (﵇) وقال : أخرجه علي (﵇) إلى الناس حين فرغ منه وكتبه فقال لهم : هذا كتاب الله ﷿ كما أنزله [الله] على محمد (﵌) وقد جمعته من اللوحين فقالوا : هو ذا عندنا مصحف جامع فيه القرآن لا حاجة لنا فيه ، فقال أما والله ما ترونه بعد يومكم هذا أبدا ، إنما كان علي أن أخبركم حين جمعته لتقرؤوه .
23. Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Salim ibn Salama, who said.

A man recited to Abu Abd Allah, while I was listening, some letters of the Qur'an that were not as the people recite them. Abu Abd Allah said, “Stop this recitation. Recite as the people recite until the Qa'im rises. When the Qa'im rises, he will recite the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, by itself, and he will bring out the codex that Ali wrote.”

And he said, “Ali brought it out to the people when he had finished it and written it. He said to them, ‘This is the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, as [God] sent it down to Muhammad, and I have gathered it from the two tablets.’ They said, ‘Here with us is a codex that contains the whole Qur'an, and we have no need of it.’ He said, ‘By God, you will never see it after this day of yours. It was only my duty to inform you, when I had gathered it, so that you would recite it.’”

n0044.caption: Imam al-Baqir, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.228, no.1
paragraphs: (باب) (انه لم يجمع القرآن كله الا الأئمة ﵈ وانهم) (يعلمون علمه كله) 1 - محمد بن يحيى ، عن أحمد بن محمد ، عن ابن محبوب ، عن عمرو بن أبي المقدام عن جابر قال : سمعت أبا جعفر ﵇ يقول : ما ادعى أحد من الناس أنه جمع القرآن كله كما أنزل إلا كذاب ، وما جمعه وحفظه كما نزله الله تعالى إلا علي بن أبي طالب ﵇ والأئمة من بعده ﵈ .
Chapter. That no one collected the whole Quran except the Imams, and that they know all of its knowledge.
1 - Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Jabir, who said that he heard Abu Ja'far say,

“No one among the people claims that he collected the whole Quran as it was sent down, except a liar. No one collected it and memorized it as God Most High sent it down except Ali ibn Abi Talib and the Imams after him.”

n0047.caption: Jabir, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.417, no.26
paragraphs: 26 - وبهذا الاسناد ، عن محمد بن سنان ، عن عمار بن مروان ، عن منخل ، عن جابر ، قال : نزل جبرئيل ﵇ بهذه الآية على محمد هكذا : " وإن كنتم في ريب مما نزلنا على عبدنا (في علي) فأتوا بسورة من مثله (3) " .
26 - Through this same chain, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Munakhkhal, from Jabir, who said,
Gabriel came down to Muhammad with this verse in this form, “If you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant (concerning Ali), then bring a surah like it.”

n0050.caption: al-Khoei, al-Bayan, p.226
paragraphs: والجواب : أن هذه الروايات لا دلالة فيها على وقوع التحريف في القرآن بالمعنى المتنازع فيه ، وتوضيح ذلك : أن كثيرا من الروايات ، وإن كانت ضعيفة السند ، فإن جملة منها نقلت من كتاب أحمد بن محمد السياري ، الذي اتفق علماء الرجال على فساد مذهبه ، وأنه يقول بالتناسخ ، ومن علي بن أحمد الكوفي الذي ذكر علماء الرجال أنه كذاب ، وأنه فاسد المذهب إلا أن كثرة الروايات تورث القطع بصدور بعضها عن المعصومين ﵈ ولا أقل من الاطمئنان بذلك ، وفيها ما روي بطريق معتبر فلا حاجة بنا إلى التكلم في سند كل رواية بخصوصها .

The answer is that these reports give no indication that distortion occurred in the Quran in the sense under dispute. To explain this, many of the reports have weak chains of transmission. A number of them were transmitted from the book of Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Sayyari, whose doctrine the scholars of biographical evaluation agreed was corrupt, and who held the belief in transmigration of souls. Others were transmitted from Ali ibn Ahmad al-Kufi, whom the scholars of biographical evaluation described as a liar with a corrupt doctrine. Nevertheless, the large number of reports produces certainty that some of them were issued by the infallible Imams, and at the very least it produces confidence in that. Among them are reports narrated through a reliable route. So we have no need to discuss the chain of each report individually.

n0051.caption: al-Muhammadi, Salamat al-Qur'an min al-Tahrif, p.120
paragraphs: لأن مجموع الروايات التي نقلها المحدث النوري - ويزعم أنها اختصت بكتب الإمامية - يصل إلى 1602 رواية موزعة على النحو الآتي : * 350 رواية ( يعنى حدود ثلث الروايات التي جمعها ) من كتاب القراءات لأحمد بن محمد السياري ، وهذا الكتاب لا قيمة له عند الإمامية ومؤلفه ضعيف الحديث عند الفريقين (2) .

The total of the reports that the hadith scholar al-Nuri transmitted, which he claims are particular to the books of the Imamis, reaches 1602 reports, distributed as follows. There are 350 reports, meaning about a third of the reports he collected, from the Book of Recitations by Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Sayyari. This book has no value among the Imamis, and its author is weak in hadith according to both groups.

n0052.caption: al-Najashi in al-Khoei, Mu'jam Rijal al-Hadith, vol.3, p.71
paragraphs: 874 - أحمد بن محمد بن سيار : = أحمد بن محمد البصري . = أحمد بن محمد السياري . قال النجاشي : " أحمد بن محمد بن سيار أبو عبد الله الكاتب بصري ، كان من كتاب آل طاهر ، في زمن أبي محمد ﵇ ، ويعرف بالسياري ، ضعيف الحديث ، فاسد المذهب - ذكر ذلك لنا : الحسين بن عبيد الله - مجفو الرواية ، كثير المراسيل ، له كتب ، وقع إلينا منها : كتاب ثواب القرآن ، كتاب الطب ، كتاب القراءات ، كتاب النوادر ، كتاب الغارات ، أخبرنا الحسين بن عبيد الله ، قال : حدثنا أحمد بن محمد بن يحيى ، عن أبيه ، قال : حدثني السياري ، إلا ما كان من غلو وتخليط " .

874. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar, who is also Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Basri and Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Sayyari. Al-Najashi said, "Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar, Abu Abd Allah the scribe, was from Basra. He was one of the secretaries of the Al Tahir in the time of Abu Muhammad, and he is known as al-Sayyari. He is weak in hadith and corrupt in doctrine, as al-Husayn ibn Ubayd Allah told us. His transmission is shunned, and he has many mursal reports. He has books, of which these reached us. The Book of the Reward of the Quran, the Book of Medicine, the Book of Recitations, the Book of Rare Reports, and the Book of the Raids. Al-Husayn ibn Ubayd Allah informed us and said, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us from his father, who said, al-Sayyari narrated to me, except for what contained exaggeration (ghuluw) and confusion."

n0056.caption: al-Tusi, al-Tibyan, vol.1, p.77
paragraphs: وأما الكلام في زيادته ونقصانه فمما لا يليق به أيضا ، لان الزيادة فيه مجمع على بطلانها والنقصان منه ، فالظاهر أيضا من مذهب المسلمين خلافه ، وهو الأليق بالصحيح من مذهبنا وهو الذي نصره المرتضى (ره) ، وهو الظاهر في الروايات غير أنه رويت روايات كثيره ، من جهة الخاصة والعامة ، بنقصان كثير من آي القرآن ، ونقل شئ منه من موضع إلى موضع ، طريقها الآحاد التي لا توجب علما ولا عملا ، والأولى الاعراض عنها ، وترك التشاغل بها ، لأنه يمكن تأويلها ولو صحت لما كان ذلك طعنا على ما هو موجود بين الدفتين ، فان ذلك معلوم صحته ، لا يعترضه أحد من الأمة ولا يدفعه ورواياتنا متناصرة بالحث على قراءته والتمسك بما فيه ، ورد ما يرد من اختلاف الاخبار في الفروع إليه .

The discussion of the Quran's increase and decrease is also unsuitable here. Increase in it is unanimously held to be invalid. As for decrease from it, the apparent position of the Muslims is the opposite. That is also the view more fitting for the sound position of our school, and it is the view that al-Murtada, may God have mercy on him, supported, and it is the apparent meaning of the reports.

Nevertheless, many reports have been narrated, from our own side (al-khassa) and from the general body of Muslims (al-'amma), that many verses of the Quran were diminished and that some of it was moved from one place to another. These reports come by solitary chains (ahad), which establish neither knowledge nor practice. It is better to turn away from them and to leave off occupying oneself with them, because they can be interpreted. Even if they were sound, that would not be a criticism of what exists between the two covers, because the soundness of that is known, no one in the community objects to it, and no one rejects it. Our reports agree in urging its recitation and holding fast to what is in it, and in referring back to it whatever differences arise among the reports on matters of detail.

n0059.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.69, no.5
paragraphs: 5 - محمد بن إسماعيل ، عن الفضل بن شاذان ، عن ابن أبي عمير ، عن هشام بن الحكم وغيره ، عن أبي عبد الله ﵇ قال : خطب النبي ﵌ بمنى فقال : أيها الناس ما جاء كم عني يوافق كتاب الله فأنا قلته وما جاء كم يخالف كتاب الله فلم أقله .
5 - Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam and others, from Abu Abd Allah, who said,

The Prophet gave a sermon at Mina and said, “O people, whatever comes to you from me that agrees with the Book of God, I said it. Whatever comes to you that contradicts the Book of God, I did not say it.”

n0060.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, Wasa'il al-Shi'a, vol.27, p.118, no.33362
paragraphs: (33362) 29 - سعيد بن هبة الله الراوندي في (رسالته) التي ألفها في أحوال أحاديث أصحابنا وإثبات صحتها ، عن محمد ، وعلي ابني علي بن عبد الصمد ، عن أبيهما ، عن أبي البركات علي بن الحسين ، عن أبي جعفر ابن بابويه ، عن أبيه ، عن سعد بن عبد الله عن أيوب بن نوح ، عن محمد ابن أبي عمير ، عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي عبد الله قال : قال الصادق (﵇) : إذا ورد عليكم حديثان مختلفان فاعرضوهما على كتاب الله ، فما وافق كتاب الله فخذوه ، وما خالف كتاب الله فردوه ، فإن لم تجدوهما في كتاب الله فاعرضوهما على أخبار العامة ، فما وافق أخبارهم فذروه ، وما خالف أخبراهم فخذوه .

(33362) 29. Sa'id ibn Hibat Allah al-Rawandi, in his treatise that he wrote on the conditions of the hadiths of our companions and the proof of their soundness, from Muhammad and Ali, the two sons of Ali ibn Abd al-Samad, from their father, from Abu al-Barakat Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Ja'far ibn Babawayh, from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abd Allah, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abd Allah, who said.

Al-Sadiq said, "When two differing hadiths reach you, present them to the Book of God. Take what agrees with the Book of God and reject what contradicts the Book of God. If you do not find them in the Book of God, present them to the reports of the general body of Muslims (al-'amma). Leave what agrees with their reports, and take what contradicts their reports."

n0063.caption: Imam al-Baqir, al-Kafi, vol.2, p.630, no.12
paragraphs: 12 - الحسين بن محمد ، عن علي بن محمد ، عن الوشاء ، عن جميل بن دراج ، عن محمد بن مسلم ، عن زرارة ، عن أبي جعفر (﵇) قال : إن القرآن واحد نزل من عند واحد ولكن الاختلاف يجيئ من قبل الرواة .
12 - al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far, who said,
“The Quran is one, sent down from One. But the disagreement comes from the side of the transmitters.”

n0064.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.2, p.630, no.13
paragraphs: 13 - علي بن إبراهيم ، عن أبيه ، عن ابن أبي عمير ، عن عمر بن أذينة ، عن الفضيل بن يسار قال : قلت لأبي عبد الله (﵇) : إن الناس يقولون : إن القرآن نزل على سبعة أحرف ، فقال : كذبوا أعداء الله ولكنه نزل على حرف واحد من عند الواحد (1) .
13 - Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said,
I said to Abu Abd Allah, “The people say that the Quran was sent down in seven ahruf.” He said, “The enemies of God have lied. Rather, it was sent down in one harf, from the One.”

n0065.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.2, p.631, no.15
paragraphs: 15 - عدة من أصحابنا ، عن سهل بن زياد ، عن علي بن الحكم ، ، عن عبد الله ابن جندب ، عن سفيان بن السمط قال : سألت أبا عبد الله (﵇) : عن تنزيل القرآن قال : اقرؤوا كما علمتم .
15 - A group of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abd Allah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Samt, who said,
I asked Abu Abd Allah about the sending down of the Quran. He said, “Recite as you were taught.”

n0069.caption: Ibn Mas'ud, Musnad Abi Ya'la, vol.8, p.470, no.5057
paragraphs: (5057) حدثنا أبو كريب حدثنا أبو بكر بن عياش عن عاصم عن زر عن عبد الله قال اختصم رجلان في سورة فقال هذا أقرأني رسول الله ﵌ وقال هذا أقرأني رسول الله فأتيا النبي ﵌ فأخبر بذلك قال فتغير وجهه فقال إقرؤوا كما علمتم فذكر فيه كلاما ثم قال فإنما هلك من كان قبلكم باختلافهم على أنبيائهم
(5057) Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Asim, from Zirr, from Abd Allah, who said,

Two men disputed over a surah. One said, “The Messenger of God taught me to recite it,” and the other said, “The Messenger of God taught me to recite it.” They came to the Prophet and he was told of this. He said that his face changed, and he said, “Recite as you were taught.”
Then he mentioned some words about it, and then said, “Those before you were destroyed only because of their disagreement with their prophets.”

n0072.caption: al-Tabataba'i, al-Mizan, vol.12, p.108
paragraphs: وكذا الاخبار التي تتضمن تمسك أئمة أهل البيت ﵈ بمختلف الآيات القرآنية في كل باب على ما يوافق القرآن الموجود عندنا حتى في الموارد التي فيها آحاد من الروايات بالتحريف وهذا أحسن شاهد على أن المراد في كثير من روايات التحريف من قولهم ﵈ كذا نزل هو التفسير بحسب التنزيل في مقابل البطن والتأويل . وكذا الروايات الواردة عن أمير المؤمنين وسائر الأئمة من ذريته ﵈ في إن ما بأيدي الناس قرآن نازل من عند الله سبحانه وان كان غير ما الفه علي ﵇ من المصحف ولم يشركوه ﵇ في التأليف في زمن أبى بكر ولا في زمن عثمان ومن هذا الباب قولهم ﵈ لشيعتهم : اقرؤوا كما قرء الناس ومقتضى هذه الروايات ان لو كان القرآن الدائر بين الناس مخالفا لما الفه علي ﵇ في شئ فإنما يخالفه في ترتيب السور أو في ترتيب بعض الآيات التي لا يؤثر اختلال ترتيبها في مدلولها شيئا ولا في الأوصاف التي وصف الله سبحانه بها القرآن النازل من عنده ما يختل به آثارها . فمجموع هذه الروايات على اختلاف أصنافها يدل دلالة قاطعة على أن الذي بأيدينا من القرآن هو القرآن النازل على النبي ﵌ من غير أن يفقد شيئا من أوصافه الكريمة وآثارها وبركاتها .

Likewise there are the reports that include the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt holding to various Qur'anic verses on every subject, in agreement with the Qur'an we have, even in the cases where there are isolated reports of alteration. This is the best evidence that what is meant in many of the alteration reports, in their saying "It was revealed thus," is explanation according to the revelation, as distinct from the inner meaning and the interpretation.

Likewise there are the reports from the Commander of the Faithful and the rest of the Imams from his descendants, saying that what is in the people's hands is a Qur'an sent down from God, Glorified, even though it differs from the codex that Ali compiled, and that they did not involve him in the compilation, either in the time of Abu Bakr or in the time of Uthman. To this category belongs their saying to their Shia, "Recite as the people recite." The implication of these reports is that if the Qur'an circulating among the people differs in anything from what Ali compiled, it differs only in the order of the surahs, or in the order of some verses whose disordering has no effect on their meaning. It does not differ in the attributes with which God, Glorified, described the Qur'an sent down from Him, so as to impair their effects.

So these reports taken together, despite their different kinds, indicate conclusively that the Qur'an in our hands is the Qur'an sent down upon the Prophet, without having lost any of its noble attributes, its effects, or its blessings.

n0076.caption: Qur'an 5:95
paragraphs: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَقْتُلُوا۟ ٱلصَّيْدَ وَأَنتُمْ حُرُمٌۭ ۚ وَمَن قَتَلَهُۥ مِنكُم مُّتَعَمِّدًۭا فَجَزَآءٌۭ مِّثْلُ مَا قَتَلَ مِنَ ٱلنَّعَمِ يَحْكُمُ بِهِۦ ذَوَا عَدْلٍۢ مِّنكُمْ هَدْيًۢا بَٰلِغَ ٱلْكَعْبَةِ أَوْ كَفَّٰرَةٌۭ طَعَامُ مَسَٰكِينَ أَوْ عَدْلُ ذَٰلِكَ صِيَامًۭا لِّيَذُوقَ وَبَالَ أَمْرِهِۦ ۗ عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَمَّا سَلَفَ ۚ وَمَنْ عَادَ فَيَنتَقِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِنْهُ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌۭ ذُو ٱنتِقَامٍ

ya ayyuha alladhina amanu la taqtulu al-sayda wa-antum hurumun, wa-man qatalahu minkum muta'ammidan fa-jaza'un mithlu ma qatala mina al-na'ami yahkumu bihi dhawa 'adlin minkum hadyan baligha al-ka'bati aw kaffaratun ta'amu masakina aw 'adlu dhalika siyaman li-yadhuqa wabala amrihi, 'afa Allahu 'amma salaf, wa-man 'ada fa-yantaqimu Allahu minhu, wa-Allahu 'azizun dhu intiqam

O you who believe, do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram. Whoever of you kills it intentionally, the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from the livestock, as two men of justice among you judge, as an offering reaching the Kaaba; or an expiation by feeding poor people; or the equivalent of that in fasting, so that he may taste the consequence of his deed. God has pardoned what is past. But whoever returns, God will take retribution from him. And God is Almighty, Lord of retribution.

n0078.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.8, p.205, no.247
paragraphs: 247 - علي بن إبراهيم ، عن أبيه ، عن ابن أبي عمير ، عن حماد بن عثمان قال : تلوت عند أبي عبد الله (﵇) " ذوا عدل منكم (2) " فقال " ذو عدل منكم " هذا مما أخطأت فيه الكتاب .
247. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said.
I recited in the presence of Abu Abd Allah, "two just men from among you."
He said, "'A just man from among you.' This is one of the things the scribes got wrong."

n0080.caption: al-Tabrisi, Majma' al-Bayan, vol.3, p.416
paragraphs: وروي في الشواذ قراءة أبي عبد الرحمن (فجزاء) منون (مثل) منصوب . وقراءة محمد بن علي الباقر ﵇ وجعفر بن محمد الصادق ﵇ : " يحكم به ذو عدل منكم " .

Among the irregular readings, there is reported the reading of Abu Abd al-Rahman, who read “penalty” with tanwin and “equivalent” in the accusative. There is also the reading of Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir and Jafar ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq, “A man of justice among you judges by it.”

n0082.caption: Imam al-Baqir, Tafsir al-Ayyashi, vol.1, p.351, no.200
paragraphs: 200 - عن زرارة قال : سمعت أبا جعفر ﵇ يقول : " يحكم به ذوا عدل منكم " قال : ذلك رسول الله ﵌ والامام من بعده ، فإذا حكم به الامام فحسبك
200 - From Zurara, who said,
I heard Abu Jafar say, “Two men of justice among you judge by it.” He said, “That is the Messenger of God and the Imam after him. When the Imam has judged by it, that is enough for you.”

n0084.caption: al-Mazandarani, Sharh Furu' al-Kafi, vol.5, p.199
paragraphs: ونسبة الخطأ إليهم لتعميمهم العدلين . هذا هو المشهور في تفسير هذا الكلام ، والأظهر أنّ المراد بالكتّاب نُسّاخ القرآن ، يعني أنّ المنزل كان ذو عدل بلفظ المفرد ، والتثنية من غلطهم .

The attribution of error to them is because they made the “two men of justice” general. This is the well-known view in the interpretation of this statement. The clearer view is that what is meant by the “scribes” is the copyists of the Qur’an. That is, what was revealed was “a man of justice” in the singular form, and the dual form comes from their mistake.

n0085.caption: al-Tabataba'i, Tafsir al-Bayan fi al-Muwafaqa bayn al-Hadith wa al-Qur'an, vol.3, p.336
paragraphs: أقول : لفظ الكتّاب بضم الكاف وتشديد التاء المنقوطة ، جمع كاتب يريدان ﵉ كتّاب المصحف
I say, the word al-kuttab, with a damma on the kaf and a doubled dotted ta, is the plural of katib (scribe). The two Imams, al-Baqir and al-Sadiq, mean the scribes of the codex (mushaf).

n0086.caption: al-Fayd al-Kashani, al-Wafi, vol.26, p.422
paragraphs: بيان : لعل المراد أنه أريد بذي العدل في الآية الإمام المعصوم ، وقد مضى في كتاب الحج .
Explanation. Perhaps what is meant is that the “man of justice” in the verse refers to the infallible Imam. This has already been covered in the Book of Pilgrimage.

n0087.caption: al-Gulpaygani, Taqrirat al-Hajj, vol.3, p.43
paragraphs: هذا مما أخطأت به الكتاب (1) . أقول : قوله ﵇ وكذا قول الباقر ﵇ : هذا مما أخطأت به الكتاب المراد من ذلك أن الألف في قوله تعالى " ذوا عدل " زيادة ، قد زاد الكتاب فيه خطأ والصحيح أنه ذو عدل بدون الألف والمراد بذي العدل هو النبي ﵆ أو الإمام الذي بعده . ولكن عن تفسير العياشي عن زرارة قال : سمعت أبا جعفر يقول : " يحكم به ذوا عدل منكم " قال : ذلك رسول الله ﵌ والإمام من بعده ، فإذا حكم به الإمام فحسبك (2) . فيظهر من الرواية أن التثنية في ذوا عدل صحيحة والمراد منهما السول والإمام صلوات الله عليهما وعلى آلهما

“This is one of the things in which the scribes made mistakes.” I say that his statement, and likewise the statement of al-Baqir, “This is one of the things in which the scribes made mistakes,” means that the alif in the words of the Most High, “two men of justice,” is an addition. The scribes added it by mistake, and the correct form is “a man of justice” without the alif. The “man of justice” means the Prophet, or the Imam after him.

But it is reported in the Tafsir of al-Ayyashi, from Zurara, who said, “I heard Abu Jafar say, ‘Two men of justice among you judge by it.’ He said, ‘That is the Messenger of God and the Imam after him. When the Imam has judged by it, that is enough for you.’” It appears from this report that the dual in “two men of justice” is correct, and that what is meant by the two is the Messenger and the Imam, may God’s blessings be upon them both and upon their family.

n0091.caption: Ibn Abbas, al-Mustadrak, vol.2, p.396
paragraphs: (حدثنا) أبو علي الحافظ أنبأ عبدان الأهوازي ثنا عمرو بن محمد الناقد ثنا محمد بن يوسف ثنا سفيان عن شعبة عن جعفر بن اياس عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس ﵄ في قوله تعالى لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم حتى تستأنسوا قال أخطأ الكاتب حتى تستأذنوا هذا حديث صحيح على شرط الشيخين ولم يخرجاه .

Abu Ali al-Hafiz narrated to us. Abdan al-Ahwazi informed us. Amr ibn Muhammad al-Naqid narrated to us. Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us. Sufyan narrated to us, from Shuba, from Jafar ibn Iyas, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas,
concerning the saying of the Most High, “Do not enter houses other than your own until you become at ease,” he said, “The scribe made a mistake. It is ‘until you ask permission.’”
This hadith is sound by the standard of the two Shaykhs, although they did not record it.

n0093.caption: Ibn Abbas, Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim, vol.8, pp.154-155, no.14560
paragraphs: [14560] حدثنا علي بن الحسين ، ثنا نصر بن علي ، أخبرني أبي عن شبل بن عباد عن قيس بن سعد ، عن عطاء عن ابن عباس : (اللَّه نُورُ السَّماواتِ والأَرْضِ مَثَلُ ( نُورِه ) * قال : هي خطأ من الكاتب هو أعظم من أن يكون نوره مثل نور المشكاة قال : مثل نور المؤمن كمشكاة .
[14560] Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us. Nasr ibn Ali narrated to us. My father informed me, from Shibl ibn Abbad, from Qays ibn Sad, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas,

“God is the Light of the heavens and the earth; the likeness of His light.” He said, “It is a mistake by the scribe. He is too great for His light to be like the light of a niche.” He said, “The likeness of the believer’s light is like a niche.”

n0095.caption: Abu Shahba, al-Madkhal, p.365, quoting Abu Hayyan
paragraphs: 1 - أن هذا القول غير صحيح في نسبته إلى ابن عباس وهو مدسوس عليه ، دسه الملاحدة والزنادقة ، قال أبو حيان ما نصه : إن من روى عن ابن عباس أنه قال ذلك فهو طاعن في الإسلام ملحد في الدين ، وابن عباس بريء من ذلك القول .

1. This statement is not correctly attributed to Ibn Abbas. It was falsely inserted into his words, and the heretics and the zindiqs inserted it. Abu Hayyan said, in these exact words, "Whoever reports from Ibn Abbas that he said this is attacking Islam and is a heretic in religion, and Ibn Abbas is innocent of that statement."

n0096.caption: Ibn Ashtah, in al-Suyuti, al-Itqan, vol.1, p.557
paragraphs: وقد أجاب ابن أشتة عن هذه الآثار كلّها بأنّ المراد أخطئوا في الاختيار ، وما هو الأولى لجمع الناس عليه من الأحرف السبعة ، لا أنّ الذي كتب خطأ خارج عن القرآن .

Ibn Ashtah answered all of these reports by saying that what is meant is that they made a mistake in choosing, from among the seven ahruf, the one that was best for bringing people together. He did not mean that what was written was an error lying outside the Quran.

n0097.caption: Ma'rifat, al-Tamhid fi Ulum al-Qur'an, vol.1, p.370
paragraphs: أمّا نفس المحتوى وصحّة ما تضمّنته من تبديل نصّ المصحف الشريف ، فهذا شيء لا نكاد نصدّقه البتة . لأنّه هوالتحريف الذي أجمعت الأُمّة الإسلاميّة على عدم تسرّبه إلى كتاب اللّه العزيز الحميد : «إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحافِظُونَ» . (5) فلابدّ من الأخذ في تأويلها إلى وجه معقول أو رفضها رأسا . (6)

As for the content itself, and the soundness of what it contains about altering the text of the noble Mushaf, this is something we can hardly ever believe. It is the very distortion that the Muslim community agreed has never seeped into the Book of God, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, "Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its guardians." (Quran 15:9) So one must either interpret these reports in some reasonable way or reject them outright.

n0102.caption: al-Layth, in al-Azhari, Tahdhib al-Lugha, vol.4, p.149
paragraphs: قال : وإنما سُمِّي المُصْحَفُ مُصْحَفاً لأنه أُصْحِفَ أي جعل جامعاً للصُّحُف المكتوبة بين الدَّفَّتَيْن .
He said that the mushaf is called a mushaf because it was "ushifa", meaning that it was made a collection of the written sheets between the two covers.

n0103.caption: al-Askari, al-Mushaf fi al-Riwayat wa al-Athar, p.10
paragraphs: إنّ المصحف اسم لكلّ كتاب مجلد قرآناً كان أم غير قرآن .
The mushaf is a name for every bound book, whether it is a Quran or not a Quran.

n0106.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.239, no.1
paragraphs: ثم سكت ساعة ثم قال : وإن عندنا لمصحف فاطمة ﵍ وما يدريهم ما مصحف فاطمة ﵍ ؟ قال : قلت : وما مصحف فاطمة ﵍ ؟ قال : مصحف فيه مثل قرآنكم هذا ثلاث مرات ، والله ما فيه من قرآنكم حرف واحد ، قال : قلت : هذا والله العلم قال : إنه لعلم وما هو بذاك .
Then he was silent for a while, and then he said, "We also have the Mushaf of Fatima. And what do they know of the Mushaf of Fatima?"
He said, "I said, 'And what is the Mushaf of Fatima?'"
He said, "It is a mushaf containing three times the like of this Quran of yours. By God, there is not a single letter of your Quran in it."
He said, "I said, 'This, by God, is knowledge.'"
He said, "It is knowledge, but it is not that."

n0107.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.240, no.2
paragraphs: 2 - عدة من أصحابنا ، عن أحمد بن محمد ، عن عمر بن عبد العزيز ، عن حماد بن عثمان قال : سمعت أبا عبد الله ﵇ يقول : تظهر الزنادقة في سنة ثمان وعشرين ومائة وذلك أني نظرت في مصحف فاطمة ﵍ ، قال : قلت : وما مصحف فاطمة ؟ قال : إن الله تعالى لما قبض نبيه ﵌ دخل على فاطمة ﵍ من وفاته من الحزن ما لا يعلمه إلا الله ﷿ فأرسل الله إليها ملكا يسلي غمها ويحدثها ، فشكت ذلك (1) إلى أمير المؤمنين ﵇ فقال : إذا أحسست بذلك وسمعت الصوت قولي لي فأعلمته بذلك فجعل أمير المؤمنين ﵇ يكتب كلما سمع حتى أثبت من ذلك مصحفا قال : ثم قال : أما إنه ليس فيه شئ من الحلال والحرام ولكن فيه علم ما يكون .
2. A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said that he heard Abu Abd Allah say,
"The heretics will appear in the year one hundred and twenty-eight, and that is because I looked in the Mushaf of Fatima."
He said, "I said, 'And what is the Mushaf of Fatima?'"

He said, "When God the Exalted took back His Prophet, there came upon Fatima, because of his death, a grief that only God the Mighty and Majestic knows. So God sent her an angel to console her in her sorrow and to speak with her. She complained of this to the Commander of the Believers, and he said, 'When you sense that and hear the voice, tell me.' She told him about it, and the Commander of the Believers began to write down everything he heard, until he had put together a mushaf from it."
He said, "Then he said, 'It contains nothing of the lawful and the unlawful, but it contains knowledge of what will happen.'"

n0108.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.240, no.3
paragraphs: 3 - عدة من أصحابنا ، عن أحمد بن محمد ، عن علي بن الحكم ، عن الحسين ابن أبي العلاء قال : سمعت أبا عبد الله ﵇ يقول : إن عندي الجفر الأبيض ، قال : قلت : فأي شئ فيه ؟ قال : زبور داود ، وتوراة موسى ، وإنجيل عيسى ، وصحف إبراهيم ﵈ والحلال والحرام ، ومصحف فاطمة ، ما أزعم أن فيه قرآنا ، وفيه ما يحتاج الناس إلينا ولا نحتاج إلى أحد حتى فيه الجلدة ، ونصف الجلدة ، وربع الجلدة وأرش الخدش .
3. A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Ala, who said that he heard Abu Abd Allah say,
"I have the White Jafr."
He said, "I said, 'And what is in it?'"

He said, "The Psalms of David, the Torah of Moses, the Gospel of Jesus, the scrolls of Abraham, the lawful and the unlawful, and the Mushaf of Fatima. I do not claim that it contains a Quran. It contains what people need from us, while we need nothing from anyone. It even contains the lash, the half lash, the quarter lash, and the compensation for a scratch."

n0112.caption: Imam Ali, al-Kafi, vol.1, p.64, no.1
paragraphs: فما نزلت على رسول الله ﵌ آية من القرآن إلا أقرأنيها وأملاها علي فكتبتها بخطي وعلمني تأويلها وتفسيرها وناسخها ومنسوخها ، ومحكمها ومتشابهها ، وخاصها وعامها ، ودعا الله أن يعطيني فهمها ، وحفظها ، فما نسيت آية من كتاب الله ولا علما أملاه علي وكتبته ، منذ دعا الله لي بما دعا ، وما ترك شيئا علمه الله من حلال ولا حرام ، ولا أمر ولا نهي كان أو يكون ولا كتاب منزل على أحد قبله من طاعة أو معصية إلا علمنيه وحفظته ، فلم أنس حرفا واحدا

No verse of the Quran was sent down to the Messenger of God except that he had me recite it and dictated it to me, and I wrote it in my own hand. He taught me its interpretation (ta'wil) and its explanation (tafsir), its abrogating and abrogated verses, its decisive and ambiguous verses, and its particular and general verses.

He prayed to God to give me understanding of it and memory of it. So I have not forgotten a verse of the Book of God, nor any knowledge that he dictated to me and I wrote down, since he prayed to God for me as he prayed.

He left nothing that God had taught him, whether permitted or forbidden, command or prohibition, what has been or what will be, or any book sent down to anyone before him, whether of obedience or of disobedience, except that he taught it to me and I memorized it. I did not forget a single letter.

n0115.caption: Imam Ali, al-Ihtijaj, vol.1, p.281
paragraphs: فلما توفي رسول الله ﵌ اشتغلت بدفنه والفراغ من شأنه ثم آليت يمينا (1) أني لا أرتدي إلا للصلاة حتى أجمع القرآن ففعلت ، ثم أخذته وجئت به فأعرضته عليهم قالوا : لا حاجة لنا به

When the Messenger of God died, I was occupied with burying him and finishing his affairs. Then I swore an oath that I would not put on my cloak except for prayer until I had collected the Quran, and I did so. Then I took it, brought it, and presented it to them.
They said, "We have no need of it."

n0118.caption: Imam Ali, Nahj al-Balagha, sermon 176, p.252
paragraphs: واعْلَمُوا أَنَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ هُوَ النَّاصِحُ الَّذِي لَا يَغُشُّ - والْهَادِي الَّذِي لَا يُضِلُّ والْمُحَدِّثُ الَّذِي لَا يَكْذِبُ
Know that this Quran is the adviser who does not deceive, the guide who does not lead astray, and the speaker who does not lie.

n0119.caption: Imam Ali, Nahj al-Balagha, sermon 156, p.219
paragraphs: وعَلَيْكُمْ بِكِتَابِ اللَّه - فَإِنَّه الْحَبْلُ الْمَتِينُ والنُّورُ الْمُبِينُ - والشِّفَاءُ النَّافِعُ والرِّيُّ النَّاقِعُ - والْعِصْمَةُ لِلْمُتَمَسِّكِ والنَّجَاةُ لِلْمُتَعَلِّقِ - لَا يَعْوَجُّ فَيُقَامَ ولَا يَزِيغُ فَيُسْتَعْتَبَ - ولَا تُخْلِقُه كَثْرَةُ الرَّدِّ ووُلُوجُ السَّمْعِ - مَنْ قَالَ بِه صَدَقَ ومَنْ عَمِلَ بِه سَبَقَ

Hold fast to the Book of God, for it is the firm rope and the clear light, the beneficial cure and the quenching drink, a protection for whoever holds to it and a rescue for whoever clings to it. It does not bend, so that it would need straightening, and it does not swerve, so that it would need to be turned back. Repeated recitation and constant hearing do not wear it out. Whoever speaks by it speaks truly, and whoever acts by it takes the lead.

n0123.caption: al-Dhahabi, Ma'rifat al-Qurra' al-Kibar, vol.1, p.208
paragraphs: وروى جماعة ، عن عمرو بن الصباح ، عن حفص الغاضري ، عن عاصم ، عن أبي عبد الرحمن ، عن علي بالقراءة . وذكر عاصم أنه لم يخالف أبا عبد الرحمن في شيء من قراءته ، وأن أبا عبد الرحمن لم يخالف عليا في شيء من قراءته .
A group transmitted from Amr ibn al-Sabbah, from Hafs al-Ghadiri, from Asim, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from Ali, concerning the recitation.
Asim mentioned that he never differed from Abu Abd al-Rahman in any part of his recitation, and that Abu Abd al-Rahman never differed from Ali in any part of his recitation.

n0124.caption: Hafs, in al-Dhahabi, Ma'rifat al-Qurra' al-Kibar, vol.1, p.208
paragraphs: ويروى عن حفص بن سليمان ، قال : قال لي عاصم : ما كان من القراءة التي قرأت بها على أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي ، فهي التي أقرأتك بها ، وما كان من القراءة التي أقرأت بها أبا بكر بن عياش ، فهي القراءة التي عرضتها على زرّ بن حبيش ، عن ابن مسعود .
It is reported from Hafs ibn Sulayman, who said.

Asim said to me, “Whatever recitation I recited to Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, that is the one I taught you. And whatever recitation I taught Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, that is the recitation I presented to Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ibn Masud.”

n0126.caption: the introduction to the Cairo printing, in al-Tabrizi, Tanzih al-Shi'a al-Ithnay Ashariyya, vol.1, p.41
paragraphs: تعريف بهذا المصحف الشريف كتب هذا المصحف وضبط على ما يوافق رواية حفص بن سليمان بن المغيرة الأسدي الكوفي بقراءة عاصم بن أبي النجود الكوفي التابعي ، عن أبي عبد الرحمن عبد الله بن حبيب السلمي ، عن عثمان بن عفان ، وعلي بن أبي طالب ﵇ ، وزيد بن ثابت ، وأبي بن كعب ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه (وآله) وسلم .

Introduction to this noble Quran codex. This codex was written and vocalized in agreement with the transmission of Hafs ibn Sulayman ibn al-Mughira al-Asadi al-Kufi, from the recitation of Asim ibn Abi al-Najud al-Kufi, a Follower, from Abu Abd al-Rahman Abd Allah ibn Habib al-Sulami, from Uthman ibn Affan, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Zayd ibn Thabit and Ubayy ibn Kab, from the Prophet.

n0129.caption: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, in Ibn Mihran, al-Mabsut, p.440
paragraphs: واختار أبو بكر بن عياش {عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ} خفيفة الراء أيضا . وهو من الحروف العشرة التي ذكرت أنه قال : " أنا أدخلتها من قراءة علي - ﵁ - في قراءة عاصم حتى استخلصت قراءته " . يعني قراءة علي بن أبي طالب ﵇ .

Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash also chose the reading "he acknowledged part of it" with a light ra. It is one of the ten readings concerning which I mentioned that he said, "I introduced them from the reading of Ali into the reading of Asim, until I had distilled his reading." He means the reading of Ali ibn Abi Talib.

n0130.caption: al-Shawkani, Fath al-Qadir, vol.2, p.183
paragraphs: قرأ حمزة والكسائي " فارقوا دينهم " وهي قراءة علي بن أبي طالب : أي تركوا دينهم وخرجوا عنه . وقرأ الباقون فرقوا بالتشديد إلا النخعي فإنه قرأ بالتخفيف .

Hamza and al-Kisai read “they parted from their religion,” which is also the reading of Ali ibn Abi Talib, meaning that they left their religion and went out from it. The other reciters read “they divided their religion,” with the doubled letter, except al-Nakhai, who read it with the light form.

n0135.caption: Zayd ibn Thabit, in al-Majlisi, Bihar al-Anwar, vol.89, pp.77-78
paragraphs: أقول : روى البخاري والترمذي في صحيحيهما وذكره في جامع الأصول في حرف التاء في باب ترتيب القرآن وتأليفه وجمعه ، عن زيد بن ثابت قال : أرسل إلى أبو بكر بعد مقتل أهل اليمامة فإذا عمر جالس عنده ، فقال أبو بكر : إن عمر جاءني فقال : إن القتل قد استحر يوم اليمامة بقراء القرآن ، وإني أخشى أن يستحر القتل بالقراء في كل المواطن ، فيذهب من القرآن كثير وإني أرى أن تذهب بجمع القرآن ، قال : قلت لعمر : وكيف أفعل شيئا لم يفعله رسول الله ﵌ فقال عمر : هو والله خير ، فلم يزل يراجعني في ذلك حتى شرح الله صدري للذي شرح له صدر عمر ، ورأيت في ذلك الذي رأي عمر ، قال زيد : فقال لي أبو بكر : إنك رجل شاب عاقل ، لا نتهمك ، قد كنت تكتب الوحي لرسول الله ﵌ فتتبع القرآن فأجمعه ، قال زيد : فوالله لو كلفني نقل جبل من الجبال ، ما كان أثقل على مما أمرني به من جمع القرآن . قال : قلت : كيف تفعلان شيئا لم يفعله رسول الله ؟ فقال أبو بكر : هو والله خير ، قال : فلم يزل أبو بكر يراجعني - وفي رواية أخرى فلم يزل عمر يراجعني - حتى شرح الله صدري للذي شرح له صدر أبي بكر قال : فتتبعت القرآن : أجمعه من الرقاع والعسب واللخاف وصدور الرجال حتى وجدت آخر سورة التوبة مع خزيمة أو أبي خزيمة الأنصاري لم أجدها مع أحد غيره " لقد جائكم رسول من أنفسكم عزيز عليه " خاتمة براءة . قال : فكانت الصحف عند أبي بكر حتى توفاه الله ثم عند عمر حتى توفاه الله ، ثم حفصة بنت عمر ، قال بعض الرواة : فيه اللخاف يعني الخزف ، قال في جامع الأصول : أخرجه البخاري والترمذي .

I say that al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi reported in their two Sahih collections, and it is also mentioned in Jami al-Usul under the letter ta, in the chapter on the arrangement, composition and collection of the Quran, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said

Abu Bakr sent for me after the killing of the people of Yamama, and Umar was sitting with him. Abu Bakr said, "Umar came to me and said, 'Killing has become fierce on the day of Yamama among the reciters of the Quran, and I fear that killing will become fierce among the reciters in every place, so that much of the Quran goes. I think you should go about the collection of the Quran.' I said to Umar, 'How can I do something the Messenger of God did not do?' Umar said, 'By God, it is good.' He kept going back to me about it until God opened my chest to what he had opened Umar's chest to, and I came to hold on that matter the view that Umar held."

Zayd said, "Abu Bakr then said to me, 'You are a young and intelligent man, and we do not suspect you. You used to write down the revelation for the Messenger of God, so seek out the Quran and collect it.'" Zayd said, "By God, if he had charged me with moving one of the mountains, it would not have been heavier on me than what he commanded me to do in collecting the Quran."

He said, "I said, 'How can you two do something the Messenger of God did not do?' Abu Bakr said, 'By God, it is good.'" He said, "Abu Bakr kept going back to me about it (in another narration, Umar kept going back to me) until God opened my chest to what he had opened Abu Bakr's chest to."

He said, "So I sought out the Quran, collecting it from scraps of parchment, palm stalks, thin stones (lakhaf) and the chests of men, until I found the end of Surat al-Tawba with Khuzayma, or Abu Khuzayma, the Ansari. I did not find it with anyone else, 'A messenger has come to you from among yourselves, it is grievous to him...', the closing verses of Bara'a." He said, "The sheets then remained with Abu Bakr until God took him, then with Umar until God took him, then with Hafsa, the daughter of Umar."
Some of the transmitters said that in this report lakhaf means pottery.
He said in Jami al-Usul that al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi transmitted it.

n0137.caption: Uthman, in al-Askari, al-Qur'an al-Karim wa Riwayat al-Madrasatayn, vol.1, p.211
paragraphs: في مسند أحمد بسنده عن ابن عباس أنه قال في حديثه عن الخليفة عثمان أنّه قال : إن رسول اللّه ( ص ) كان مما يأتي عليه الزمان ينزل عليه من السور ذوات العدد ، وكان إذا أنزل عليه الشيء يدعو بعض من يكتب عنده ، يقول : ضعوا هذا في السورة التي يذكر فيها كذا وكذا ، وينزل عليه الآيات فيقول : ضعوا هذه الآيات في السورة التي يذكر فيها كذا وكذا ، وينزل عليه الآية فيقول : ضعوا هذه الآية في السورة التي يذكر فيها كذا وكذا (9) .
In the Musnad of Ahmad, with its chain of transmission, from Ibn Abbas, who said in his report about the caliph Uthman that he said.

“Time would often pass for the Messenger of God while a number of surahs were being revealed to him. Whenever something was revealed to him, he would call one of those who wrote for him and say, ‘Put this in the surah in which such and such is mentioned.’ Verses would be revealed to him and he would say, ‘Put these verses in the surah in which such and such is mentioned.’ A verse would be revealed to him and he would say, ‘Put this verse in the surah in which such and such is mentioned.’”

n0140.caption: Imam Ali, Ibn Abi Dawud, Kitab al-Masahif, p.67, no.39
paragraphs: [ 39 ] حدثنا (39) عبد اللّه قال حدثنا سهل بن صالح قال قال حدثنا أبو داود ويعقوب قالا أخبرنا شعبة عن علقمة بن مرثد عن سويد بن غفلة قال قال علي في المصاحف لو لم يصنعه عثمان لصنعته [ قال أبو داود « * » عن رجل عن سويد ] .

[39] Abd Allah narrated to us, he said, Sahl ibn Salih narrated to us, he said, he said, Abu Dawud and Yaqub narrated to us, both said, Shuba informed us, from Alqama ibn Marthad, from Suwayd ibn Ghafala, who said.
Ali said about the codices, “If Uthman had not done it, I would have done it.”
[Abu Dawud said, from a man, from Suwayd.]

n0147.caption: al-Saduq, al-I'tiqadat, p.86
paragraphs: اعتقادنا أن القرآن الذي أنزله الله تعالى على نبيه محمد ﵌ هو ما بين الدفتين ، وهو ما في أيدي الناس ، ليس بأكثر من ذلك ، ومبلغ سوره عند الناس مائة وأربع عشرة سورة . وعندنا أن الضحى وألم نشرح سورة واحدة ، ولايلاف وألم تر كيف سورة واحدة (1) . ومن نسب إلينا أنا نقول إنه أكثر من ذلك فهو كاذب .

Our belief is that the Quran which God Almighty sent down to His Prophet Muhammad is what lies between the two covers, and it is what is in people's hands. It is not more than that. The number of its surahs among the people is one hundred and fourteen. We hold that al-Duha and Alam Nashrah are one surah, and that Li-Ilaf and Alam Tara Kayfa are one surah. Whoever attributes to us the claim that it is more than that is a liar.

n0150.caption: al-Mufid, al-Masa'il al-Sarawiyya, pp.78-79
paragraphs: المسألة التاسعة : صيانة القرآن من التحريف ما قولة - أدام الله تعالى حراسته (1) - في القرآن : أهو ما بين الدفتين ، الذي في أيدي الناس ، أم هل ضاع مما أنزل الله تعالى على نبيه منه شئ ، أم لا ؟ وهل هو ما جمعه أمير المؤمنين ﵇ ، أم ما جمعه عثمان بن عفان على ما يذكره المخالفون ؟ الجواب : لا شك (2) أن الذي بين الدفتين من القرآن جميعه (3) كلام الله تعالى وتنزيله ، وليس فيه شئ من كلام البشر ، وهو جمهور المنزل . والباقي مما أنزله (4) الله تعالى (5) عند المستحفظ للشريعة ، المستودع للأحكام ، لم يضع (1) منه شئ (2) . وإن كان الذي جمع ما بين الدفتين الآن لم يجعله في جملة ما جمع لأسباب (3) دعته إلى ذلك ، منها : قصوره عن معرفة بعضه . ومنها : شكه فيه وعدم تيقنه (4) . ومنها : ما تعمد إخراجه منه . وقد جمع أمير المؤمنين ﵇ القرآن المنزل من أوله إلى آخره ، وألفه بحسب ما وجب من تأليفه ، فقدم المكي على المدني ، والمنسوخ على الناسخ ، ووضع كل شئ منه في محله (5) . فلذلك قاد جعفر بن محمد الصادق ﵉ : " أما والله لو قرئ القرآن كما أنزل لألفيتمونا فيه مسمين كما سمي من كان قبلنا " (6) .

Ninth question, the protection of the Quran from alteration. What is the opinion of the shaykh, may God Almighty prolong his guardianship, about the Quran? Is it what lies between the two covers, which is in people's hands, or has some of what God Almighty sent down to His Prophet been lost, or not? And is it what the Commander of the Faithful collected, or what Uthman ibn Affan collected, as the opponents say?

The answer is that there is no doubt that what lies between the two covers, all of it, is the speech of God Almighty and His revelation, and that nothing in it is the speech of human beings. It is the majority of what was revealed. The rest of what God Almighty revealed is with the one entrusted to preserve the law and to whom the rulings are committed, and none of it has been lost. This is so even though the one who collected what lies between the two covers did not include it all in what he collected, for reasons that led him to that. Among them were his limited knowledge of some of it, his doubt about some of it and his lack of certainty about it, and his deliberate exclusion of some of it.

The Commander of the Faithful collected the revealed Quran from its beginning to its end and arranged it as its arrangement required. He placed the Meccan before the Medinan and the abrogated before the abrogating, and put everything in its proper place. For that reason Jafar ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq said, “By God, if the Quran were recited as it was revealed, you would find us named in it, just as those before us were named.”

n0151.caption: al-Mufid, al-Masa'il al-Sarawiyya, p.81
paragraphs: غير أن الخبر قد صح عن أئمتنا ﵈ أنهم أمروا بقراءة ما بين الدفتين ، وأن لا (1) يتعداه إلا زيادة فيه ولا نقصان منه حتى يقوم القائم ﵇ فيقرأ للناس (2) القرآن على ما أنزله الله تعالى وجمعه أمير المؤمنين ﵇ (3) .

However, the report has been established as sound from our Imams that they commanded the recitation of what lies between the two covers, and that one should not go beyond it, whether by adding to it or by subtracting from it, until the Riser rises and recites to the people the Quran as God Almighty revealed it and as the Commander of the Faithful collected it.

n0152.caption: al-Mufid, Awa'il al-Maqalat, pp.82-83
paragraphs: وأما النقصان فإن العقول لا تحيله ولا تمنع من وقوعه ، وقد امتحنت مقالة من ادعاه ، وكلمت عليه المعتزلة وغيرهم طويلا فلم اظفر منهم بحجة اعتمدها في فساده . وقد قال جماعة من أهل الإمامة إنه لم ينقص من كلمة ولا من آية ولا من سورة ولكن حذف ما كان مثبتا في مصحف أمير المؤمنين ( ع ) من تأويله وتفسير معانيه على حقيقة تنزيله وذلك كان ثابتا منزلا وإن لم يكن من جملة كلام الله تعالى الذي هو القرآن المعجز ، وقد يسمى تأويل القرآن قرآنا قال الله تعالى : ( ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه وقل رب زدني علما ) فسمى تأويل القرآن قرآنا ، وهذا ما ليس فيه بين أهل التفسير اختلاف . وعندي أن هذا القول أشبه من مقال من ادعى نقصان كلم من نفس القرآن على الحقيقة دون التأويل ، وإليه أميل والله أسأل توفيقه للصواب . وأما الزيادة فيه فمقطوع على فسادها من وجه ويجوز صحتها من وجه ، فالوجه الذي أقطع على فساده أن يمكن لأحد من الخلق زيادة مقدار سورة فيه على حد يلتبس به عند أحد من الفصحاء ، وأما الوجه المجوز فهو أن يزاد فيه الكلمة والكلمتان والحرف والحرفان وما أشبه ذلك مما لا يبلغ حد الاعجاز ، ويكون ملتبسا عند أكثر الفصحاء بكلم القرآن ، غير أنه لا بد متى وقع ذلك من أن يدل الله عليه ، ويوضح لعباده عن الحق فيه ، ولست أقطع على كون ذلك بل أميل إلى عدمه وسلامة القرآن عنه ، ومعي بذلك حديث عن الصادق جعفر بن محمد (ع) ، وهذا المذهب بخلاف ما سمعناه عن بني نوبخت - ﵏ - من الزيادة في القرآن والنقصان فيه ، وقد ذهب إليه جماعة من متكلمي الإمامية وأهل الفقه منهم والاعتبار .

As for omission, reason does not rule it out or prevent it from happening. I have examined the claim of those who asserted it, and I have spoken at length about it with the Mu'tazila and others, but I found in them no argument that I could rely on to show it false. A group of the Imamis have said that no word, verse or chapter was left out. What was removed, they say, is what had been written in the codex of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, namely its interpretation and the explanation of its meanings according to the truth of its revelation. That material was established and sent down, even though it was not part of the speech of God Most High that is the inimitable Quran.

The interpretation of the Quran can also be called Quran. God Most High said, "Do not hasten with the Quran before its revelation is completed to you, and say, 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge.'" So He called the interpretation of the Quran "Quran," and the scholars of exegesis do not disagree about this. In my view this position is closer to the truth than the statement of those who claimed that actual words were lost from the Quran itself, rather than from its interpretation. I incline toward it, and I ask God for success in reaching what is correct.

As for addition to the Quran, one kind is certainly false and another kind is possible. The kind I am certain is false is that any human being could add the length of a chapter to it in such a way that it would be confused with the Quran in the judgment of any eloquent speaker. The kind that is possible is that a word or two words, or a letter or two letters, or something similar that does not reach the level of inimitability, was added to it and was mistaken for Quranic words by most eloquent speakers. Even so, if that had happened, God would necessarily have pointed it out and made the truth about it clear to His servants. I am not certain that it happened. I incline instead toward its not having happened and toward the Quran being free of it, and I have a report from al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, that supports this.

This position differs from what we heard from the Banu Nawbakht, may God have mercy on them, about addition to the Quran and omission from it. A group of Imami theologians, including their jurists and scholars of reflection, have held to it.

n0156.caption: al-Murtada, al-Dhakhira, pp.361-362
paragraphs: فان قيل : كيف يكون أحد الامرين كالآخر والامامية تدّعي تغييرا في القرآن ونقصانا ، وكذلك حشوية أصحاب الحديث ؟ قلنا : قد بيّنا صحة نقل القرآن في المسائل الطرابلسيات (3) ، وأنه غير منقوص ولا مبدّل ولا مغيّر ، وأن العلم بأن هذا القرآن الذي في أيدينا هو الذي ظهر على يد رسول اللّه « ص » كالعلم بالبلدان والحوادث الكبار والوقائع العظام ، والكتب المصنفة المشهورة ، والاشعار المدونة . وذكرنا أن العناية اشتدت بالقرآن والدواعي توفرت على نقله وحراسته وبلغت إلى حدّ لم يبلغه في نقل الحوادث والوقائع والكتب المصنفة ، لأن القرآن معجز النبوة ، وأصل العلم بالشريعة والاحكام الدينية . وكل شيء دعا إلى نقل جميع ما تقدم حاصل فيه ، ويستبدّ بدواع إلى النقل ليست في الحوادث وما أشبهها ، وأن علماء المتكلمين بلغوا في ضبطه وحمايته ، وان عرفوا كل شيء اختلف (1) فيه من اعرابه والقراءات المختلفة في حروفه حتى فرّقوا بين ما روي وعرف ، وبين ما لم يذكر ولم يسطر . فكيف يجوز أن يكون مغيّرا أو منقوصا مع هذه العناية الصادقة والضبط الشديد ؟

If it is asked how one of the two matters can be like the other, when the Imamis claim alteration and diminution in the Quran, and so do the Hashwiyya among the hadith folk, we say that we have already explained the soundness of the transmission of the Quran in al-Masa'il al-Tarabulusiyyat. We showed that it is not diminished, replaced, or altered. We also showed that knowledge that this Quran in our hands is what appeared at the hands of the Messenger of God is like knowledge of countries, great events, major incidents, famous compiled books, and recorded poems.

We mentioned also that care for the Quran was intense, and that the motives to transmit and guard it were abundant, to a degree not reached in the transmission of events, incidents, and compiled books. The reason is that the Quran is the miracle that proves prophethood and the foundation of knowledge of the Law and of religious rulings. Everything that prompted the transmission of all those earlier things is present in it, and it alone has motives for transmission that events and the like do not have. The scholars among the theologians went so far in preserving and protecting it that they even knew everything disputed in it, such as its grammatical inflection and the different readings of its letters, until they distinguished between what was narrated and known and what was not mentioned or written down. So how can it be altered or diminished, given this genuine care and strict preservation?

n0159.caption: al-Tabrisi, Majma' al-Bayan, vol.1, pp.42-43
paragraphs: ومن ذلك : الكلام في زيادة القرآن ونقصانه فإنه لا يليق بالتفسير . فأما الزيادة فيه : فمجمع على بطلانه . وأما النقصان منه : فقد روى جماعة من أصحابنا ، وقوم من حشوية العامة ، أن في القرآن تغييرا أو نقصانا ، والصحيح من مذهب أصحابنا خلافه

Of this kind is the discussion of increase and decrease in the Quran, which is unsuitable for exegesis. As for increase in it, its invalidity is unanimously agreed. As for decrease from it, a group of our companions and a group of the Hashwiyya of the general body of Muslims (al-'amma) have narrated that the Quran contains alteration or diminution. The sound position of our companions is the opposite.

n0162.caption: al-Khoei, al-Bayan, p.259
paragraphs: ومما ذكرناه : قد تبين للقارئ أن حديث تحريف القرآن حديث خرافة وخيال ، لا يقول به إلا من ضعف عقله ، أو من لم يتأمل في أطرافه حق التأمل ، أو من ألجأه إليه يجب القول به . والحب يعمي ويصم ، وأما العاقل المنصف المتدبر فلا يشك في بطلانه وخرافته .

From what we have mentioned, it has become clear to the reader that the talk of the Qur'an's alteration is a superstitious tale and a fantasy. No one holds it except one whose reason is weak, or one who has not reflected on its aspects with the reflection they deserve, or one whom love of holding the view drives to it. Love blinds and deafens. But the sensible, fair-minded person who reflects has no doubt that it is false and a superstitious tale.

n0165.caption: al-Khomeini, Anwar al-Hidaya, vol.1, pp.207-208
paragraphs: أمّا الأولى : فلمنع وقوع التحريف فيه جدّاً ، كما هو مذهب المحقّقين من علماء العامّة والخاصّة ، والمعتبرين من الفريقين ، وإن شئت شطراً من الكلام في هذا المقام فارجع إلى مقدّمة تفسير آلاء الرحمن للعلّامة البلاغي المعاصر ﵋ (2) . وأزيدك توضيحاً : أنّه لو كان الأمر كما توهّم صاحب «فصل الخطاب» الذي كان كتبه لا يفيد علماً ولا عملًا ، وإنّما هو إيراد روايات أعرض عنها الأصحاب ، واختلاط ضعاف بين الروايات بعد تنزيهها عنها أولو الألباب من قدماء أصحابنا كالمحمّدين الثلاثة المتقدّمين ﵏ . هذا حال كتب روايته غالباً ك «المستدرك» ، ولا تسأل عن سائر كتبه المشحونة بالقصص والحكايات الغريبة التي غالبها بالهزل أشبه منه بالجدّ ، وهو ﵀ شخص صالح متتبّع ، إلّاأنّ اشتياقه لجمع الضعاف والغرائب والعجائب وما لا يقبلها العقل السليم والرأي المستقيم ، أكثر من الكلام النافع ، والعجب من معاصريه من أهل اليقظة ! كيف ذهلوا وغفلوا حتّى وقع ما وقع ممّا بكت عليه السماوات ، وكادت تتدكدك على الأرض ؟ ! وبالجملة : لو كان الأمر كما ذكره هذا وأشباهه ، من كون الكتاب الإلهي مشحوناً بذكر أهل البيت وفضلهم ، وذكر أمير المؤمنين وإثبات وصايته وإمامته ، فلِمَ لم يحتجّ بواحد من تلك الآيات النازلة والبراهين القاطعة من الكتاب الإلهي أميرُالمؤمنين ، وفاطمة ، والحسن ، والحسين ﵈ وسلمان ، وأبوذرّ ، ومقداد ، وعمّار ، وسائر الأصحاب الذين لا يزالون يحتجّون على خلافته ﵇ (1) ؟ ! ولمَ تشبّث ﵇ بالأحاديث النبوية (2) ، والقرآن بين أظهرهم ؟ !

As for the first, it is because the occurrence of distortion in it is utterly ruled out, as is the position of the verifying scholars among the general body of Muslims (al-'amma) and the particular group, and of the reliable authorities of both camps. If you want a portion of the discussion on this point, turn to the introduction of the Quran commentary Ala al-Rahman by the great contemporary scholar al-Balaghi. I add a further clarification for you. If the matter were as the author of Fasl al-Khitab imagined, whose books give neither knowledge nor practical benefit, and are only a presentation of reports that the associates turned away from, and a mixing of weak reports among the reports, after people of understanding among our early scholars, such as the three earlier Muhammads, had cleared them of these weak ones.

This is the condition of his books of narration for the most part, such as al-Mustadrak. Do not ask about the rest of his books, which are crammed with strange stories and tales, most of which resemble jest more than earnest. He was a righteous and diligent researcher, except that his eagerness to gather weak, strange and wondrous reports, which sound reason and upright judgment do not accept, was greater than his eagerness for useful discourse. It is astonishing that his contemporaries among the people of alertness were so stunned and heedless that what happened did happen, the thing over which the heavens wept and almost crumbled onto the earth!

In short, if the matter were as he and his like have stated, that the divine Book is crammed with mention of the Ahl al-Bayt and their merit, and with mention of the Commander of the Faithful and proof of his designation as successor and his imamate, then why did none of those revealed verses and decisive proofs from the divine Book get cited as argument by the Commander of the Faithful, Fatima, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, or by Salman, Abu Dharr, al-Miqdad, Ammar, and the rest of the Companions who kept arguing for his caliphate? And why did he hold fast to the prophetic traditions while the Quran was in their midst?

n0167.caption: al-Sistani, Istifta'at, p.131, no.489
paragraphs: 489 . السؤال : لقد قرأت كثيرا في ما ينشر على الانترنت عن موضوع تحريف القرآن ، حيث ينسبونه إلى الشيعة ويستدلون بأدلة من المذهب الشيعي ، فلا أعلم مدى صحة هذه الأقاويل ؟ الجواب : دعوى باطلة أجيب عليها من قبل علماء الشيعة مرات عديدة وهم يكررون القول الباطل وعقيدتنا أن القرآن المنزل من الله تعالى على النبي الأكرم - ﵌ - هو نفس القرآن الموجود لدى المسلمين حاليا من دون زيادة ولا نقيصة .

489. Question. I have read a great deal of what is published on the internet about the subject of the distortion of the Qur'an. They attribute it to the Shia and cite evidence from the Shia school, and I do not know how valid these claims are.

Answer. It is a false claim. Shia scholars have answered it many times, yet they keep repeating the false statement. Our belief is that the Qur'an sent down by God Almighty upon the Noble Prophet is the very Qur'an that Muslims have today, without addition or deficiency.

n0170.caption: al-Fayd al-Kashani, al-Safi, vol.1, p.52
paragraphs: أقول : المستفاد من مجمع هذه الأخبار وغيرها من الروايات من طريق أهل البيت (عيهم السلام) إن القرآن الذي بين أظهرنا ليس بتمامه كما انزل على محمد (﵌) منه ما هو خلاف ما أنزل الله ومنه ما هو مغير ومحرف وإنه قد حذف عنه أشياء كثيرة منها اسم علي (﵇) في كثير من المواضع ومنها غير ذلك وأنه ليس أيضا على الترتيب المرضي عند الله وعند رسوله (﵌) .

I say. What is gathered from the whole of these reports and from other narrations by way of the Ahl al-Bayt is that the Qur'an among us is not complete as it was sent down to Muhammad. Part of it is contrary to what God sent down, and part of it is altered and distorted. Many things have been removed from it, among them the name of Ali in many places, and other things besides. It is also not in the order that is pleasing to God and to His Messenger.

n0171.caption: al-Fayd al-Kashani, al-Safi, vol.1, p.54
paragraphs: أقول : ويرد على هذا كله إشكال وهو أنه على هذا التقدير لم يبق لنا اعتماد على شئ من القرآن إذ على هذا يحتمل كل آية منه أن يكون محرفا ومغيرا ويكون على خلاف ما أنزل الله فلم يبق لنا في القرآن حجة أصلا فتنتفي فائدته وفائدة الأمر باتباعه والوصية بالتمسك به إلى غير ذلك ، وأيضا قال الله ﷿ : وإنه لكتاب عزيز لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه . وقال : إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون فكيف يتطرق إليه التحريف والتغيير ، وأيضا قد استفاض عن النبي (﵌) والأئمة (﵈) حديث عرض الخبر المروي على كتاب الله ليعلم صحته بموافقته له وفساده بمخالفته فإذا كان القرآن الذي بأيدينا محرفا فما فائدة العرض مع أن خبر التحريف مخالف لكتاب الله مكذب له فيجب رده والحكم بفساده أو تأويله .

I say that an objection arises against all of this. On this assumption, we are left with nothing in the Quran that we can rely on. For on this view every verse in it could be altered and changed, and could differ from what God sent down. Then nothing in the Quran would remain a proof for us at all, so its benefit would be lost. The benefit of the command to follow it and of the instruction to hold fast to it would be lost too, and so on.

Also, God, mighty and majestic, said, "And it is indeed a mighty Book. Falsehood cannot come at it from before it or from behind it." And He said, "It is We who sent down the Reminder, and it is We who will guard it." So how could alteration or change reach it?

Also, the hadith about presenting a transmitted report to the Book of God is widely reported from the Prophet and the Imams. By it, the soundness of a report is known through its agreement with the Book, and its falseness through its disagreement. If the Quran in our hands were altered, what would be the use of this presentation? Moreover, the report of alteration contradicts the Book of God and denies it. So it must be rejected and judged false, or else interpreted.

n0172.caption: al-Fayd al-Kashani, al-Safi, vol.1, p.55
paragraphs: ولا يبعد أيضا أن يقال إن بعض المحذوفات كان من قبيل التفسير والبيان ولم يكن من أجزاء القرآن فيكون التبديل من حيث المعنى أي حرفوه وغيروه في تفسيره وتأويله أعني حملوه على خلاف ما هو به ، فمعنى قولهم (﵈) كذا نزلت أن المراد به ذلك لا أنها نزلت مع هذه الزيادة في لفظها فحذف منها ذلك اللفظ .

It is also not far-fetched to say that some of the omitted material was explanation and clarification, and was not part of the Quran. In that case the substitution is in the meaning. That is, they altered and changed the Quran in its explanation and interpretation, by which I mean they applied it contrary to what it really means. So the saying of the Imams, "It was revealed thus," means that the intended sense is that one. It does not mean that the verse was revealed with this addition in its wording, and that this wording was then removed from it.

n0173.caption: al-Fayd al-Kashani, al-Safi, vol.1, p.58
paragraphs: أقول : يكفي في وجوده في كل عصر وجوده جميعا كما أنزله الله محفوظا عند أهله ووجود ما احتجنا إليه منه عندنا وإن لم نقدر على الباقي كما أن الإمام (﵇) كذلك فان الثقلين سيان في ذلك .

I say, for its existence in every age it is enough that all of it exists, just as God sent it down, preserved with its people, and that what we need of it is with us, even if we are unable to reach the rest. The Imam is the same in this respect, for the two weighty things are alike in that.

blocks.text: The Preserved Qur'an

Imami scholars from al-Saduq to al-Sistani hold that the Qur'an between the two covers is the Qur'an God sent down. Imami books carry reports of loss, and Sunni books carry reports of scribal error. Al-Tusi classed the Imami reports as solitary, and Sunni scholars graded the Sunni reports sound, interpreted them or rejected them. Scholars of both schools disputed what the reports show.
# The Preserved Qur'an

**Premise 1.** Ibn Hazm charged the Imamiyya with holding that the Qur'an was changed, with words added and many removed. He exempted one Imami and two companions. Al-Safadi quotes the charge in his entry on al-Sharif al-Murtada. His quotation names the exempted man Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa, which is al-Murtada's name.
**Premise 2.** The Qur'an uses tahrif for moving words from their places and meanings. Al-Khoei names the loss of revealed text as the sense of tahrif that Muslims dispute.

**Premise 3.** Al-Kafi carries reports of a larger revelation and of verses Jibril brought "in this form" with a name added. It also carries a report of a scribal error in Qur'an 5:95. Sunni books carry reports in which Ibn Abbas calls words of the codex a scribe's error.

**Premise 4.** The Imams ﵈ told their followers to judge reports by the Qur'an. They also told them to recite as the people recite until al-Qa'im rises. Al-Tusi classes the reports of loss as solitary reports, which yield neither certain knowledge nor grounds for action.

**Premise 5.** Al-Saduq, al-Murtada, al-Khoei, al-Tabataba'i, al-Khomeini and al-Sistani hold that the Qur'an in Muslim hands is the Qur'an God sent down. Al-Tabrisi calls that the sound view of the school, and al-Tusi calls it the view more fitting for the sound position of his school. Al-Majlisi, and al-Fayd al-Kashani in al-Safi, read some reports as evidence of loss.

**Conclusion.** Imami scholars including al-Saduq, al-Murtada, al-Khoei, al-Tabataba'i, al-Khomeini and al-Sistani affirm the received Qur'an, and some Imami scholars accepted reports of omission. Sunni books carry reports of scribal error, which Sunni scholars accepted, interpreted or rejected. Al-Tusi classed the Imami reports of loss as solitary, and scholars of both schools disputed what the reports show. Ibn Hazm's charge presents that dispute as the doctrine of the Imamiyya.

## The Charge Ibn Hazm Recorded
- **Source:** Ibn Hazm, al-Fisal fi al-Milal wa al-Ahwa' wa al-Nihal, vol.4, p.182; al-Safadi, al-Wafi bil-Wafayat, vol.21, pp.2-3
- **Speaker:** Ibn Hazm al-Andalusi (d.456 AH); Salah al-Din al-Safadi (d.764 AH)
- **Claim:** all Imamiyya hold the Qur'an was altered, except one named Imami and his two companions

Ibn Hazm, an Andalusian scholar, surveys religions and sects in al-Fisal. He attributes the view of an altered Qur'an to all the Imamiyya, the Imami Shia, early and late. He exempts one Imami with Mu'tazili leanings. The printed al-Fisal names him Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Musa and traces his descent to Musa ibn Ja'far. Ibn Hazm reports that this man rejected the view and called its holders unbelievers. He reports the same of two companions, Abu Ya'la Milad al-Tusi and Abu al-Qasim al-Razi.

Al-Safadi, a biographer of the eighth century AH, quotes this passage in his entry on al-Sharif al-Murtada. The entry opens with al-Murtada's lineage, Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa, traced to Musa ibn Ja'far. In the quotation, Ibn Hazm exempts a man of that same name, so al-Safadi treats the exempted man as al-Murtada. The printed al-Fisal gives the lineage in a different form. It has al-Hasan where al-Safadi has al-Husayn, at the start and near the end of the chain. It also lacks one Musa between Muhammad and Ibrahim. The identification of the exempted man with al-Murtada therefore rests on al-Safadi's quotation of Ibn Hazm.
## What Tahrif Means
- **Source:** al-Jawhari, al-Sihah, vol.4, p.31; Ibn Manzur, Lisan al-Arab, vol.9, p.43
- **Speaker:** two classical lexicographers
- **Claim:** tahrif of speech is changing it, and the Qur'an uses the verb for changing meanings

Al-Jawhari defines the tahrif of speech as changing it from its places. Ibn Manzur says the Jews changed the meanings of the Torah by look-alikes. He quotes the Qur'an's words "they distort words from their places", which occur in Qur'an 4:46 and 5:13.
- **Verse:** Qur'an 4:46
- **Claim:** some of the Jews distort words from their places
