paragraphs.text: 3 - عدة من أصحابنا ، عن أحمد بن محمد ، عن علي بن الحكم ، عن الحسين ابن أبي العلاء قال : سمعت أبا عبد الله ﵇ يقول : إن عندي الجفر الأبيض ، قال : قلت : فأي شئ فيه ؟ قال : زبور داود ، وتوراة موسى ، وإنجيل عيسى ، وصحف إبراهيم ﵈ والحلال والحرام ، ومصحف فاطمة ، ما أزعم أن فيه قرآنا ، وفيه ما يحتاج الناس إلينا ولا نحتاج إلى أحد حتى فيه الجلدة ، ونصف الجلدة ، وربع الجلدة وأرش الخدش .
3. A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Ala, who said that he heard Abu Abd Allah say,
"I have the White Jafr."
He said, "I said, 'And what is in it?'"

He said, "The Psalms of David, the Torah of Moses, the Gospel of Jesus, the scrolls of Abraham, the lawful and the unlawful, and the Mushaf of Fatima. I do not claim that it contains a Quran. It contains what people need from us, while we need nothing from anyone. It even contains the lash, the half lash, the quarter lash, and the compensation for a scratch."

paragraphs.text: فما نزلت على رسول الله ﵌ آية من القرآن إلا أقرأنيها وأملاها علي فكتبتها بخطي وعلمني تأويلها وتفسيرها وناسخها ومنسوخها ، ومحكمها ومتشابهها ، وخاصها وعامها ، ودعا الله أن يعطيني فهمها ، وحفظها ، فما نسيت آية من كتاب الله ولا علما أملاه علي وكتبته ، منذ دعا الله لي بما دعا ، وما ترك شيئا علمه الله من حلال ولا حرام ، ولا أمر ولا نهي كان أو يكون ولا كتاب منزل على أحد قبله من طاعة أو معصية إلا علمنيه وحفظته ، فلم أنس حرفا واحدا

No verse of the Quran was sent down to the Messenger of God except that he had me recite it and dictated it to me, and I wrote it in my own hand. He taught me its interpretation (ta'wil) and its explanation (tafsir), its abrogating and abrogated verses, its decisive and ambiguous verses, and its particular and general verses.

He prayed to God to give me understanding of it and memory of it. So I have not forgotten a verse of the Book of God, nor any knowledge that he dictated to me and I wrote down, since he prayed to God for me as he prayed.

He left nothing that God had taught him, whether permitted or forbidden, command or prohibition, what has been or what will be, or any book sent down to anyone before him, whether of obedience or of disobedience, except that he taught it to me and I memorized it. I did not forget a single letter.

paragraphs.text: فلما توفي رسول الله ﵌ اشتغلت بدفنه والفراغ من شأنه ثم آليت يمينا (1) أني لا أرتدي إلا للصلاة حتى أجمع القرآن ففعلت ، ثم أخذته وجئت به فأعرضته عليهم قالوا : لا حاجة لنا به

When the Messenger of God died, I was occupied with burying him and finishing his affairs. Then I swore an oath that I would not put on my cloak except for prayer until I had collected the Quran, and I did so. Then I took it, brought it, and presented it to them.
They said, "We have no need of it."

paragraphs.text: وعَلَيْكُمْ بِكِتَابِ اللَّه - فَإِنَّه الْحَبْلُ الْمَتِينُ والنُّورُ الْمُبِينُ - والشِّفَاءُ النَّافِعُ والرِّيُّ النَّاقِعُ - والْعِصْمَةُ لِلْمُتَمَسِّكِ والنَّجَاةُ لِلْمُتَعَلِّقِ - لَا يَعْوَجُّ فَيُقَامَ ولَا يَزِيغُ فَيُسْتَعْتَبَ - ولَا تُخْلِقُه كَثْرَةُ الرَّدِّ ووُلُوجُ السَّمْعِ - مَنْ قَالَ بِه صَدَقَ ومَنْ عَمِلَ بِه سَبَقَ

Hold fast to the Book of God, for it is the firm rope and the clear light, the beneficial cure and the quenching drink, a protection for whoever holds to it and a rescue for whoever clings to it. It does not bend, so that it would need straightening, and it does not swerve, so that it would need to be turned back. Repeated recitation and constant hearing do not wear it out. Whoever speaks by it speaks truly, and whoever acts by it takes the lead.

paragraphs.text: ويروى عن حفص بن سليمان ، قال : قال لي عاصم : ما كان من القراءة التي قرأت بها على أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي ، فهي التي أقرأتك بها ، وما كان من القراءة التي أقرأت بها أبا بكر بن عياش ، فهي القراءة التي عرضتها على زرّ بن حبيش ، عن ابن مسعود .
It is reported from Hafs ibn Sulayman, who said.

Asim said to me, “Whatever recitation I recited to Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, that is the one I taught you. And whatever recitation I taught Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, that is the recitation I presented to Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ibn Masud.”

paragraphs.text: تعريف بهذا المصحف الشريف كتب هذا المصحف وضبط على ما يوافق رواية حفص بن سليمان بن المغيرة الأسدي الكوفي بقراءة عاصم بن أبي النجود الكوفي التابعي ، عن أبي عبد الرحمن عبد الله بن حبيب السلمي ، عن عثمان بن عفان ، وعلي بن أبي طالب ﵇ ، وزيد بن ثابت ، وأبي بن كعب ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه (وآله) وسلم .

Introduction to this noble Quran codex. This codex was written and vocalized in agreement with the transmission of Hafs ibn Sulayman ibn al-Mughira al-Asadi al-Kufi, from the recitation of Asim ibn Abi al-Najud al-Kufi, a Follower, from Abu Abd al-Rahman Abd Allah ibn Habib al-Sulami, from Uthman ibn Affan, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Zayd ibn Thabit and Ubayy ibn Kab, from the Prophet.

paragraphs.text: قرأ حمزة والكسائي " فارقوا دينهم " وهي قراءة علي بن أبي طالب : أي تركوا دينهم وخرجوا عنه . وقرأ الباقون فرقوا بالتشديد إلا النخعي فإنه قرأ بالتخفيف .

paragraphs.text: أقول : روى البخاري والترمذي في صحيحيهما وذكره في جامع الأصول في حرف التاء في باب ترتيب القرآن وتأليفه وجمعه ، عن زيد بن ثابت قال : أرسل إلى أبو بكر بعد مقتل أهل اليمامة فإذا عمر جالس عنده ، فقال أبو بكر : إن عمر جاءني فقال : إن القتل قد استحر يوم اليمامة بقراء القرآن ، وإني أخشى أن يستحر القتل بالقراء في كل المواطن ، فيذهب من القرآن كثير وإني أرى أن تذهب بجمع القرآن ، قال : قلت لعمر : وكيف أفعل شيئا لم يفعله رسول الله ﵌ فقال عمر : هو والله خير ، فلم يزل يراجعني في ذلك حتى شرح الله صدري للذي شرح له صدر عمر ، ورأيت في ذلك الذي رأي عمر ، قال زيد : فقال لي أبو بكر : إنك رجل شاب عاقل ، لا نتهمك ، قد كنت تكتب الوحي لرسول الله ﵌ فتتبع القرآن فأجمعه ، قال زيد : فوالله لو كلفني نقل جبل من الجبال ، ما كان أثقل على مما أمرني به من جمع القرآن . قال : قلت : كيف تفعلان شيئا لم يفعله رسول الله ؟ فقال أبو بكر : هو والله خير ، قال : فلم يزل أبو بكر يراجعني - وفي رواية أخرى فلم يزل عمر يراجعني - حتى شرح الله صدري للذي شرح له صدر أبي بكر قال : فتتبعت القرآن : أجمعه من الرقاع والعسب واللخاف وصدور الرجال حتى وجدت آخر سورة التوبة مع خزيمة أو أبي خزيمة الأنصاري لم أجدها مع أحد غيره " لقد جائكم رسول من أنفسكم عزيز عليه " خاتمة براءة . قال : فكانت الصحف عند أبي بكر حتى توفاه الله ثم عند عمر حتى توفاه الله ، ثم حفصة بنت عمر ، قال بعض الرواة : فيه اللخاف يعني الخزف ، قال في جامع الأصول : أخرجه البخاري والترمذي .

I say that al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi reported in their two Sahih collections, and it is also mentioned in Jami al-Usul under the letter ta, in the chapter on the arrangement, composition and collection of the Quran, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said

Abu Bakr sent for me after the killing of the people of Yamama, and Umar was sitting with him. Abu Bakr said, "Umar came to me and said, 'Killing has become fierce on the day of Yamama among the reciters of the Quran, and I fear that killing will become fierce among the reciters in every place, so that much of the Quran goes. I think you should go about the collection of the Quran.' I said to Umar, 'How can I do something the Messenger of God did not do?' Umar said, 'By God, it is good.' He kept going back to me about it until God opened my chest to what he had opened Umar's chest to, and I came to hold on that matter the view that Umar held."

Zayd said, "Abu Bakr then said to me, 'You are a young and intelligent man, and we do not suspect you. You used to write down the revelation for the Messenger of God, so seek out the Quran and collect it.'" Zayd said, "By God, if he had charged me with moving one of the mountains, it would not have been heavier on me than what he commanded me to do in collecting the Quran."

He said, "I said, 'How can you two do something the Messenger of God did not do?' Abu Bakr said, 'By God, it is good.'" He said, "Abu Bakr kept going back to me about it (in another narration, Umar kept going back to me) until God opened my chest to what he had opened Abu Bakr's chest to."

He said, "So I sought out the Quran, collecting it from scraps of parchment, palm stalks, thin stones (lakhaf) and the chests of men, until I found the end of Surat al-Tawba with Khuzayma, or Abu Khuzayma, the Ansari. I did not find it with anyone else, 'A messenger has come to you from among yourselves, it is grievous to him...', the closing verses of Bara'a." He said, "The sheets then remained with Abu Bakr until God took him, then with Umar until God took him, then with Hafsa, the daughter of Umar."
Some of the transmitters said that in this report lakhaf means pottery.
He said in Jami al-Usul that al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi transmitted it.

paragraphs.text: في مسند أحمد بسنده عن ابن عباس أنه قال في حديثه عن الخليفة عثمان أنّه قال : إن رسول اللّه ( ص ) كان مما يأتي عليه الزمان ينزل عليه من السور ذوات العدد ، وكان إذا أنزل عليه الشيء يدعو بعض من يكتب عنده ، يقول : ضعوا هذا في السورة التي يذكر فيها كذا وكذا ، وينزل عليه الآيات فيقول : ضعوا هذه الآيات في السورة التي يذكر فيها كذا وكذا ، وينزل عليه الآية فيقول : ضعوا هذه الآية في السورة التي يذكر فيها كذا وكذا (9) .
In the Musnad of Ahmad, with its chain of transmission, from Ibn Abbas, who said in his report about the caliph Uthman that he said.

“Time would often pass for the Messenger of God while a number of surahs were being revealed to him. Whenever something was revealed to him, he would call one of those who wrote for him and say, ‘Put this in the surah in which such and such is mentioned.’ Verses would be revealed to him and he would say, ‘Put these verses in the surah in which such and such is mentioned.’ A verse would be revealed to him and he would say, ‘Put this verse in the surah in which such and such is mentioned.’”

paragraphs.text: [ 39 ] حدثنا (39) عبد اللّه قال حدثنا سهل بن صالح قال قال حدثنا أبو داود ويعقوب قالا أخبرنا شعبة عن علقمة بن مرثد عن سويد بن غفلة قال قال علي في المصاحف لو لم يصنعه عثمان لصنعته [ قال أبو داود « * » عن رجل عن سويد ] .

[39] Abd Allah narrated to us, he said, Sahl ibn Salih narrated to us, he said, he said, Abu Dawud and Yaqub narrated to us, both said, Shuba informed us, from Alqama ibn Marthad, from Suwayd ibn Ghafala, who said.
Ali said about the codices, “If Uthman had not done it, I would have done it.”
[Abu Dawud said, from a man, from Suwayd.]

paragraphs.text: اعتقادنا أن القرآن الذي أنزله الله تعالى على نبيه محمد ﵌ هو ما بين الدفتين ، وهو ما في أيدي الناس ، ليس بأكثر من ذلك ، ومبلغ سوره عند الناس مائة وأربع عشرة سورة . وعندنا أن الضحى وألم نشرح سورة واحدة ، ولايلاف وألم تر كيف سورة واحدة (1) . ومن نسب إلينا أنا نقول إنه أكثر من ذلك فهو كاذب .

Our belief is that the Quran which God Almighty sent down to His Prophet Muhammad is what lies between the two covers, and it is what is in people's hands. It is not more than that. The number of its surahs among the people is one hundred and fourteen. We hold that al-Duha and Alam Nashrah are one surah, and that Li-Ilaf and Alam Tara Kayfa are one surah. Whoever attributes to us the claim that it is more than that is a liar.

paragraphs.text: المسألة التاسعة : صيانة القرآن من التحريف ما قولة - أدام الله تعالى حراسته (1) - في القرآن : أهو ما بين الدفتين ، الذي في أيدي الناس ، أم هل ضاع مما أنزل الله تعالى على نبيه منه شئ ، أم لا ؟ وهل هو ما جمعه أمير المؤمنين ﵇ ، أم ما جمعه عثمان بن عفان على ما يذكره المخالفون ؟ الجواب : لا شك (2) أن الذي بين الدفتين من القرآن جميعه (3) كلام الله تعالى وتنزيله ، وليس فيه شئ من كلام البشر ، وهو جمهور المنزل . والباقي مما أنزله (4) الله تعالى (5) عند المستحفظ للشريعة ، المستودع للأحكام ، لم يضع (1) منه شئ (2) . وإن كان الذي جمع ما بين الدفتين الآن لم يجعله في جملة ما جمع لأسباب (3) دعته إلى ذلك ، منها : قصوره عن معرفة بعضه . ومنها : شكه فيه وعدم تيقنه (4) . ومنها : ما تعمد إخراجه منه . وقد جمع أمير المؤمنين ﵇ القرآن المنزل من أوله إلى آخره ، وألفه بحسب ما وجب من تأليفه ، فقدم المكي على المدني ، والمنسوخ على الناسخ ، ووضع كل شئ منه في محله (5) . فلذلك قاد جعفر بن محمد الصادق ﵉ : " أما والله لو قرئ القرآن كما أنزل لألفيتمونا فيه مسمين كما سمي من كان قبلنا " (6) .

Ninth question, the protection of the Quran from alteration. What is the opinion of the shaykh, may God Almighty prolong his guardianship, about the Quran? Is it what lies between the two covers, which is in people's hands, or has some of what God Almighty sent down to His Prophet been lost, or not? And is it what the Commander of the Faithful collected, or what Uthman ibn Affan collected, as the opponents say?

The answer is that there is no doubt that what lies between the two covers, all of it, is the speech of God Almighty and His revelation, and that nothing in it is the speech of human beings. It is the majority of what was revealed. The rest of what God Almighty revealed is with the one entrusted to preserve the law and to whom the rulings are committed, and none of it has been lost. This is so even though the one who collected what lies between the two covers did not include it all in what he collected, for reasons that led him to that. Among them were his limited knowledge of some of it, his doubt about some of it and his lack of certainty about it, and his deliberate exclusion of some of it.

The Commander of the Faithful collected the revealed Quran from its beginning to its end and arranged it as its arrangement required. He placed the Meccan before the Medinan and the abrogated before the abrogating, and put everything in its proper place. For that reason Jafar ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq said, “By God, if the Quran were recited as it was revealed, you would find us named in it, just as those before us were named.”

paragraphs.text: غير أن الخبر قد صح عن أئمتنا ﵈ أنهم أمروا بقراءة ما بين الدفتين ، وأن لا (1) يتعداه إلا زيادة فيه ولا نقصان منه حتى يقوم القائم ﵇ فيقرأ للناس (2) القرآن على ما أنزله الله تعالى وجمعه أمير المؤمنين ﵇ (3) .

However, the report has been established as sound from our Imams that they commanded the recitation of what lies between the two covers, and that one should not go beyond it, whether by adding to it or by subtracting from it, until the Riser rises and recites to the people the Quran as God Almighty revealed it and as the Commander of the Faithful collected it.

paragraphs.text: وأما النقصان فإن العقول لا تحيله ولا تمنع من وقوعه ، وقد امتحنت مقالة من ادعاه ، وكلمت عليه المعتزلة وغيرهم طويلا فلم اظفر منهم بحجة اعتمدها في فساده . وقد قال جماعة من أهل الإمامة إنه لم ينقص من كلمة ولا من آية ولا من سورة ولكن حذف ما كان مثبتا في مصحف أمير المؤمنين ( ع ) من تأويله وتفسير معانيه على حقيقة تنزيله وذلك كان ثابتا منزلا وإن لم يكن من جملة كلام الله تعالى الذي هو القرآن المعجز ، وقد يسمى تأويل القرآن قرآنا قال الله تعالى : ( ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه وقل رب زدني علما ) فسمى تأويل القرآن قرآنا ، وهذا ما ليس فيه بين أهل التفسير اختلاف . وعندي أن هذا القول أشبه من مقال من ادعى نقصان كلم من نفس القرآن على الحقيقة دون التأويل ، وإليه أميل والله أسأل توفيقه للصواب . وأما الزيادة فيه فمقطوع على فسادها من وجه ويجوز صحتها من وجه ، فالوجه الذي أقطع على فساده أن يمكن لأحد من الخلق زيادة مقدار سورة فيه على حد يلتبس به عند أحد من الفصحاء ، وأما الوجه المجوز فهو أن يزاد فيه الكلمة والكلمتان والحرف والحرفان وما أشبه ذلك مما لا يبلغ حد الاعجاز ، ويكون ملتبسا عند أكثر الفصحاء بكلم القرآن ، غير أنه لا بد متى وقع ذلك من أن يدل الله عليه ، ويوضح لعباده عن الحق فيه ، ولست أقطع على كون ذلك بل أميل إلى عدمه وسلامة القرآن عنه ، ومعي بذلك حديث عن الصادق جعفر بن محمد (ع) ، وهذا المذهب بخلاف ما سمعناه عن بني نوبخت - ﵏ - من الزيادة في القرآن والنقصان فيه ، وقد ذهب إليه جماعة من متكلمي الإمامية وأهل الفقه منهم والاعتبار .

As for omission, reason does not rule it out or prevent it from happening. I have examined the claim of those who asserted it, and I have spoken at length about it with the Mu'tazila and others, but I found in them no argument that I could rely on to show it false. A group of the Imamis have said that no word, verse or chapter was left out. What was removed, they say, is what had been written in the codex of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, namely its interpretation and the explanation of its meanings according to the truth of its revelation. That material was established and sent down, even though it was not part of the speech of God Most High that is the inimitable Quran.

The interpretation of the Quran can also be called Quran. God Most High said, "Do not hasten with the Quran before its revelation is completed to you, and say, 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge.'" So He called the interpretation of the Quran "Quran," and the scholars of exegesis do not disagree about this. In my view this position is closer to the truth than the statement of those who claimed that actual words were lost from the Quran itself, rather than from its interpretation. I incline toward it, and I ask God for success in reaching what is correct.

As for addition to the Quran, one kind is certainly false and another kind is possible. The kind I am certain is false is that any human being could add the length of a chapter to it in such a way that it would be confused with the Quran in the judgment of any eloquent speaker. The kind that is possible is that a word or two words, or a letter or two letters, or something similar that does not reach the level of inimitability, was added to it and was mistaken for Quranic words by most eloquent speakers. Even so, if that had happened, God would necessarily have pointed it out and made the truth about it clear to His servants. I am not certain that it happened. I incline instead toward its not having happened and toward the Quran being free of it, and I have a report from al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, that supports this.

This position differs from what we heard from the Banu Nawbakht, may God have mercy on them, about addition to the Quran and omission from it. A group of Imami theologians, including their jurists and scholars of reflection, have held to it.

paragraphs.text: فان قيل : كيف يكون أحد الامرين كالآخر والامامية تدّعي تغييرا في القرآن ونقصانا ، وكذلك حشوية أصحاب الحديث ؟ قلنا : قد بيّنا صحة نقل القرآن في المسائل الطرابلسيات (3) ، وأنه غير منقوص ولا مبدّل ولا مغيّر ، وأن العلم بأن هذا القرآن الذي في أيدينا هو الذي ظهر على يد رسول اللّه « ص » كالعلم بالبلدان والحوادث الكبار والوقائع العظام ، والكتب المصنفة المشهورة ، والاشعار المدونة . وذكرنا أن العناية اشتدت بالقرآن والدواعي توفرت على نقله وحراسته وبلغت إلى حدّ لم يبلغه في نقل الحوادث والوقائع والكتب المصنفة ، لأن القرآن معجز النبوة ، وأصل العلم بالشريعة والاحكام الدينية . وكل شيء دعا إلى نقل جميع ما تقدم حاصل فيه ، ويستبدّ بدواع إلى النقل ليست في الحوادث وما أشبهها ، وأن علماء المتكلمين بلغوا في ضبطه وحمايته ، وان عرفوا كل شيء اختلف (1) فيه من اعرابه والقراءات المختلفة في حروفه حتى فرّقوا بين ما روي وعرف ، وبين ما لم يذكر ولم يسطر . فكيف يجوز أن يكون مغيّرا أو منقوصا مع هذه العناية الصادقة والضبط الشديد ؟

If it is asked how one of the two matters can be like the other, when the Imamis claim alteration and diminution in the Quran, and so do the Hashwiyya among the hadith folk, we say that we have already explained the soundness of the transmission of the Quran in al-Masa'il al-Tarabulusiyyat. We showed that it is not diminished, replaced, or altered. We also showed that knowledge that this Quran in our hands is what appeared at the hands of the Messenger of God is like knowledge of countries, great events, major incidents, famous compiled books, and recorded poems.

We mentioned also that care for the Quran was intense, and that the motives to transmit and guard it were abundant, to a degree not reached in the transmission of events, incidents, and compiled books. The reason is that the Quran is the miracle that proves prophethood and the foundation of knowledge of the Law and of religious rulings. Everything that prompted the transmission of all those earlier things is present in it, and it alone has motives for transmission that events and the like do not have. The scholars among the theologians went so far in preserving and protecting it that they even knew everything disputed in it, such as its grammatical inflection and the different readings of its letters, until they distinguished between what was narrated and known and what was not mentioned or written down. So how can it be altered or diminished, given this genuine care and strict preservation?

paragraphs.text: ومن ذلك : الكلام في زيادة القرآن ونقصانه فإنه لا يليق بالتفسير . فأما الزيادة فيه : فمجمع على بطلانه . وأما النقصان منه : فقد روى جماعة من أصحابنا ، وقوم من حشوية العامة ، أن في القرآن تغييرا أو نقصانا ، والصحيح من مذهب أصحابنا خلافه

Of this kind is the discussion of increase and decrease in the Quran, which is unsuitable for exegesis. As for increase in it, its invalidity is unanimously agreed. As for decrease from it, a group of our companions and a group of the Hashwiyya of the general body of Muslims (al-'amma) have narrated that the Quran contains alteration or diminution. The sound position of our companions is the opposite.

paragraphs.text: ومما ذكرناه : قد تبين للقارئ أن حديث تحريف القرآن حديث خرافة وخيال ، لا يقول به إلا من ضعف عقله ، أو من لم يتأمل في أطرافه حق التأمل ، أو من ألجأه إليه يجب القول به . والحب يعمي ويصم ، وأما العاقل المنصف المتدبر فلا يشك في بطلانه وخرافته .

From what we have mentioned, it has become clear to the reader that the talk of the Qur'an's alteration is a superstitious tale and a fantasy. No one holds it except one whose reason is weak, or one who has not reflected on its aspects with the reflection they deserve, or one whom love of holding the view drives to it. Love blinds and deafens. But the sensible, fair-minded person who reflects has no doubt that it is false and a superstitious tale.

paragraphs.text: أمّا الأولى : فلمنع وقوع التحريف فيه جدّاً ، كما هو مذهب المحقّقين من علماء العامّة والخاصّة ، والمعتبرين من الفريقين ، وإن شئت شطراً من الكلام في هذا المقام فارجع إلى مقدّمة تفسير آلاء الرحمن للعلّامة البلاغي المعاصر ﵋ (2) . وأزيدك توضيحاً : أنّه لو كان الأمر كما توهّم صاحب «فصل الخطاب» الذي كان كتبه لا يفيد علماً ولا عملًا ، وإنّما هو إيراد روايات أعرض عنها الأصحاب ، واختلاط ضعاف بين الروايات بعد تنزيهها عنها أولو الألباب من قدماء أصحابنا كالمحمّدين الثلاثة المتقدّمين ﵏ . هذا حال كتب روايته غالباً ك «المستدرك» ، ولا تسأل عن سائر كتبه المشحونة بالقصص والحكايات الغريبة التي غالبها بالهزل أشبه منه بالجدّ ، وهو ﵀ شخص صالح متتبّع ، إلّاأنّ اشتياقه لجمع الضعاف والغرائب والعجائب وما لا يقبلها العقل السليم والرأي المستقيم ، أكثر من الكلام النافع ، والعجب من معاصريه من أهل اليقظة ! كيف ذهلوا وغفلوا حتّى وقع ما وقع ممّا بكت عليه السماوات ، وكادت تتدكدك على الأرض ؟ ! وبالجملة : لو كان الأمر كما ذكره هذا وأشباهه ، من كون الكتاب الإلهي مشحوناً بذكر أهل البيت وفضلهم ، وذكر أمير المؤمنين وإثبات وصايته وإمامته ، فلِمَ لم يحتجّ بواحد من تلك الآيات النازلة والبراهين القاطعة من الكتاب الإلهي أميرُالمؤمنين ، وفاطمة ، والحسن ، والحسين ﵈ وسلمان ، وأبوذرّ ، ومقداد ، وعمّار ، وسائر الأصحاب الذين لا يزالون يحتجّون على خلافته ﵇ (1) ؟ ! ولمَ تشبّث ﵇ بالأحاديث النبوية (2) ، والقرآن بين أظهرهم ؟ !

As for the first, it is because the occurrence of distortion in it is utterly ruled out, as is the position of the verifying scholars among the general body of Muslims (al-'amma) and the particular group, and of the reliable authorities of both camps. If you want a portion of the discussion on this point, turn to the introduction of the Quran commentary Ala al-Rahman by the great contemporary scholar al-Balaghi. I add a further clarification for you. If the matter were as the author of Fasl al-Khitab imagined, whose books give neither knowledge nor practical benefit, and are only a presentation of reports that the associates turned away from, and a mixing of weak reports among the reports, after people of understanding among our early scholars, such as the three earlier Muhammads, had cleared them of these weak ones.

This is the condition of his books of narration for the most part, such as al-Mustadrak. Do not ask about the rest of his books, which are crammed with strange stories and tales, most of which resemble jest more than earnest. He was a righteous and diligent researcher, except that his eagerness to gather weak, strange and wondrous reports, which sound reason and upright judgment do not accept, was greater than his eagerness for useful discourse. It is astonishing that his contemporaries among the people of alertness were so stunned and heedless that what happened did happen, the thing over which the heavens wept and almost crumbled onto the earth!

In short, if the matter were as he and his like have stated, that the divine Book is crammed with mention of the Ahl al-Bayt and their merit, and with mention of the Commander of the Faithful and proof of his designation as successor and his imamate, then why did none of those revealed verses and decisive proofs from the divine Book get cited as argument by the Commander of the Faithful, Fatima, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, or by Salman, Abu Dharr, al-Miqdad, Ammar, and the rest of the Companions who kept arguing for his caliphate? And why did he hold fast to the prophetic traditions while the Quran was in their midst?

paragraphs.text: 489 . السؤال : لقد قرأت كثيرا في ما ينشر على الانترنت عن موضوع تحريف القرآن ، حيث ينسبونه إلى الشيعة ويستدلون بأدلة من المذهب الشيعي ، فلا أعلم مدى صحة هذه الأقاويل ؟ الجواب : دعوى باطلة أجيب عليها من قبل علماء الشيعة مرات عديدة وهم يكررون القول الباطل وعقيدتنا أن القرآن المنزل من الله تعالى على النبي الأكرم - ﵌ - هو نفس القرآن الموجود لدى المسلمين حاليا من دون زيادة ولا نقيصة .

489. Question. I have read a great deal of what is published on the internet about the subject of the distortion of the Qur'an. They attribute it to the Shia and cite evidence from the Shia school, and I do not know how valid these claims are.

Answer. It is a false claim. Shia scholars have answered it many times, yet they keep repeating the false statement. Our belief is that the Qur'an sent down by God Almighty upon the Noble Prophet is the very Qur'an that Muslims have today, without addition or deficiency.

paragraphs.text: أقول : المستفاد من مجمع هذه الأخبار وغيرها من الروايات من طريق أهل البيت (عيهم السلام) إن القرآن الذي بين أظهرنا ليس بتمامه كما انزل على محمد (﵌) منه ما هو خلاف ما أنزل الله ومنه ما هو مغير ومحرف وإنه قد حذف عنه أشياء كثيرة منها اسم علي (﵇) في كثير من المواضع ومنها غير ذلك وأنه ليس أيضا على الترتيب المرضي عند الله وعند رسوله (﵌) .

I say. What is gathered from the whole of these reports and from other narrations by way of the Ahl al-Bayt is that the Qur'an among us is not complete as it was sent down to Muhammad. Part of it is contrary to what God sent down, and part of it is altered and distorted. Many things have been removed from it, among them the name of Ali in many places, and other things besides. It is also not in the order that is pleasing to God and to His Messenger.

paragraphs.text: أقول : ويرد على هذا كله إشكال وهو أنه على هذا التقدير لم يبق لنا اعتماد على شئ من القرآن إذ على هذا يحتمل كل آية منه أن يكون محرفا ومغيرا ويكون على خلاف ما أنزل الله فلم يبق لنا في القرآن حجة أصلا فتنتفي فائدته وفائدة الأمر باتباعه والوصية بالتمسك به إلى غير ذلك ، وأيضا قال الله ﷿ : وإنه لكتاب عزيز لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه . وقال : إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون فكيف يتطرق إليه التحريف والتغيير ، وأيضا قد استفاض عن النبي (﵌) والأئمة (﵈) حديث عرض الخبر المروي على كتاب الله ليعلم صحته بموافقته له وفساده بمخالفته فإذا كان القرآن الذي بأيدينا محرفا فما فائدة العرض مع أن خبر التحريف مخالف لكتاب الله مكذب له فيجب رده والحكم بفساده أو تأويله .

I say that an objection arises against all of this. On this assumption, we are left with nothing in the Quran that we can rely on. For on this view every verse in it could be altered and changed, and could differ from what God sent down. Then nothing in the Quran would remain a proof for us at all, so its benefit would be lost. The benefit of the command to follow it and of the instruction to hold fast to it would be lost too, and so on.

Also, God, mighty and majestic, said, "And it is indeed a mighty Book. Falsehood cannot come at it from before it or from behind it." And He said, "It is We who sent down the Reminder, and it is We who will guard it." So how could alteration or change reach it?

Also, the hadith about presenting a transmitted report to the Book of God is widely reported from the Prophet and the Imams. By it, the soundness of a report is known through its agreement with the Book, and its falseness through its disagreement. If the Quran in our hands were altered, what would be the use of this presentation? Moreover, the report of alteration contradicts the Book of God and denies it. So it must be rejected and judged false, or else interpreted.

paragraphs.text: ولا يبعد أيضا أن يقال إن بعض المحذوفات كان من قبيل التفسير والبيان ولم يكن من أجزاء القرآن فيكون التبديل من حيث المعنى أي حرفوه وغيروه في تفسيره وتأويله أعني حملوه على خلاف ما هو به ، فمعنى قولهم (﵈) كذا نزلت أن المراد به ذلك لا أنها نزلت مع هذه الزيادة في لفظها فحذف منها ذلك اللفظ .

It is also not far-fetched to say that some of the omitted material was explanation and clarification, and was not part of the Quran. In that case the substitution is in the meaning. That is, they altered and changed the Quran in its explanation and interpretation, by which I mean they applied it contrary to what it really means. So the saying of the Imams, "It was revealed thus," means that the intended sense is that one. It does not mean that the verse was revealed with this addition in its wording, and that this wording was then removed from it.

paragraphs.text: أقول : يكفي في وجوده في كل عصر وجوده جميعا كما أنزله الله محفوظا عند أهله ووجود ما احتجنا إليه منه عندنا وإن لم نقدر على الباقي كما أن الإمام (﵇) كذلك فان الثقلين سيان في ذلك .

I say, for its existence in every age it is enough that all of it exists, just as God sent it down, preserved with its people, and that what we need of it is with us, even if we are unable to reach the rest. The Imam is the same in this respect, for the two weighty things are alike in that.
